[p-3]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Banī Isrā'īl (The Children of Israel)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque﴾, etc.

We have already stated in the introduction to this blessed book that among the kinds of clarification (bayan) it contains is that some scholars make a statement about a verse, while there is within the verse an indication (qarinah) that shows the statement is not valid, and we clarify that.

Having understood this, know that this Isra' (night journey) of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in this noble verse was claimed by some scholars to have been of his spirit (rūḥ) alone, not his body, on the basis that it was in a dream and not in wakefulness, since the dreams of the prophets are revelation.

Some of them also claimed that the Isra' was with the body and the Mi'raj (ascension) was with the spirit alone, without the body. But the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that it was with his spirit and body ﷺ, in wakefulness and not in a dream, because He said ﴿His servant﴾, and "servant" refers to the combination of spirit and body. Also, He said "Glory be to Him," and glorification is only uttered at great matters; if it had been a dream it would not have been of great importance to be marvelled at. Supporting this is His saying: ﴿The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾ [al-Najm 53:17], because sight belongs to the instruments of the self (dhāt), not the spirit, and His saying here: ﴿That We might show him of Our signs﴾ [al-Isra' 17:1].

Among the clearest Qur'anic proofs for this is His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾ [al-Isra' 17:60]. It is a vision of the eye in wakefulness, not a vision of sleep, as is authentically reported from Ibn 'Abbas and others.

Also among the clear proofs for this: if it had been a dream vision, it would not have been a trial, nor a cause of the disbelief of Quraysh, because the vision of a dream is not an object of denial, since in a dream one may see what is not real. What God made a trial was what he saw with his own eye of the strange and wondrous things.

The polytheists claimed that whoever claimed to have seen that with his own eyes was certainly a liar, and so it became a trial for them. As for the cursed tree, which is in truth the tree of al-Zaqqum, being a trial for them: when God revealed His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that grows in the root of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat 37:64], they said, "His lie has become evident, for trees do not grow in dry land, so how would it grow in the root of the fire?" as was mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah.

What supports our statement that it was a vision of the eye in wakefulness is His saying here: ﴿That We might show him of Our signs﴾ (etc.) [al-Isra' 17:1], and His saying: ﴿The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾ [al-Najm 53:17-18].

What some scholars claimed, that linguistically the word "ru'ya" (vision) is not applied with this meaning except to a dream vision, is rejected. Rather, the truth is that the word ru'ya is used in the language of the Arabs for seeing with the eye in wakefulness as well. From this is the saying of the shepherd poet, who was a pure Arab:

"He exclaimed at the sight, and his heart was delighted, and he gave good news to a soul that had once been blaming it."

He means the sighting of a hunter with his own eye. Also from this is the saying of Abu al-Tayyib:

"And your sight is sweeter in the eyes than closing them."

This was cited by the author of Lisan al-Arab.

Some scholars claimed that the meaning of "ru'ya" in His saying: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you﴾ [al-Isra' 17:60] is a dream vision, and that it is the one mentioned in His saying: ﴿Certainly did Allah fulfil for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security﴾ [al-Fath 48:27], but the first claim is the correct one.

His mounting the Buraq (a heavenly steed) indicates that the Isra' was with his body, because the spirit does not ride animals, as is well known. In any case, the authentic hadiths have been transmitted continuously (mutawatir) from him: "that he was taken by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, and that he was ascended from the Farthest Mosque until he passed beyond the seven heavens."

The aforementioned hadiths indicate that both the Isra' and the Mi'raj were with his body and spirit, in wakefulness and not in a dream, just as the verses we mentioned also indicate.

Those among the people of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah) who are considered reliable hold this view, and no account is taken of those among the heretics who deny it.

What is established in the two Sahihs through the chain of Sharik from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the aforementioned Isra' occurred in a dream, does not contradict what we have mentioned, which is the position of the people of the Sunnah and the Community and what the texts of the Book and the Sunnah indicate. It is possible that he saw the aforementioned Isra' in sleep, and then that vision came like the break of dawn, so he was taken by night in wakefulness, confirming that dream vision. Just as he saw in sleep that they had entered the Sacred Mosque, and then that vision came like the break of dawn, and they entered the Sacred Mosque in the Umrah of Qada' in the seventh year, in wakefulness and not in a dream, confirming that vision. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Certainly did Allah fulfil for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security﴾ [al-Fath 48:27].

This is supported by the authentic hadith of 'A'ishah: "He never saw a vision except that it came like the break of dawn." Moreover, a group of scholars said that Sharik ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir had poor memorization in that report from Anas, and he added to it, omitted from it, and changed its order. Others among the memorizers related it from Anas correctly, and they did not mention the dream that Sharik mentioned. Look at their narrations with their chains and texts in the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, for he collected the routes of the hadith of the Isra' in a fine and precise manner. Then he, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"The truth is that he, upon him be prayers and peace, was taken by night in wakefulness and not in a dream, from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), riding the Buraq. When he reached the door of the mosque, he tied the animal at the door, entered, and prayed two rak'ahs in its qiblah as the greeting of the mosque. Then the Mi'raj was brought to him, which was like a ladder with rungs, by which one ascends. He ascended in it to the lowest heaven, then to the rest of the seven heavens. Those nearest to God in each heaven welcomed him, and he greeted the prophets who were in the heavens according to their stations and ranks, until he passed by Musa the Interlocutor in the sixth, and Ibrahim the Friend in the seventh, then he went beyond their abodes, upon them both and upon all the prophets, until he reached a level where he heard the scratching of the pens, meaning the pens of divine decree, with what was to occur. He saw the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and there covered it a great splendour from the command of Allah, the Exalted, of golden butterflies and various colours, and the angels surrounded it. There he saw Jibril in his own form, having six hundred wings, and he saw a green silken canopy that had filled the horizon, and he saw the House Frequented (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur), and Ibrahim the Friend, builder of the earthly Ka'bah, leaning his back against it, for it is the heavenly Ka'bah which seventy thousand angels enter every day, worshipping in it, and then they do not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. He saw Paradise and Hellfire. Allah prescribed for him there fifty prayers, then reduced them to five out of His mercy and kindness to His servants.

In this there is attention to the honour and greatness of the prayer. Then he descended to Bayt al-Maqdis, and the prophets descended with him. He led them in prayer there when the prayer time came, and it is possible that it was the Fajr prayer of that day. Some people claim that he led them in prayer in the heavens, but what the reports widely attest is that it was at Bayt al-Maqdis. However, in some of them it is that it was at the first time he entered it, but the apparent meaning is that it was after his return to it, because when he passed by them in their abodes, he began asking Jibril about them one by one, and he was informing him about them, and this is the most fitting. For he was first summoned to the Exalted Presence so that He might prescribe for him and his community what Allah willed.

Then, when he had finished what was intended for him, he gathered with his brothers from among the prophets. Then he manifested his nobility and virtue over them by putting him forward in leading them, and this was at the indication of Jibril, peace be upon him, in that matter. Then he left Bayt al-Maqdis, mounted the Buraq, and returned to Mecca before dawn. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best." End of quote in its wording from the Tafsir of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him.

Al-Qurtubi said in his commentary on this noble verse: "The Isra' is established in all the books of hadith, and it is related from the Companions in every region of the Islamic lands, so it is mutawatir in this respect." He mentioned al-Naqqash as having related it from twenty Companions. Then he began to mention some of its routes in the two Sahihs and others, and the full account of the Isra', which we have omitted because of its fame among the common people and its being widely transmitted in the hadiths.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned at the end of his discussion of this noble verse two benefits. He said in the first of them: "A fine and great benefit. The Hafiz Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani related in the book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, through the route of Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Waqidi: Malik ibn Abi al-Rijal narrated to me, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Dihyah ibn Khalifah to Caesar...'" Then he mentioned his arrival and coming to him. In the context there is a great indication of the abundant intellect of Heraclius. Then he summoned the merchants who were in Syria, and Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb and his companions were brought, and he asked them about those famous questions which al-Bukhari and Muslim related, as will come with its explanation.

Abu Sufyan strove to belittle his affair and to diminish him in Heraclius's eyes. In this context, concerning Abu Sufyan, it is said: "By Allah, what prevented me from saying about him a statement by which I would bring him down in his eyes was only that I disliked to lie in his presence, a lie he would hold against me, and he would not believe me in anything. He said: Until I mentioned his saying on the night he was taken by night. He said: I said: O King, shall I inform you of a report by which you will know that he has lied? He said: And what is it? He said: I said: He claims to us that he went out from our land, the land of the Haram, one night, then came to this mosque of yours, the mosque of Iliya', and returned to us that same night before morning. He said: And the patriarch of Iliya' was at Caesar's head, so the patriarch of Iliya' said: I knew that night."

He said: "Caesar looked at him and said: And what is your knowledge of this? He said: I used not to sleep a night until I had closed the doors of the mosque. When that night came, I closed all the doors except one door, which overpowered me. I sought help against it from my workers and all who were present, but they overpowered us, and we could not move it, as if we were trying to move a mountain. So I called the carpenters and builders, and they looked at it and said: This door has had its lintel and structure fall upon it, and we cannot move it until morning, when we will see where he came from. He said: So I returned and left the two doors open. When morning came, I went out to them, and behold, the hole in the corner of the mosque had been pierced, and in it was a trace of a tethering place for an animal. He said: So I said to my companions: This door was only held shut last night for a prophet, and he prayed in our mosque last night."

End.

Then he said in the other place: "Benefit: The memorizer Abu al-Khattab Umar ibn Dihya (ibn Dihyah) said in his book (al-Tanwir fi Mawlid al-Siraj al-Munir), and he mentioned the hadith of the Isra' (Night Journey) through the route of Anas, and spoke on it, excelling and benefiting. Then he said: The narrations of the hadith of the Isra' have been transmitted with mass transmission (tawatur) from Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Dharr, Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Ibn Abbas, Shaddad ibn Aws, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abd al-Rahman ibn Qurt, Abu Habbah and Abu Layla al-Ansariyyayn, Abd Allah ibn Amr, Jabir, Hudhayfah, Buraydah, Abu Ayyub, Abu Umamah, Samurah ibn Jundub, Abu al-Hamra', Suhayb al-Rumi, Umm Hani', Aisha, and Asma', the two daughters of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them all. Among them are those who related it in full, and among them are those who abridged it as it occurs in the Musnads, even if the narration of some of them is not up to the condition of soundness." So the hadith of the Isra' has been agreed upon by the Muslims, and the zindiqs (heretics) and atheists have turned away from it; "They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it" (al-Saff 61:8). End of quotation from Ibn Kathir in his wording.

We have already mentioned that the best grammatical analysis of "Subhan" [al-Isra' 1] is that it is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), governed by a deleted verb: i.e., "I glorify Allah with glorification (subhanan), i.e., tasbih." Tasbih means distancing from evil. Its meaning in the Sharia is declaring Allah free of whatever does not befit His majesty and perfection, as we have mentioned. Some scholars claimed that the word "Subhan" is a proper noun (alam) for tanzih (declaration of transcendence). On this view, it is a proper noun of genus (alam jins) for the meaning of tanzih, in line with Ibn Malik's statement in al-Khulasah, pointing out that the alam jins may refer to a meaning just as it may refer to an entity: "Like it is Barrah for piety, and Fujjar is a proper noun for the wicked."

And if it is a proper noun, then it is diptote (mamnu' min al-sarf) due to being a proper noun and the addition of the alif and nun. However, what appears to me, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that it is not a proper noun, and that the meaning of "Subhan" is declaring Allah free of whatever does not befit Him. The word "Subhan" is among the words that are obligatorily construed with an idafah (genitive construction), and its occurrence unaccompanied by idafah is rare, as in the saying of al-A'sha:
"When his boasting came to me, I said: Glory be to the Alqamah the boaster" (subhana min Alqamata al-fakhir).

Among the evidences that it is not a proper noun is its obligatory idafah, whereas proper nouns are rarely made into idafah. I have heard "Subhan" used unaccompanied by idafah, both indefinite with tanwin and definite. An example of it with tanwin is the saying: "Subhanahu, then subhanan, we seek refuge in Him, and before us the Judi and the rocks glorified (Him)." An example of it in the definite is the rajaz verse: "Glory be to You, O Allah, O Possessor of glory (subhanaka Allahumma dha al-subhan)."

The expression "servant" (abd) in this great station clearly indicates that the station of servanthood is the noblest, greatest and most exalted of the attributes of created beings. For had there been an attribute greater than it, He would have used it in this great station, in which the servant traversed the seven heavens and saw of the greatest signs of his Lord. A poet said about a created beloved, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude:
"O people, my heart is with Zahra', whom the hearer and the beholder recognize.
Do not call me except by 'Abdiha (her servant), for it is the noblest of my names."

The scholars differed regarding the rhetorical reason for which "layla" (a night) was indefinitely expressed in this noble verse.

Al-Zamakhshari said in [al-Kashshaf]: By his saying "laylan" [al-Isra' 1] in indefinite form he intended to minimize the duration of the Isra', and that he was taken by night during part of the night from Makkah to al-Sham, a journey of forty nights. This is because indefiniteness here indicates the meaning of partiality, and this is confirmed by the reading of Abd Allah and Hudhayfah: "min al-layl," i.e., part of the night, like His saying: "And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a supererogatory act" [al-Isra' 79], meaning by standing (in prayer) during part of the night. Some scholars objected to this.

Some have mentioned that the indefiniteness in His saying "laylan" is for glorification, i.e., a night of what greatness, in which the lover drew near to the beloved; and other things have been said. We have already mentioned that asra and sara are two dialects, like saqa and asqa, and the saying of Hassan, may Allah be pleased with him, combined both:
"Greetings to al-Nadirah, the lady of the curtain; she traveled (asrat) to you, and she was not one who travels (tasri)."
Here "tasri" is with the letter ta' vowelled with fatha, and the ba' in both dialects is for transitivity, like the ba' in "Allah took away their light" [al-Baqarah 17]. Examples of this have already been given in Surah Hud.

Note
Scholars differed on whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw his Lord on the night of the Isra' with the eye of his head or not. Ibn Abbas and others said: "He saw Him with the eye of his head." Aisha and others said: "He did not see Him." This is a well-known and established difference among the scholars.

The author of this commentary, may Allah forgive him, says: The verified position indicated by the texts of the Sharia is that he ﷺ did not see Him with the eye of his head. What is reported from some of the Salaf that he saw Him is to be understood as seeing with the heart, as in Sahih Muslim: "He saw Him with his heart twice," not with the eye of the head.

Among the clearest evidences for this is that Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him (and he is the one of truthful speech), asked the Prophet ﷺ about this very question, and he answered him with what implies that he did not see Him. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Waki' related to us, from Zayd ibn Ibrahim, from Qatadah, from Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Dharr who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Did you see your Lord? He said: 'Light, how could I see Him?'"

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, my father related to us. (H) And Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir related to me, Affan ibn Muslim related to us, Hammam related to us, both from Qatadah, from Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq who said: "I said to Abu Dharr: If I had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ I would have asked him. He said: About what would you have asked him? I said: I would have asked him: Did you see your Lord? Abu Dharr said: I did ask, and he said: 'I saw light.'" This is the wording of Muslim.

Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim: As for his saying ﷺ: "Light, how could I see Him," it is with tanwin on "nur," with fatha on the hamzah of "anna" and with shaddah and fatha on the nun, and "arahu" with fatha on the hamzah. All the narrators related it this way in all the originals and narrations. Its meaning: His veil is light, so how could I see Him!

Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Mazari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The pronoun in "arahu" refers to Allah the Exalted, and its meaning is that the light prevented me from seeing Him, just as it is customary for lights to blind the eyes and prevent them from perceiving what the light stands between the seer and him. His saying ﷺ "I saw light" means: I saw only light, and I did not see anything else. He said: It has also been narrated as "nurani" with fatha on the ra', kasrah on the nun and shaddah on the ya'. It is possible that its meaning returns to what we have said, i.e., the Creator of the light which prevents seeing Him, so it would be among the attributes of acts.

Qadi Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This narration has not reached us, and we have not seen it in any of the originals. End of the point of relevance from al-Nawawi's words.

The author of this commentary, may Allah forgive him, says: The verified position beyond doubt is that the meaning of the hadith is what has been mentioned: that no one can see Him because of the strength of the light which is His veil. Among the clearest evidences for this too is the agreed-upon hadith of Abu Musa: "His veil is light, or fire; were He to uncover it, the glories of His face would burn away whatever His sight reaches of His creation." This is the meaning of his saying ﷺ: "Light, how could I see Him?" That is, how could I see Him when His veil is light, whose attribute is that if He uncovered it, it would burn whatever His sight reached of His creation.

We have already mentioned that the verified position regarding seeing Allah the Majestic and Exalted with the eyes is that it is rationally possible in this world and the Hereafter, by the proof of Musa's saying: "My Lord, show me, that I may look at You" [al-A'raf 143], since he does not ignorantly attribute to Allah the Exalted what is impossible for Him. And it is permissible by Sharia and will occur on the Day of Resurrection, but it is prohibited by Sharia in this world, as He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain..." [al-A'raf 143] up to His saying: "He made it crumble to dust" [al-A'raf 143].

Among the clearest evidences in this is the hadith: "Indeed you will not see your Lord until you die," in Sahih Muslim and Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, as previously mentioned.

As for His saying: "Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bows' length or nearer" [al-Najm 8-9], that refers to Jibril according to the verified view, not Allah the Majestic and Exalted.

His saying, the Exalted: "Around which We had blessed" [al-Isra' 1].

The most apparent interpretation of it is that the meaning of "We had blessed around it" [al-Isra' 1] is that We increased around it goodness and blessing through trees, fruits and rivers. Verses have come indicating this, such as His saying: "And We saved him and Lut to the land which We had blessed for all peoples" [al-Anbiya' 71], and His saying: "And to Sulayman (We subjected) the wind, blowing strongly, running by his command to the land which We had blessed, and We are Knowing of all things" [al-Anbiya' 81]. The land intended there is al-Sham. And the meaning of His blessing it is that He multiplied in it blessing and goodness through fertility, trees, fruits and water, as the majority of scholars hold.

Some scholars said: the meaning of His blessing it is that He sent prophets from it. And other things have been said. Allah knows best.

His saying, the Exalted: "That We might show him some of Our signs" [al-Isra' 1].

The apparent meaning of what Allah showed him of His signs in this noble verse is that He showed them to him with the sight of the eye. The hamzah of causation enters upon "ra'a" of sight, like your saying: "Did you show Zayd the house of Amr?", i.e., you caused him to see it with his eye. "Min" in the verse is partitive, and the meaning is: "That We might show him of Our signs," i.e., some of Our signs, so that We make him see them with his eye. That is what he ﷺ saw with his eye on the night of the Isra' of the wonders and marvels, as has come explained in many hadiths.

What we have mentioned is supported by His saying, the Exalted, in Surah al-Najm: "The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord" [al-Najm 17-18].

﴿And We gave Musa the Book.﴾

Since Allah, exalted is He, in this noble verse showed the greatness of the status of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), He mentioned the greatness of Musa's status through the mighty Book that He sent down to him, which is the Torah, clarifying that He made it a guidance for the Children of Israel. Allah, exalted is He, repeated this meaning in the Qur'an,

- such as His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book, so be not in doubt about meeting him. And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, and We appointed from among them leaders who guided by Our command when they were patient and they were certain of Our signs.﴾ [As-Sajdah: 23-24],

- and His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book after We had destroyed the earlier generations, as insight for mankind﴾, to the end of the verse [Al-Qasas: 43],

- and His saying: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book, complete upon the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of all things﴾, to the end of the verse [Al-An'am: 154],

- and His saying: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things﴾, to the end of the verse [Al-A'raf: 145],

and other verses besides these.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿That you not take other than Me as a trustee.﴾

Know that the majority of the reciters (qurra') read this letter as ﴿Allā tattakhidhūna﴾ with the taa' (second person address), and on this reading "an" (أنْ) is the explanatory particle (al-mufassirah). Thus, making the Torah a guidance for the Children of Israel is explained by forbidding them from taking a trustee other than Allah, because sincerity in worship in its entirety is the fruit of the Books sent down to the Prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them. On this reading, the "lā" in His saying ﴿allā tattakhidhū﴾ [Al-Isra': 2] is a prohibitive particle.

Abu 'Amr, among the Seven, read it ﴿allā yattakhidhū min dūnī wakīlā﴾ with the yaa' (third person, absent form). On this reading, the verbal noun formed from "anna" and its relative clause is in the genitive, governed by an elided particle of causation. That is, "And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel so that they would not take other than Me as a trustee." This is because taking a trustee to whom affairs are attributed and entrusted, other than Allah, is not part of guidance. Thus the two readings return to one meaning, which is that reliance (tawakkul) is only upon Allah alone and not upon anyone else.

(p-12) He repeated this meaning in many places,

- such as His saying: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but Him, so take Him as a trustee﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9],

- and His saying: ﴿Say: "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied."﴾ [Al-Mulk: 29],

- and His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is Lord of the Throne."﴾ [At-Tawbah: 129],

- and His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him﴾ [At-Talaq: 3],

- and His saying: ﴿Their messengers said to them: "We are only men like you, but Allah bestows favor upon whom He wills of His servants. It is not for us to bring you authority except by permission of Allah, and upon Allah let the believers rely." And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient over what you have harmed us, and upon Allah let those who rely, rely.﴾ [Ibrahim: 11-12],

- and His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾ [Hud: 56],

- and His saying: ﴿And recite to them the news of Nuh, when he said to his people: "O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminder of the signs of Allah has been burdensome to you, then upon Allah I have relied"﴾, to the end of the verse [Yunus: 71],

- and His saying: ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a trustee﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 3],

- and His saying: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾, to the end of the verse [Al-Furqan: 58],

- and His saying: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾, to the end of the verse,

- and His saying: ﴿But it increased them in faith, and they said: "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Trustee."﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 173],

and the verses of this kind are very many.

Al-wakīl (الوكيل) is on the pattern fa'īl from tawakkul (reliance); that is, one upon whom reliance is placed, to whom you entrust your affairs, so that He brings you benefit and averts harm from you.

Az-Zamakhshari said: "wakīlā [Al-Isra': 2]; that is, a lord to whom you entrust your affairs."

Ibn Jarir said: "a guardian for you other than Me."

Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi said: "It is said of the Lord that He is a Wakil because of His sufficiency and His management of the affairs of His servants, not in the sense of the elevation of the status of the one who entrusts and the lowering of the affair of the trustee." End of quote. This was said by Abu Hayyan in al-Bahr.

Al-Qurtubi said: "wakīlā; that is, a partner, according to Mujahid. It was said: a guarantor of their affairs, related by al-Farra'. It was said: a lord upon whom they rely in their affairs, said by al-Kalbi. Al-Farra' said: sufficient." End of quote. The meanings are close, and they return to one thing, which is that the wakīl is the one upon whom reliance is placed, so that affairs are entrusted to him, that he may bring good and repel evil. This is not valid except for Allah alone, exalted is He. For this reason He warned against taking a trustee other than Him, because nothing benefits or harms, and nothing suffices, except Him alone, exalted is He. Upon Him we have relied, and He is our sufficiency and the best Trustee.

(p-١٣)His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The offspring of those whom We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.﴾

In this noble verse, He mentioned those whom He carried with Noah, as a reminder of the blessing by which He saved them from drowning, so that this would stir their offspring to obey Allah. That is, "O offspring of those whom We carried with Noah, whom We saved from drowning, emulate your father and be thankful for Our blessings." He alluded to this meaning in His saying: ﴿Those are the ones on whom Allah bestowed favour from among the prophets, of the offspring of Adam and of those whom We carried with Noah﴾ [Maryam: 58], and so on.

In other places He explained who those were whom He carried with Noah, explained the thing in which He carried them, explained who had descendants and posterity from among them, and who had no descendants or posterity.

He made clear that those whom He carried with Noah were his family and those from his people who believed with him, in His saying: ﴿We said: Load into it two of every pair, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe﴾ [Hud: 40]. He also made clear that those from his people who believed were few, in His saying: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud: 40].

He made clear that among his family, those against whom the word had already gone forth for wretchedness included his wife and his son. About his wife He said: ﴿Allah presents as an example for those who disbelieve the wife of Noah﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10], up to His saying: ﴿And it was said: Enter the Fire with those who enter﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10]. About his son He said: ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned﴾ [Hud: 43], and He also said about him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose deeds are not righteous﴾ [Hud: 46]. His saying ﴿He is not of your family﴾ [Hud: 46] means: he is not among those promised salvation in His saying: ﴿Load into it two of every pair, and your family﴾ [Hud: 40], and similar verses.

He made clear that the thing in which He carried them was the ship, in His saying: ﴿We said: Load into it﴾ [Hud: 40], that is, the ship. His saying: ﴿Load into it two of every pair﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27], that is, enter into it, meaning the ship: ﴿of every pair two, and your family﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27].

He made clear that none of the offspring of those carried with Noah remained except the offspring of Noah, in His saying: ﴿And We made his offspring the remaining ones﴾ [al-Saffat: 77]. Noah used to praise Allah for his food and drink, his clothing, and all his affairs. Therefore Allah named him "a grateful servant."

(p-١٤)The most apparent of the grammatical possibilities (i'rab, grammatical analysis) in His saying ﴿The offspring of those whom We carried﴾ [al-Isra': 3], and the verse, is that it is a vocative (munada) with an elided particle.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾ — the verse — the most apparent of the opinions regarding it is that it means: We informed them and made them know.

Among the meanings of qada' (decree, judgment) is ikhbar (informing) and i'lam (making known). A parallel to this in the Qur'an is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We conveyed to him that matter, that the last remnant of these would be cut off by morning﴾ [al-Hijr: 66]. The apparent reading is that its construction with "ila" (to) is because it is implicitly containing the meaning of revelation (iya'). It was also said that it implicitly contains the meaning of: "We forewarned them and informed them," as Ibn Kathir stated. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 7:

﴿If you do good, you do good for your own selves; and if you do evil, it is for them.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explains that whoever does good, that is, through faith and obedience, is in fact doing good to himself, because the benefit of that belongs to him alone. And whoever does evil, that is, through disbelief and sins, is in fact doing evil to himself, because the harm of that returns to him alone.

This meaning is stated in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self; and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46 and 45 \ 15], and the verse continues,

• His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7-8],

• His saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief; and whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare﴾ [al-Rum: 44], and other verses.

The lam in His saying ﴿and if you do evil, it is for them﴾ [al-Isra': 7] carries the meaning of ʿala ("upon"), i.e., "it is upon them," as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and whoever does evil, it is upon it﴾ [Fussilat: 46, 45 \ 15]. Among the instances of lam being used in the sense of ʿala is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and they fall down upon their faces (lil-adhqan)﴾ [al-Isra': 109], i.e., upon them, and His saying: ﴿So peace be upon you (fa-salamun laka)﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 91].

That is, "peace be upon you," according to what some scholars have said. A parallel to this in Arabic speech is the saying of Jabir al-Taghlibi, or Shurayh al-Absi, or Zuhayr al-Muzani, or others:

*He struck him with the spear, then he bent over him, so he fell prone, for the two hands and for the mouth.*

That is, upon the two hands and upon the mouth. The use of this lam in this verse is for mushakalah (a stylistic correspondence, i.e., matching the phrasing to what precedes it), as we previously mentioned regarding passages such as ﴿and the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40], and ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 194]. (p. 15)

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, to sadden your faces﴾

The verse. The answer to "idha" (when) in this noble verse is omitted, and it is what the lam in His saying ﴿li-yasu'u﴾ [al-Isra': 7] is connected to. Its estimated meaning is: "So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will send them to sadden your faces." This is evidenced by His saying in the first instance: ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours﴾ [al-Isra': 5], and the best of what the Qur'an is interpreted by is the Qur'an itself. Ibn Qutaybah said in Mushkil al-Qur'an: A parallel to this in omitting the governing word is the saying of Humayd ibn Thawr:

*She saw me with her two ropes (of hair), so she turned away out of fear, and in the rope was a terrified-hearted, startled one.*

That is: "She saw me approaching, or approaching (me)."

In this letter there are three canonical readings (qira'at sab'iyyat). Al-Kisa'i recited it as ﴿li-nasu'a wujuhakum﴾ with the nun of majesty and a fatha on the hamzah; that is, "that We may sadden it," by Our empowering them over you, so they kill you and torment you. Ibn ʿAmir, Hamzah, and Shu'bah, from ʿAsim, recited it as ﴿li-yasu'a wujuhakum﴾ with the ya' and a fatha on the hamzah, and the subject is a pronoun referring to Allah; that is, "that He may sadden your faces," by His empowering them over you.

The rest recited it as ﴿li-yasu'u wujuhakum﴾ with the ya' and a damma on the hamzah after it, with the waw of plurality which is the subject of the verb, and it was put in the accusative, so the nun was dropped. The pronoun of the subject, which is the waw, refers to those whom Allah sent against them, "to sadden their faces" with various kinds of torment and killing.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾.

When Exalted and Majestic Allah explained that the Children of Israel were decreed in the Scripture that they would cause corruption on the earth twice, and that when the promise of the first of the two came, He would send against them servants of His possessing great might, who invaded their lands and tormented them; and that when the promise of the last time came, He would send against them a people to disfigure their faces, to enter the masjid (mosque) as they had entered it the first time, and to destroy utterly whatever they had conquered (see Qur'an 17:4–7)...

He also explained that if they returned to corruption a third time, then Exalted and Majestic Allah would return to take vengeance upon them by giving their enemies power over them. This is in His saying: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ [al-Isra' 8]. He did not state here whether they returned to corruption a third time or not.

However, He indicated in other verses that they did return to corruption by denying the Messenger ﷺ, concealing his attributes, breaking their covenants, aiding his enemy against him, and other of their ugly deeds. So Exalted and Majestic Allah returned to take vengeance upon them, confirming His saying: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ [al-Isra' 8]. He gave His Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims power over them, so there befell Banu Qurayza, al-Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa' (p-16) and Khaybar what befell them of killing, captivity and expulsion, and the imposition of the jizya (poll tax) upon those of them who remained, and the stamping of humiliation and wretchedness upon them.

Among the verses indicating that they returned to corruption is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them, and before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls, that they disbelieve in what Allah has revealed, out of resentment that Allah would send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants. So they returned with anger upon anger, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Baqara 89–90]; and His saying: ﴿Is it not that every time they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside?﴾ the verse [al-Baqara 100]; and His saying: ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾ the verse [al-Ma'ida 13]; and similar verses.

Among the verses indicating that He, exalted is He, returned to take vengeance upon them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but Allah came upon them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts, so they destroyed their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O you with vision﴾ ﴿And had not Allah decreed for them the exile, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾ ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah, indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾ [al-Hashr 2–4, 46]; and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He brought down those among the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts; a party you killed and a party you took captive. And He made you inherit their land, their homes and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden﴾ the verse [al-Ahzab 26–27]; and similar verses.

We have omitted detailing the account of those who were given power over them on the two occasions, because they are Israelite reports, and they are well known in the books of tafsir and history. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have made Hell a prison (ḥaṣīr) for the disbelievers﴾.

In His saying ﴿ḥaṣīr﴾ [al-Isra' 8] in this noble verse there are two well-known interpretations among the scholars, each of which is supported in its meaning by the Qur'an. We have previously mentioned in the translation of this blessed book that a verse may contain two or more interpretations, all of them sound and supported by the Qur'an; so we set out all of them, since all of it is truth:

The first: that ḥaṣīr means a place of confinement and a prison, from ḥaṣr, which is confinement. Al-Jawhari said: it is said "ḥaṣarahu yaḥṣuruhu ḥaṣran," meaning he constricted him and surrounded him. This interpretation is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will call out there for destruction﴾ [al-Furqan 13], and similar verses.

The second interpretation: that the meaning of ḥaṣīr is bedding and a cushion, from the ḥaṣīr (mat) that is spread out, because the Arabs call a small rug a ḥaṣīr. Al-Tha'labi said: this is a good interpretation. This interpretation is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them are coverings﴾ the verse [al-A'raf 41], and similar verses. And mihad means bedding.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 9 (part 1 of 6):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, mentions that this great Qur'an, which is the greatest of the heavenly scriptures, the most comprehensive of them for all the sciences, and the last of them in covenant with the Lord of the worlds, exalted is He, guides to that which is most upright; that is, the way which is most sound, most just, and most correct. So "allati" (that which) is an adjective (na't) for a omitted noun (mawsuf mahdhuf), in accordance with the saying of Ibn Malik in the Khulasa:

"What is known of the modified and the modifier may be omitted, though with the modifier it is rare."

Al-Zajjaj, al-Kalbi and al-Farra' said: it means "for the state which is the most upright of states," and it is the tawhid of Allah and belief in His messengers.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, has summarized in it all of the guidance in the Qur'an to the best, most just, and most correct paths. If we were to follow its detailed explanation fully, we would go through the entire great Qur'an, because it encompasses all of the guidance in it to the good of both this world and the Hereafter. But we will, God willing, mention many sufficient points, in various and numerous directions, from the guidance of the Qur'an to the path which is most upright, as an explanation of some of what this noble verse indicates, drawing attention through some of it to the whole, concerning the great issues and the issues which the atheists among the disbelievers denied, and through which they cast doubt on the religion of Islam, due to the deficiency of their understanding in grasping its profound wisdom.

Among that is the tawhid of Allah, exalted is He. The Qur'an has guided, in it, to the path which is the most upright and just of paths, and it is His tawhid, exalted is He, in His lordship (rububiyyah), in His worship (ibadah), and in His names and attributes. The inductive survey (istiqra') of the great Qur'an has shown that the tawhid of Allah divides into three categories:

The first: His tawhid in His lordship. This type of tawhid is innate in the natural disposition (fitrah) of rational beings. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ — the verse [az-Zukhruf: 87]. And He said: ﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who controls hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who arranges the affair?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [Yunus: 31]. The denial of Pharaoh of this type of tawhid in his saying: ﴿Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 23] was feigned ignorance from one who knew that he was a created, owned servant; the evidence for this is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿[Moses] said, "You certainly know that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidences"﴾ — the verse [al-Isra': 102], and His saying: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [an-Naml: 14]. This type of tawhid does not benefit except with sincere worship of Allah, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106]. The verses indicating this are very numerous.

The second: His tawhid, exalted is He, in His worship. The governing principle of this type of tawhid is the realization of the meaning of "There is no deity except Allah" (La ilaha illa Allah), which is composed of negation and affirmation. The meaning of its negation is: renouncing all types of objects of worship other than Allah, whatever they may be, in all types of worship, whatever they may be. The meaning of its affirmation is: singling out Allah, exalted is He, alone for all types of worship, with sincerity, in the manner which He prescribed through the tongues of His messengers, upon them be prayers and peace. Most of the verses of the Qur'an are about this type of tawhid, and it is the one over which the battles between the messengers and their peoples took place: ﴿Has he made the gods one God? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!﴾ [Sad: 5].

Among the verses indicating this type of tawhid is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ — the verse [Muhammad: 19]; and His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut"﴾ [an-Nahl: 36]; and His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]; and His saying: ﴿And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint deities other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 45]; and His saying: ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that your God is but one God, so will you submit?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108]. In this noble verse He commanded that he say that what is revealed to him is restricted to this type of tawhid, because the statement "There is no deity except Allah" encompasses everything that came in the books, since it requires obedience to Allah by worshipping Him alone. This includes all beliefs, commands, and prohibitions, and what follows from them of reward and punishment. The verses concerning this type of tawhid are numerous.

The third type: His tawhid, exalted is He, in His names and attributes. This type of tawhid is founded upon two principles:

The first: exalting Allah, exalted is He, above resembling created beings in their attributes, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [ash-Shura: 11].

The second: belief in what Allah has described Himself with, or what His Messenger ﷺ has described Him with, in the manner befitting His perfection and majesty, as He said after His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, along with cutting off hope of comprehending the modality of the attribute. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 110]. We have previously presented this topic in full, clarified with Qur'anic verses, "in Surat al-A'raf".

It is frequent in the great Qur'an to argue against the disbelievers using their acknowledgment of His lordship, exalted is He, as proof for the obligation of tawhid in worship. Therefore, He addresses them regarding the tawhid of lordship with interrogatives of affirmation (istifham al-taqrir). When they acknowledge His lordship, He argues against them with it, that He is the one deserving to be worshipped alone, and He rebukes them, denouncing their associating others with Him, while they acknowledge that He is the Lord alone; for whoever acknowledges that He is the Lord alone is necessarily obliged to acknowledge that He is the one deserving to be worshipped alone.

Among examples of that is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who controls hearing and sight"﴾ [Yunus: 31] up to His saying: ﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 31]. So when they acknowledged His lordship, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [Yunus: 31].

And among them is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?" They will say, "To Allah."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 84, 85]. When they acknowledged it, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿Say, "Will you not then remember?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 85]. Then He said: ﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the great Throne?" ﴾ ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 86-87]. When they acknowledged it, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿Say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 87]. Then He said: ﴿Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things, who protects while none can be protected against Him, if you know?" They will say, "Allah."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88, 89]. When they acknowledged it, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 89].

And among them is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allah."﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 16]. When the acknowledgment was established, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿Say, "Have you then taken from other than Him protectors who possess not for themselves any benefit or harm?"﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 16].

(p-20) And among them is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 87]. When their acknowledgment was established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿How then are they deluded?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 87].

And among them is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 61]. When their acknowledgment was established, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿How then are they deluded?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 61]. And His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who sends down from the sky water and gives life thereby to the earth after its death, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 63]. When their acknowledgment was established, He rebuked them, denouncing their associating others with Him, by His saying: ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah," but most of them do not reason.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 63]. And His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [Luqman: 25]. When their acknowledgment was established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah," but most of them do not know.﴾ [Luqman: 25]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ ﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delightful beauty, which you could not have caused their trees to grow?﴾ [an-Naml: 59-60]. There is no doubt that the answer, for which they have no answer at all other than it, is that He who is capable of creating the heavens and the earth and what is mentioned with them is better than a lifeless object which has no power over anything. When their acknowledgment was necessarily established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Rather, they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him].﴾ [an-Naml: 60]. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or who made the earth a stable place and made within it rivers and made for it firmly set mountains and made between the two seas a barrier?﴾ [an-Naml: 61]. There is no doubt that the answer, for which there is no other answer, is as the one before it. When their acknowledgment was necessarily established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ [an-Naml: 61]. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you successors on the earth?﴾ [an-Naml: 62]. There is no doubt that the answer is as before. When their acknowledgment of that was necessarily established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember.﴾ [an-Naml: 62]. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy?﴾ [an-Naml: 63]. There is no doubt that the answer is as the one before it. When their acknowledgment of that was necessarily established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate.﴾ [an-Naml: 63]. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or who originates creation and then repeats it, and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ [an-Naml: 64]. There is no doubt that the answer is as before. When acknowledgment was necessarily established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Say, "Bring your proof, if you should be truthful."﴾ [an-Naml: 64]. And His saying: ﴿Allah is He who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, then gives you life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?﴾ [ar-Rum: 40]. There is no doubt that the answer for which they have no other answer is: No, meaning: none of our partners is able to do anything of that mentioned creation, provision, causing death, and giving life. When their acknowledgment was necessarily established, He rebuked them, denouncing it, by His saying: ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate.﴾ [ar-Rum: 40].

The verses of this kind are very numerous. For this reason, we have mentioned elsewhere that all questions related to the tawhid of lordship are interrogatives of affirmation, intended so that when they acknowledge, rebuke and denunciation follow that acknowledgment; because the one who affirms lordship necessarily must affirm divinity (uluhiyyah); such as His saying: ﴿Is there doubt about Allah?﴾ [Ibrahim: 10], and His saying: ﴿Say, "Is it other than Allah I should seek as a lord?"﴾ [al-An'am: 164]. And although some scholars claimed that this is an interrogative of denial (istifham inkar), because the inductive survey of the Qur'an shows that the interrogative related to lordship is an interrogative of affirmation and not of denial, since they do not deny lordship, as you have seen from the abundance of verses indicating it.

The discussion of the divisions of tawhid you will find, God willing, in many places in this blessed book, according to the occasions in the verses that we discuss, with other verses.

Among the guidance of the Qur'an to that which is most upright is His making divorce (talaq) in the hand of the man, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ — the verse [at-Talaq: 1], and similar verses; because women are fields and cultivated lands, into which seed is sown as grain is sown in the earth, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 223].

Undoubtedly, the way that is most upright of all ways is this: a farmer cannot be forced to cultivate a field he has no desire to farm, because he sees it as unsuitable for him. The clear, sensory proof for what the Qur'an has brought, that the man is the sower and the woman is the field, is that the instrument of sowing is with the man. If a woman wished to have intercourse with a man who was averse to her and had no desire for her, he would not become aroused, and his member would not rise toward her, so she could do nothing with him. By contrast, he may compel her while she is unwilling, and she conceives and gives birth, as Abu Kabir al-Hudhali said:

*From those whom they conceived while their girdles were knotted, he grew up, not a weakling (muhabbal).*

Nature and creation thus indicate that he is the actor and she is the one acted upon. For this reason, rational people have unanimously agreed that the child is attributed to the man, not to the woman.

Treating woman as equal to man in this respect is obstinacy against what is sensed, as is clear.

* *

From the guidance of the Qur'an toward what is most upright is its permission of polygamy up to four wives, and that if a man fears he will not be just among them, he is obliged to limit himself to one wife, or to what his right hand possesses. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women, two, three, or four; but if you fear you will not be just, then only one, or what your right hands possess.﴾ [An-Nisa: 3]. There is no doubt that the way that is most upright and most just is the permission of plural marriage, for matters that are sensed and known to all rational people.

Among them: a single woman menstruates, falls ill, experiences postpartum bleeding, and other obstacles that prevent her from fulfilling the most essential requirements of marriage. The man, however, is ready to contribute to increasing the nation's population. If he were confined to her during the periods of her excuses, his capacities would be rendered useless without any fault on his part.

Also among them: God has established the custom that men are fewer in number than women across the regions of the world, and more exposed to causes of death than women in all fields of life. If a man were limited to one wife, a large number of women would remain deprived of marriage, and they would be compelled to commit immorality. Abandoning the guidance of the Qur'an in this matter is among the greatest causes of the loss of morals and of descent to the level of beasts in failing to guard chastity, honor, manliness, and virtue. Glory be to the All-Wise, the All-Aware. ﴿A Book whose verses are perfected and then elaborated from One who is All-Wise and All-Aware.﴾

Also among them: all women are ready for marriage, while many men lack the ability to meet the requirements of marriage because of poverty. Thus the men ready for marriage are fewer than the women ready for it, because a woman has no impediment, whereas a man is hindered by poverty and inability to meet the requirements of marriage. If each man were limited to one woman, many women who are ready for marriage would also be lost for lack of husbands. That would cause the loss of virtue, the spread of vice, moral decline, and the loss of human values, as is obvious.

If a man fears he will not be just among them, he is obligated to limit himself to one wife, or to what his right hand possesses, because God says: ﴿Indeed, God commands justice and grace﴾ [An-Nahl: 90]. Inclining with preference in legal rights among them is not permitted, because of His saying: ﴿So do not incline completely [toward one], leaving her as if suspended﴾ [An-Nisa: 129]. As for the natural inclination of loving some more than others, it is not within human ability to prevent, because it is an emotional impression and psychological affection, not an action. This is what is meant by His saying: [p. 23] ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [An-Nisa: 129], as we have explained in other places.

As for what some of the heretics, enemies of the religion of Islam, claim, that plural marriage necessarily brings constant quarrelling and strife leading to a wretched life, because whenever he pleases one of the two co-wives, the other becomes angry, so that he is always between two angers, and that this is not wisdom: this is a worthless statement, whose worthlessness is evident to every rational person. This is because quarrelling and conflict among members of a household are unavoidable. They occur between a man and his mother, between him and his father, between him and his children, and between him and his one wife. It is a common matter with no great significance, and it is negligible compared with the great benefits we mentioned of plural marriage: the protection of women, facilitating marriage for all of them, and increasing the numbers of the nation so that it may stand with its large numbers against the enemies of Islam. The greater benefit takes precedence over averting the lesser harm.

If we assumed that the alleged strife in plural marriage is a harm, or that hurting the heart of the first wife by a co-wife is a harm, those great, preponderant benefits we mentioned would still take precedence over it, as is known in the principles of jurisprudence. In Marāqī al-Saʿūd, [the author] said, joining what has a harm that is outweighed by a preponderant benefit:

*Or if reform is preferred, as with captives who are ransomed with what benefits the Christians.*

*And look at the hanging clusters of grapes, in every east and every west.*

The ransoming of captives is a preponderant benefit, while the ransom's benefit to the enemy is an outweighed harm. So the preponderant benefit takes precedence over it. However, if benefit and harm are equal, or if the harm is greater, as in ransoming captives with weapons by which the enemy can kill as many captives or more of the Muslims, then the benefit is cancelled because it is not preponderant, as the author of Marāqī said:

*Excise the attribute that is joined to a harm that is necessary to the ruling, and which is known not to be outweighed.*

Similarly, grapes are pressed to produce wine, which is the mother of all evils. Yet the benefit of the existence of grapes and raisins and benefiting from them in the regions of the world is a preponderant benefit over the harm of pressing wine from them, so this outweighed harm is set aside for their sake. Likewise, the gathering of men and women in the same town may sometimes cause fornication. But cooperation within society of males and females is a benefit preponderant over that harm. For this reason, no scholar has said that women must be isolated in a separate place away from men, and that a strong fortress must be built around them that cannot be approached, with the keys placed in the hands of a trustworthy person [p. 24] known for piety and religiosity, as is established in the principles.

Thus the Qur'an permitted plural marriage for the benefit of women, so they are not deprived of marriage; for the benefit of the man, so that his capacities are not rendered idle when a woman has an excuse; and for the benefit of the nation, so that its numbers increase and it can resist its enemy, so that the word of God may be supreme. It is a legislation of the All-Wise, the All-Aware. None will criticize it except one whom God has blinded in insight by the darkness of disbelief. Limiting wives to four is a limitation from the All-Wise, the All-Aware. It is a matter of moderation between fewness, which leads to the neglect of some of the man's capacities, and abundance, which is likely to make him unable to meet the requirements of marriage for all of them. And God knows best.

* *

From the guidance of the Qur'an toward what is most upright: its preference of the male over the female in inheritance, as God says: ﴿And if there are siblings, men and women, then the male receives the share of two females. God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, and God is Knowing of all things.﴾ [An-Nisa: 176].

In this noble verse, God has explicitly stated that He makes this clarification for His creation, of which the preference of the male over the female in inheritance is a part, so that they do not go astray. Whoever equates the two in this is certainly astray.

Then He showed that He is most knowing of the wisdoms, the benefits, and of everything in His creation, by His saying: ﴿And God is Knowing of all things﴾ [An-Nisa: 176], and He said: ﴿God instructs you concerning your children: for the male, the equivalent of the share of two females﴾ [An-Nisa: 11].

Undoubtedly, the way that is most upright and most just of ways is the preference of the male over the female in the inheritance that God has mentioned. As God indicated by His saying: ﴿Men are in charge of women by what God has given preference to one over the other﴾ [An-Nisa: 34], that is, men over [p. 25] women, and His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 228]. This is because maleness has natural perfection, natural strength, nobility, and beauty, whereas femaleness is a natural deficiency and natural weakness, as is sensed and observed by all rational people, which only an obstinate person who denies what is sensed would deny.

God, the Exalted, has indicated this by His saying: ﴿Is one raised in ornaments while being in dispute not clear?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 18]. This is because God, in this noble verse, rebuked them for attributing to Him offspring unfitting for Him, while attributing to Him the lowest, most deficient, and weakest of the two kinds of offspring. Therefore she is raised in ornaments, that is, adornment of various kinds of jewelry and clothing, so that she may compensate for her natural deficiency [p. 26] by beautification with jewelry and clothing; she is the female. By contrast, the perfection of the male's maleness, his strength, and his beauty suffice him without jewelry, as the poet said:

*Jewelry is only an adornment for a deficiency, completing beauty when beauty falls short.*

*But when beauty is abundant, like yours, it need not be embellished.*

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Is it for you the male and for Him the female? That would be an unjust division﴾ [An-Najm: 21–22]. This division was unjust, that is, not equitable, because the female is naturally and inherently less than the male. They assigned this deficient share to God, the Exalted, exalted far above that, and assigned the perfect share to themselves, as He said: ﴿And they assign to God what they dislike﴾ [An-Nahl: 62], that is, daughters. He also said: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes darkened and he is filled with suppressed anger... evil is what they judge﴾ [An-Nahl: 58–59]. He said: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of what he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, that is, a female, his face becomes darkened and he is filled with suppressed anger﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 17].

All these Qur'anic verses indicate that the female is deficient by the requirement of creation and nature, and that the male is more excellent and more complete than her: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is wrong with you, how do you judge?﴾ [As-Saffat: 153–154]; ﴿Has your Lord preferred you with sons and taken for Himself females from the angels?﴾ [Al-Isra: 40]. The verses indicating His preference of the male over the female are very numerous.

It is known to the general body of rational people that the female is a possession who must be cared for by someone who looks after her affairs and protects her.

Scholars have differed about enjoying a wife: is it a necessity (qut), or a delight (tafakkuh)? The Malikī scholars applied this disagreement to the ruling of obligating a son to marry his poor father. They said: according to the view that marriage is a necessity, he is obliged to marry him off, because it is part of the necessities owed to him. According to the view that it is a delight, some of them say that it is not obligatory on him. Observe how women are compared to food and fruit among the scholars. The authentic Sunnah has come with the prohibition of killing women and children in jihad, because they are part of the property of the Muslims who take booty, unlike men, who are killed.

Among the evidences for the superiority of the male over the female is that the first woman was created from the first man's rib. Her origin is part of him. Therefore, having learned from these evidences that femaleness is a natural deficiency and natural weakness, know that sound reason, which perceives wisdoms and secrets, dictates that the deficient and weak by nature and disposition must be under the supervision of the one who is complete in creation and strong by nature, [p. 26 continued] so that he may bring to her the benefit she cannot bring for herself and ward off from her the harm she cannot ward off, as God said: ﴿Men are in charge of women by what God has given preference to some of them over others﴾ [An-Nisa: 34].

And when you know this, know that since perfect wisdom requires that the weak and deficient be supported and maintained by the strong and complete, it follows that the man is obligated to spend on his wives and to meet all their needs in life, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And because they spend of their wealth﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:34]. The inheritance property is not something they labored to acquire, nor did they have any causal part in it at all. It is rather a transfer of ownership from God, who conferred it upon them by a compulsory transfer. Therefore the wisdom of the All-Wise, All-Aware requires that the man be given preference over the woman in inheritance, even if they both derive from one cause. This is because the man is always expecting loss, through spending on his wives, giving them dowries, and expending in the calamities of time. The woman is always expecting increase, through the man's giving her the dowry, his maintaining her, and his caring for her affairs. Preferring the one who always expects loss over the one who always expects gain serves to compensate for some of his anticipated loss. Its wisdom is manifest and clear, and none denies it except one whom God has blinded in insight through disbelief and sins. This is why God the Exalted said: ﴿The share of the male is equal to the portion of two females﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:11]. And for the sake of these wisdoms which we have explained, the superiority of the male kind over the female kind in original creation and nature is established. The All-Wise, All-Aware made the man the one responsible for the woman in all her circumstances. He specified him with messengership, prophethood, and caliphate to the exclusion of her, made divorce in his hand to the exclusion of her, made him the guardian (wali) in marriage to the exclusion of her, and made lineage of children attributed to him and not to her. He made his testimony in property matters equal to the testimony of two women, as in His saying: ﴿But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:282]. He made his testimony acceptable in the hudud (fixed penalties) and retaliation (qisas) to the exclusion of hers, and so on, among the sensory, moral, and legal differences between them.

Do you not see that physical weakness and inability to express oneself clearly in dispute is a deficiency in men, although it is counted among the attractions of women that draw hearts to them? Jarir said:

The eyes that have in their glance a languor (hawar),
they have slain us, then they do not revive our slain.

They overcome the possessor of intellect until he has no movement
in him, though they are the weakest of God's creatures in their supports.

And Ibn al-Dumayna said:

By myself and my family, those who, if they are exposed
to some harm, he does not know how to respond.

He does not offer the excuse of the innocent,
and he remains in silence until it is said, "He is doubtful."

The first praised them for the weakness of their frames, and the second for their inability to express themselves in dispute, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And he is in dispute not clear [in expression]﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 43:18]. Because of this difference in perfection and strength between the two kinds, it is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he cursed whoever of them imitates the other. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us, from Qatada, from Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the men who imitate women and the women who imitate men." This is the wording of al-Bukhari in his Sahih. It is known that whoever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) curses is cursed in the Book of Allah, because Allah says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger has given you, take it﴾ [Al-Hashr 59:7], as is established from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), as has been mentioned before.

So let those women know, who try to be like men in all affairs, that they are masculinized women imitating men, and that they are cursed in the Book of Allah upon the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ). Likewise the effeminate men who imitate women: they too are cursed in the Book of Allah upon the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ). Indeed he spoke truly who said of them:

What amazes me is not that women have become masculine,
but that men have become feminine, which is strange.

Know, may Allah grant you and me success in what He loves and is pleased with, that this corrupt, erroneous, and failing notion, opposed to sense, reason, the divine revelation, and the legislation of the Creator and Originator, namely equating the female with the male in all rulings and fields, contains corruption and disruption of the order of human society, which is hidden from no one except one whom Allah has blinded in insight. This is because Allah, majestic and exalted, made the female, with her particular characteristics, suited to kinds of participation in building human society, a suitability that no other can replace for her, such as pregnancy and childbirth, nursing, raising children, serving the home, and caring for its affairs: cooking, kneading, sweeping, and the like. These services which she performs for human society inside her home, in covering, protection, chastity, preservation of honor, virtue, and human values, are not less than the service of the man through earning. Yet those base, ignorant ones among the disbelievers and their followers claimed that the woman has the same rights in service outside her home as the man, although during her pregnancy, nursing, and postpartum period she cannot undertake any work involving hardship, as is observed. When she and her husband go out, all the household services are left wasted: keeping young children, nursing whoever is still in the nursing period, and preparing food and drink for the man when he comes from his work. If they were to hire a person to take her place, that person would be occupied in that house with the same idleness from which the woman fled. The result, then, returns to its starting point: the woman's going out and debasing herself in it means the loss of manliness and religion, because the woman is a possession (mata'), the best possession of this world, and the most exposed of the world's possessions to betrayal.

For the treacherous eye, when it looks at something of her beauty, has already exploited some benefit of that beauty through treachery and deceit. Exposing her to becoming a feast for the treacherous contains what is hidden from no person of even the least intelligence. Likewise, when the body of a treacherous man touches some part of her body, the pleasure of that touch spreads into his blood and flesh by the nature of human instinct, especially if the heart is empty of fear of Allah the Exalted. He then exploits the blessing of that body through betrayal and treachery. Stirring instincts by such looking and touching generally becomes a cause of what is worse than it, as is observed in abundance in lands that have abandoned the teachings of Islam and left off protection, so that their women go out displaying themselves, their bodies bare except what Allah wills. This is because Allah has removed from their men the attribute of manliness and jealousy for their womenfolk. There is no power nor might except with Allah, the Exalted, the Mighty. We seek refuge in Allah from the distortion of conscience and taste, and from every evil, and from the claim of the ignorant and base that the constant going out of women with heads, necks, wrists, forearms, shins, and the like uncovered removes the arousal of men's instincts, because frequent touching removes the sensation. This is a statement of utmost baseness and vileness, because its meaning is satisfaction of desire in what is not permitted, until the need disappears through frequent practice of it. This is as you see. Moreover, constancy does not remove the arousal of instinct by the agreement of the sensible, because a man remains with his wife for many years until she bears their children, and his touching her and seeing parts of her body continue to stir his instinct, as is observed, which none denies except the obstinate:

You have made them hear, had you called a living one,
but there is no life for one you call.
