The Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Creator of this existence and the Manager of its affairs, who knows its hidden matters and all that was and all that will be, has commanded lowering the gaze from what is not lawful. He the Exalted said: ﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts; that is purer for them. Indeed Allah is Acquainted with what they do﴾. ﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts and not expose their adornment…﴾ [An-Nur 24:30-31].

He forbade the woman to strike her foot so as to make men hear the sound of her anklet, in His saying: ﴿And let them not strike their feet so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known﴾ [An-Nur 24:31]. He forbade them softness of speech, lest those of corrupt desire be drawn to them, as God the Exalted said: ﴿So do not be soft in speech lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech﴾ [Al-Ahzab/As-Sajda 32:33]. The detailed discussion of the question of hijab will come, Allah willing, in (Surat al-Ahzab), as we promised in the introduction to this blessed book.

* *

From the guidance of the Qur'an toward that which is most upright: ownership of slaves, expressed in the Qur'an as "what your right hands possess," in many verses:

• As in His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just, then one, or what your right hands possess﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:3];
• And His saying: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 23:5-6] in "Surat Qad Aflaha al-Mu'minun, wa sa'ala sa'il";
• And His saying: ﴿And the neighbor who is near and the neighbor who is distant and the companion at your side and the traveler and what your right hands possess﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:36];
• And His saying: ﴿And married women, except what your right hands possess, as the decree of Allah upon you﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:24];
• And His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿And those who seek a writing from what your right hands possess﴾ [An-Nur 24:33];
• And His saying: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:52];
• And His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their due compensation, and what your right hand possesses from what Allah has granted you﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:50], and His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿…nor their women, nor what their right hands possess﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:55];
• And His saying: ﴿Or their women, or what their right hands possess﴾ [An-Nur 24:31];
• And His saying: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:25];
• And His saying: ﴿So those who were favored do not give their provision to what their right hands possess﴾ [An-Nahl 16:71];
• And His saying: ﴿Do you have from what your right hands possess any partners?﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:28],

and other verses besides these.

So what is meant by "possession of the right hand" in all these verses and similar ones is ownership of the slave through servitude. Among the verses indicating the ownership of slaves is His saying: ﴿Allah presents an example: a slave owned (mamluk)﴾ [An-Nahl 16:75], and His saying: ﴿And a believing slave is better than a polytheist﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:221], and similar verses.

The cause of ownership through servitude is disbelief and fighting against Allah and His Messenger. When Allah empowers the Muslim fighters who spend their lives, their wealth, and all their strength, and what Allah has given them, so that the word of Allah may be supreme over the disbelievers, He makes them property of the Muslims by captivity, unless the Imam chooses release or ransom, because of the benefit to the Muslims in that.

This ruling is among the most just, clearest, and most manifest of rulings in wisdom. This is because Allah the Exalted created creation so that they would worship Him and affirm His oneness, comply with His commands, and avoid His prohibitions, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want that they feed Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 51:56-57]. And He lavished upon them His blessings, apparent and hidden.

[p-31] Just as He said: ﴿And if you tried to count God's favour, you could never enumerate it. Indeed, man is greatly unjust and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. In the other verse, in Surat al-Nahl: ﴿And if you tried to count God's favour, you could never enumerate it. Indeed, God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 18]. He gave them hearing, sight and hearts so that they would be grateful to Him, as the Exalted said: ﴿God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing, and He gave you hearing, sight and hearts, so that you might give thanks﴾ [al-Nahl: 78]. Yet the disbelievers rebelled against their Lord, transgressed and became arrogant. They declared war on His messengers, so that His word would not be supreme. They used all the faculties with which He had blessed them to fight against Him, to commit what angers Him, and to oppose Him and His allies who uphold His command. This is the greatest crime a human being can conceive of.

So the Wise, Just, Gentle and All-Aware, exalted is He, punished them with a severe punishment proportionate to their crime. He deprived them of the right to dispose of themselves, and lowered them from the rank of humanity to a rank beneath it, like the rank of animals. He permitted their sale and purchase and other financial transactions, although He did not completely strip them of the rights of humanity. He made it obligatory for their owners to be kind and gentle towards them, to feed them from what the owners eat, to clothe them from what the owners wear, and not to burden them with work they cannot bear; and if they do burden them, they must help them. This is well known from the Sunnah transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ), together with the exhortation concerning them in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿Worship God and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, kinsfolk, orphans…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and those whom your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nisa: 36], as has preceded.

The Lawgiver (al-Shari') was exceedingly eager for freedom and for releasing people from slavery. So he multiplied the causes of that, as he made it obligatory in expiations (kaffarat) for accidental killing, zihar and oaths and other things. He made the spreading of manumission (sirayat al-itq) obligatory, commanded contractual manumission (kitaba) in His saying: ﴿So make a contract with them if you know any good in them﴾ [al-Nur: 33], and strongly encouraged emancipation. Suppose—and to God belongs the highest likeness—that one of those governments that deny ownership through slavery and vilify the religion of Islam for it, had a man among its subjects upon whom it had showered blessings and bestowed every kind of kindness, and he plotted against it a fierce revolt (p-32) intended to overthrow its rule, to stop its word from being obeyed, and to prevent it from implementing its laws, which it sees as the means of the society's welfare; then it overpowered him after fierce resistance and killed him in the most terrible way. There is no doubt that such killing strips him of all his dispositions and all his benefits. So it is far more severely depriving of human disposal and benefits than slavery, by many stages. And the disbeliever has spent everything in his power to prevent the establishment of God's system, which He legislated for His creatures to follow, so that through it security and tranquillity, prosperity and justice, and equality in legitimate rights would spread across the earth, and life would be organised in the most perfect, just and exalted manner: ﴿God commands justice, goodness and giving to kinsfolk, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing and oppression. He admonishes you, that you may remember﴾ [al-Nahl: 90]. Therefore God punished him with this punishment by depriving him of his dispositions, and lowering his rank and his crime makes him deserving of this punishment.

If it is said: If the slave is a Muslim, what is the basis of his being owned through slavery, given that the cause of slavery, which is disbelief and fighting God and His messengers, has ceased to exist?

The answer: The well-known principle among scholars and all rational people is that a prior right is not cancelled by a later right, and that precedence in right through being first is evident and clear. When the Muslims took the disbelievers as spoils through captivity, their right of ownership was established by the legislation of the Creator of all, who is the Wise and All-Aware. Once this right became settled and established, and then the slave embraced Islam afterwards, his right to be freed from slavery through Islam is preceded by the right of the warrior whose ownership came before Islam. It is neither just nor fair to cancel a prior right by a right that comes after it, as is known to rational people. Yes, it is good and commendable for the owner to free him when he embraces Islam, and the Lawgiver has commanded this and encouraged it, and opened for him many doors, as we have mentioned. So glory be to the Wise, the All-Aware: ﴿The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 115]. His saying "in truth" means in reports, and His saying "and justice" means in rulings. There is no doubt that among that justice is ownership through slavery and other rulings of the Qur'an:

*How many a critic has found fault with a sound statement, while his error lay in a diseased understanding.*

* *

Among the guidance of the Qur'an towards what is most upright is retaliation (qisas). When a person becomes angry and intends to kill another person, then he remembers that if he kills him he will be killed for it, and he fears the consequence and abandons the killing. Thus the one who was to be killed is kept alive, and he too is kept alive, because he did not kill and so was not killed in retaliation. The killing of a killer thus preserves lives that only God knows in number, as we have mentioned. God said: ﴿And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding, that you may be God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqara: 179]. There is no doubt that this is among the most just and upright of ways. For this reason, it is observed throughout the regions of the world, past and present, that killing is rarely committed in the lands that rule by the Book of God, because retaliation deters the crime of murder, as God mentioned in the verse cited just above. As for what the enemies of Islam claim—that retaliation does not accord with wisdom, because it reduces the number of the society by killing a second person after the first has died, and that he should be punished with something other than killing, by being imprisoned, and in prison he may have children who increase the society—all of this is worthless speech, devoid of wisdom. For imprisonment does not deter people from killing. If the punishment is not a deterrent, then many fools will commit killing, and the loss to the society will multiply through the increase of killing.

* *

Among the guidance of the Qur'an towards what is most upright is the cutting off of the hand of the thief, which is stated in God's saying: ﴿As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, as an exemplary punishment from God. God is Almighty, All-Wise﴾. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Even if Fatima had stolen, I would have cut off her hand."

The majority of scholars hold that the cutting is from the wrist (al-kuʿ), and that it is the right hand. Ibn Mas'ud and his companions used to recite "fa-qtaʿū aymanahumā" (cut off their right hands).

The majority also hold that if he steals a second time, his left foot is cut off; then if he steals again, his left hand; then if he steals again, his right foot; then he is disciplined (yu'azzar). It has also been said that he is to be killed, as came in the hadith: "There is no cutting except for a quarter dinar or its value, or three dirhams," as is well known in the reports.

Our purpose here is not to detail the rulings on theft and the conditions for cutting, such as the minimum value (nisab) and removal from a secured place (hirz). Rather, our aim is to show that cutting off the thief's hand is among the guidance of the Qur'an towards what is most upright. That is because this hand, which is corrupt and treacherous, was created by God so that it would seize and earn in everything that pleases Him by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and by taking part in building human society. Instead, it stretched its treacherous fingers to the property of others to take it without right, and it used the power of seizing that was placed in it for betrayal and deceit and for taking people's wealth in this ugly way. It is a filthy, foul hand, striving to disrupt the order of society, since there is no order for it without wealth. So its Creator punished it with cutting and removal, like a diseased limb which drags disease to the rest of the body, which is removed entirely to preserve the body and cleanse it from sickness. For this reason, cutting off the hand purifies the thief from the stain of the sin of committing the disobedience of theft, along with a deterrent effect by the cutting from theft. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: "Chapter: The prescribed punishments are an expiation." Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, "from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit (may God be pleased with him), who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a gathering, and he said: 'Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery,' and he recited this whole verse: 'Whoever among you fulfils it, his reward is with God; and whoever incurs any of that and is punished for it, that is his expiation; and whoever incurs any of that and God conceals it, then it is up to God: if He wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He punishes him.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari in his Sahih. The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying in this sound hadith, "that is his expiation," is a clear text that the prescribed punishments purify those who commit them from sin.

The correct position on this is what some scholars have verified: the rights of God are purified by carrying out the prescribed punishment, while the right of the created being remains. So committing the crime of theft, for example, is purified by the prescribed punishment, but liability for the property remains, because theft is a cause that necessitates two rulings: cutting and compensation. As the author of Maraqi al-Su'ud said:

*That applies to the many rulings: it is stated generally, like the cutting together with the liability for the value of the stolen amount.*

However, a group of scholars said: there is no liability for compensation together with the cutting, based on the apparent wording of the noble verse, for it specified cutting and did not mention compensation.

A group said: the stolen property must be compensated in all cases, whether it has been consumed or not, whether the thief is poor or wealthy, and if he is poor, it is owed as a debt.

A group said: the stolen item must be returned if it still exists. If it no longer exists, its value must be returned if he is wealthy; if he is poor, nothing is owed of him, and it is not owed as a debt.

The first is the position of Abu Hanifa. The second is the position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. The third is the position of Malik. The cutting of the thief was known in the pre-Islamic period, and Islam confirmed it.

Ibn al-Kalbi composed a chapter on those who were cut off for theft in the pre-Islamic period. He mentioned the story of those who stole the gazelle of the Ka'ba and were cut off in the time of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and he mentioned among those who were cut off for theft 'Awf ibn 'Abd ibn 'Amr ibn Makhzum, Maqis ibn Qays ibn 'Adi ibn Sahm and others, and that 'Awf was the first to be cut for this. End of quotation.

Among the offerings of the Ka'ba was the image of two gazelles of gold, which the Persians had sent as gifts to the sacred House of God, as al-Badawi al-Shinqiti recorded in his versified work 'Amud al-Nasab:

*And among its treasures was a golden gazelle; the Persians sent the two of them to the House of the Arabs.*

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: The thief was cut off in the pre-Islamic period, and the first to rule for his cutting in the pre-Islamic period was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Then God commanded his cutting in Islam. The first thief whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) cut off in Islam, among men, was al-Khiyar ibn 'Adi ibn Nawfal ibn 'Abd Manaf, and among women, Murra bint Sufyan ibn 'Abd al-Asad of the Banu Makhzum. Abu Bakr cut off the hand of the Yemeni who stole the necklace. 'Umar cut off the hand of Ibn Sumura, brother of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sumura. End of quotation.

The compiler of this work, may God pardon him, says: What al-Qurtubi (may God have mercy on him) mentioned, that the Makhzumite woman whose hand the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off first was Murra bint Sufyan, is contrary to the verified position. The verified position is that she was Fatima bint al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Makhzum. She was the daughter of the brother of Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Asad, the noble companion who had been the husband of Umm Salama before the Prophet (ﷺ). Her father was killed as a disbeliever on the day of Badr, killed by Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (may God be pleased with him). The Prophet's (ﷺ) cutting of her hand took place during the conquest (Fath). As for the theft of Umm 'Amr bint Sufyan ibn 'Abd al-Asad, the cousin of the aforementioned woman, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) cutting of her hand, that was during the Farewell Pilgrimage, more than two years after the first incident.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 17, verse 9 (part 5 of 6)**

If it is said: al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated in their Sahihs, and the authors of the Sunan and others, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "the Prophet ﷺ cut off the hand for a shield (mijann, a large shield) whose value was three dirhams," and in the wording of some of them, "whose value (qimah) was three dirhams." Al-Shaykhan narrated in their Sahihs, and the authors of the Sunan other than Ibn Majah and others, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that "the Prophet ﷺ used to cut off the hand of the thief for a quarter of a dinar or more." Hadiths similar to these are very numerous. Yet it is known from the Shari'ah that the hand carries half the diyah (blood money), and the diyah for gold is a thousand dinars. Thus the diyah of the hand would be five hundred dinars. How then is it taken in exchange for a quarter of a dinar? What is the justice and fairness in that?

The answer: this type of objection belongs to the objections of those who are heretics while professing belief in Allah and His Messenger. It is what al-Ma'arri versified when he said:

> "A hand whose diyah was five hundred gold pieces,
> why was it cut off for a quarter of a dinar?"

The scholars have many answers to this, in verse and in prose. Among them is the statement of al-Qadi 'Abd al-Wahhab, answering him in the same metre and rhyme:

> "The dignity of trustworthiness, its price is high and its price is low:
> the humiliation of betrayal. So understand the wisdom of the Creator."

Some of them said: "When it betrayed, it was humiliated." It is evident that this base, treacherous hand, when it bore the vileness of theft, and the name of theft was applied to it for a trifling thing such as the value of a shield or a citron (utrujjah), it was reasonable and sensible that it be cut off for that small thing in which it bore this great vileness.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: "Then we answered this criticism by saying that the Shari'ah only cut off his hand because he bore baseness and lowliness in stealing that small amount. It is not far-fetched that the Shari'ah should punish him for that baseness with this great punishment." End of quotation.

Look at what the Qur'an calls for of noble characteristics and keeping away from what is unbecoming. The cutting off of the thief's hand for a quarter of a dinar or more shows that the divine legislation lowers the rank of the traitor from five hundred degrees to a quarter of a degree. Behold this great lowering of his rank because of his committing of vices.

Some people have found it problematic that the hand of the thief is cut off specifically for theft and not for the other offences against property, such as usurpation (ghasb), plundering (intihab), and the like.

Al-Mazari and those who followed him said: Allah preserved property by making the cutting off of its thief obligatory. He singled out theft because the other crimes, such as plunder and usurpation, are few in comparison with it, and because it is easy to establish evidence (bayyinah) for other than theft, unlike theft. He made the punishment for it severe so that it would be more effective as a deterrent. And He did not make the diyah for injury to the limb that is cut off equal to the amount for which it is cut off, as a protection of the hand. Then, "when it betrayed, it was humiliated." In this there is an allusion to the doubt attributed to Abu al-'Ala' al-Ma'arri in his saying:

> "A hand whose diyah was five hundred gold pieces,
> why was it cut off for a quarter of a dinar?"

Al-Qadi 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Maliki answered him with his saying:

> "The preservation of the limb: its price is high and its price is low.
> The protection of property: so understand the wisdom of the Creator."

The explanation of this: if the diyah were a quarter of a dinar, injuries to hands would multiply; and if the threshold for amputation were five hundred dinars, injuries to property would multiply. So the wisdom is manifest on both sides, and in this there is preservation from both extremes.

The meaning mentioned above, of the distinction between theft and plunder and the like, was difficult to grasp for some of those who deny analogy (qiyas, reasoning by analogy). He said: "Cutting off the hand for theft and not for usurpation and others is not a meaningful ruling, for usurpation is a greater violation of sanctity than theft. This shows that analogy is not to be considered, for if it is not acted upon in the greater case, it is not acted upon in the equal case."

Its answer: the evidences for acting upon analogy are too well known to be burdened with citing them, and some indication of that will come in the Book of Rulings (Kitab al-Ahkam). End of quotation, via the transmission of Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The distinction between theft and usurpation and the like, which al-Mazari pointed to, is clear: plunder, usurpation and the like are few in comparison with theft. Also, the matter that is evident is usually such that evidence for it is found, unlike theft, for the thief only steals secretly, in such a way that no one notices him, so it is hard to secure justice from him. Therefore the crime was made grave so that it would be more effective as a deterrent. And Allah Ta'ala knows best.

* *

From the guidance of the Qur'an to what is most upright: the stoning of the married adulterer, male or female, and the flogging of the unmarried (bikr) adulterer one hundred lashes, male or female.

As for stoning: it is stated explicitly in a verse whose recitation has been abrogated (naskh al-tilawah) while its rulings remain, and it is His saying, Ta'ala: "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit adultery, stone them definitively as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Mighty and Wise."

We have already mentioned the Qur'an's censure of those who turn away from what is in the Torah concerning the ruling of stoning. The Qur'an, in clear verses such as His saying: ﴿They say: If you are given this, take it﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 41), and His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, being called to the Book of Allah that it may judge between them?﴾ (Al 'Imran: 23), indicates the establishment of the ruling of stoning in the Shari'ah of our Prophet ﷺ, since it censures in our Book those who turn away from it, as has preceded.

What we have mentioned, that the ruling of stoning is established by the Qur'an, does not contradict the saying of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when he stoned a woman on a Friday: "I stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," because the Sunnah is what explained that the ruling of the verse of stoning remains after the abrogation of its recitation.

What confirms this is the saying of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, in his well-known sound hadith: "Among what was revealed to him was the verse of stoning. We recited it, understood it and memorised it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him..." (the hadith).

The heretics say that stoning is a savage killing which does not suit the wisdom of legislation, and it should not be in the systems by which man is governed, due to the shortcomings of their understanding in grasping the profound wisdoms of Allah in His legislation.

The conclusion: stoning is a divine punishment whose meaning is rational, because the adulterer, when he inserts his private part into the private part of a woman in a manner of betrayal and treachery, has committed the basest crime known to humankind: violating honour, defiling sanctities, and striving to destroy the lineages of human society. The woman who submits to him in that is like him. Whoever is like this is impure and filthy, not fit for companionship. So his Creator, the Wise, the All-Aware, punished him with death to repel his evil, which reaches the utmost of baseness and vileness, and the evil of his like from society, and to purify him from the defilement of that filth which he committed. He made his killing the most atrocious killing, because his crime is the most atrocious crime, and the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

The pure Shari'ah has indicated that the insertion of the private part into a private part permitted by the Shari'ah requires ritual washing (ghusl), and prohibits each of the two from entering the mosque until he washes with water. This shows that this act requires purity in principle. And its spiritual purification, if it was unlawful, is the killing of its partner if he is married (muhsan), because if he is stoned, that expiates for him the sin of fornication, but the right of the human being remains upon him, as with the husband if he commits adultery with a married woman, and the right of the guardians to not bring shame upon them, as we have indicated earlier.

The extreme ugliness of fornication is something inherent in human natures. Hind bint 'Utbah, while she was a disbeliever, said: "How ugly that act is when it is lawful! Then how about it when it is unlawful!" Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, made the punishment of the married person by stoning more severe than the punishment of the unmarried by one hundred lashes, because the married person has tasted the sweetness (usaylah) of women, and whoever is like this finds it difficult to be patient without them. So when the motive towards fornication is greater, the deterrent against it is greater, and that is stoning.

As for the flogging of the unmarried adulterer, male or female, one hundred lashes: this is stated explicitly in His saying, Ta'ala: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man: flog each one of them one hundred lashes﴾ (al-Nur: 2), because this punishment deters him and those like him from fornication, and purifies him from the sin of fornication, as has preceded. The detailed explanation of what is obligatory for male and female fornicators, slaves and free persons, will come, if Allah Ta'ala wills, "in Surah al-Nur."

The legislation of the Wise, the All-Aware, the Majestic and Exalted, comprises all wisdoms: repelling corruptions, bringing about benefits, following noble characteristics and good customs. And there is no doubt that among the most upright ways is punishing a heinous crime with a severe punishment, a fitting recompense.

* *

From the guidance of the Qur'an to what is most upright: its guidance that advancement is not incompatible with adherence to the religion. What the enemies of religion have imagined to weak minds among those who claim affiliation with Islam, that advancement is not possible except by stripping oneself of the religion of Islam, is false and has no foundation. The noble Qur'an calls to advancement in all fields that have importance in worldly life or religion, but that advancement is within the bounds of religion and adorned with its noble manners and its heavenly teachings. Allah Ta'ala said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ (al-Anfal: 60). And He said: ﴿And We had given David bounty from Us: O mountains, repeat with him the praises, and the birds; and We made the iron soft for him. That make full coats of mail and measure well the links﴾ (Saba': 10-11), and "Do righteousness."

His saying: ﴿That make full coats of mail and measure well the links﴾ indicates preparation for confronting the enemy. His saying: ﴿and do righteousness﴾ indicates that this preparation for confronting the enemy is within the bounds of the upright religion. David is among the prophets mentioned in Surah al-An'am, in His saying: ﴿And from his descendants, David﴾ (al-An'am: 84). Allah Ta'ala, addressing our Prophet ﷺ after mentioning them, said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ (al-An'am: 90).

It is established in the Sahih of al-Bukhari that Mujahid asked Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "From where did you take the prostration in Surah Sad?" He said: "Do you not recite: ﴿And from his descendants, David﴾ up to His saying ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ (al-An'am: 84-90)? David prostrated for it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated for it."

This shows that we are addressed by what the verse contains of what David was commanded with. So it is incumbent upon us to prepare to confront the enemy while adhering to our religion. Consider His saying, Ta'ala: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾. It is a decisive command to prepare everything within one's capacity of power, even if power reaches whatever level of development it reaches. It is therefore a decisive command to keep pace with development in worldly matters, and not to remain rigid upon former conditions when a new development arises. But all of that is together with adherence to the religion.

And among the clearest proofs for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a party of them stand with you and let them take their arms. Then, when they have prostrated, let them go behind you, and let another party who have not prayed come and pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their arms﴾ [an-Nisa': 102]. The prayer of fear mentioned in this noble verse indicates the obligation to combine fighting the enemy with carrying out what Allah, exalted and majestic, has prescribed in His religion. His command in this verse to establish the prayer at the moment of the clash of armed combat indicates this with the utmost clarity. Allah, exalted is He, has also said: ﴿O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may succeed﴾ [al-Anfal: 45]. His command in this noble verse to remember Allah much at the moment of the clash of battle indicates this too, with clear indication.

The disbelievers deceived weak-minded people into thinking that the relationship between progress and adherence to religion, and between good qualities and noble morals, is a relationship of contradiction (tabayun al-muqabalah), like the contradiction of two opposites such as non-existence and existence, negation and affirmation, or the two contraries (al-diddan) such as blackness and whiteness, motion and rest, or the two correlatives (al-mutadaifan) such as fatherhood and sonship, above and below, or privation and possession (al-adam wal-malakah) such as sight and blindness.

Existence and non-existence cannot be combined in one thing at one time in one respect, and likewise motion and rest, for example, and likewise fatherhood and sonship. Every entity for which fatherhood is established is impossible to be, with respect to the same entity, a son, such that one person would be both a father and a son of one and the same person. This is like the impossibility of combining blackness and whiteness in one simple point, or motion and rest in one body. Likewise, sight and blindness cannot be combined.

So they led them to imagine that progress and adherence to religion are mutually contradictory in the sense of the contradiction of opposites, such that their combination is impossible. As a result of this, they abandoned religion out of desire for progress. They lost this world and the Hereafter; that is the manifest loss.

The truth of the matter is that the relationship between progress and adherence to religion, considered by reason alone and setting aside the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, is only a contradiction of contrariety in the sense of disagreement (tabayun al-mukhalafah). The defining rule for two things in a contradiction of disagreement is that the reality of each of them in itself differs from the reality of the other, yet both can be combined in reason in another entity, such as whiteness and coldness, speaking and sitting, or blackness and sweetness.

The reality of whiteness in itself differs from the reality of coldness, yet whiteness and coldness can be combined in one entity, such as snow. Likewise, speaking and sitting: the reality of speaking differs from the reality of sitting, yet it is possible for one person to be sitting and speaking at the same time. Thus the relationship between adherence to religion and progress, considered by the judgment of reason, is of this kind. Just as a white body may rationally be cold like snow, and a seated person may rationally be speaking, so too the one who adheres to religion may rationally be progressive. There is no obstacle in the judgment of reason to the one who guards the obedience to Allah's commands and avoidance of His prohibitions being engaged in all the progressive fields, as is not hidden, and as history has recorded for the Prophet (ﷺ), his Companions, and those who followed them in excellence.

As for considering the texts of the Book and the Sunnah:
• Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 40], and the rest of the verse.
• And His saying: ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers﴾ [ar-Rum: 47].
• And His saying: ﴿And已 Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be given victory, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious﴾ [as-Saffat: 171–173].
• And His saying: ﴿Allah has decreed, "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21].
• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and the rest of the verse.
• And His saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ [at-Tawbah: 14].
And similar verses, and what carries their meaning of hadiths.

The relationship between adherence to religion and progress is like the relationship between the necessitating (al-mulzum) and its necessary consequence (al-lazim). This is because adherence to religion necessitates progress, in the sense that progress follows from it, as the aforementioned verses explicitly state. It is known that the relationship between the necessitating and its necessary consequence is no more than one of two things: either equality (al-musawah) or absolute specificity (al-khusus al-mutlaq), since the necessitating cannot be more general than its consequence. It may be equal to it or more specific than it, and it goes no further than that. An example of this: the human being, for instance. He necessitates animal-humanity (al-bashariyyah al-hayawaniyyah), in the sense that being human necessarily entails being a human being (bashar) and being an animal (hayawan). One of these two necessary consequences is equal to him in extension, which is "human being" (bashar). The second is more general than him in extension, which is "animal" (hayawan). So the human is more specific than it in absolute specificity, as is well known.

Consider how they led them to imagine that the link between the necessitating and its consequence is like the incompatibility between two contradictories and two contraries. They obeyed them in this out of their naivety, ignorance, and blindness of insight. They did not invent lies against the Islamic religion and attribute to it what is innocent of it except to repel from it weak-minded people who claim affiliation to Islam, so that they could gain control over them. For if they truly knew the religion and followed it, they would have done to them what their predecessors did to their predecessors. The religion is the same religion, and its connection to Allah is the same connection. But most of those who claim to belong to it in most regions of the world have turned away from it and looked upon it with the eye of hatred and contempt. So Allah made them slaves to the wicked disbelievers. If they returned to their religion, their honor and glory would return to them, and they would lead all the people of the earth. This is something beyond doubt: ﴿That, and had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others﴾ [Muhammad: 4].

* *

Among the guidance of the Qur'an to that which is most upright is its explanation that whoever follows a legislation other than the legislation brought by the master of the children of Adam, Muhammad ibn Abdullah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, then following that opposing legislation is manifest disbelief (kufr bawah), which takes one out of the Islamic community. When the disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The sheep dies; who killed it?" He said to them: "Allah killed it." They said to him: "What is slaughtered by their hands is lawful, but what Allah slaughters with His noble hand you call unlawful! So are you then better than Allah?" Allah revealed concerning them His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not eat from that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiance. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. The omission of the fa' from His saying "indeed you are polytheists" indicates an omitted oath, in the manner of His saying in the Khulasah:
"Omit, when a condition and an oath gather, the answer of whichever is placed last; it is then obligatory."
For if the clause were the answer to the condition, it would be joined with fa', in the manner of His saying also in the Khulasah:
"Join with fa' the answer, necessarily, if you make it the condition, since 'in' and others do not take it."
So this is an oath from Allah, exalted and majestic, by which He swears that whoever follows Satan in making lawful what is carrion is a polytheist. This polytheism takes one out of the religion by the consensus of the Muslims. Allah will rebuke its perpetrator on the Day of Resurrection by His saying: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60], because obeying him in his legislation that opposes revelation is worshipping him. Allah said: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols], and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan﴾ [an-Nisa': 117], meaning they worship none but Satan, and that is by their following his legislation. He said: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ [al-An'am: 137], and so He called them "partners" because they obeyed them in disobedience to Allah, exalted is He. He said of His intimate friend (Khalil) [Abraham]: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾ [Maryam: 44], meaning by obeying him in disbelief and sins. When 'Adi ibn Hatim asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 31], he explained to him that its meaning is that they obeyed them in forbidding what Allah had permitted and permitting what He had forbidden. Verses like this are many.

It is strange that someone would judge by other than the legislation of Allah and then claim to be a Muslim, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to refer their disputes to the false deity (taghut), while they have been commanded to reject it? And Satan wants to lead them far astray﴾ [an-Nisa': 60]. He also said: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - it is those who are the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. And He said: ﴿Then is it other than Allah I should seek as judge, while it is He who has sent down to you the Book detailed? And those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be of the doubters﴾ [al-An'am: 114].

[[The author's speech was abridged due to its great length.]]

The words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man has always been hasty.﴾

There are two interpretations (tafsir, meaning explanation of the Qur'an) of this noble verse among the scholars, and one of them is supported by another Qur'anic verse.

The meaning of the verse according to this view is ﴿And man prays for evil﴾ [al-Isra': 11], such as when a person in a moment of irritation over some matter prays against himself or his child for destruction, saying, "O Allah, destroy me," or "destroy my child." He prays for evil in a way that he would not want to be answered. The words ﴿as he prays for good﴾ mean that he prays for evil just as he prays for good. So he says in a moment of irritation, "O Allah, destroy my child," just as he says at other times, "O Allah, grant him well-being," and similar supplications.

If Allah answered his prayer for evil, he would be destroyed. This meaning is supported by the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾ [Yunus: 11]. That is, if He hastened for them the answer with evil just as He hastens for them the answer with good, ﴿their term would have been decreed for them﴾, meaning they would have been destroyed (p-55) and died. So the word "istti'jal" (hastening) here means "ta'jil" (causing to happen quickly).

Included in a person's praying for evil is the statement of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith al-Abdari: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32].

Among those who explained the noble verse in the way we have mentioned are Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah. This is the more correct of the two interpretations because of the evidence of the verse of Yunus.

The second interpretation of the verse is that just as a person prays for good, asking Allah for Paradise and for safety from the Fire and from the punishment of the grave, so too he may pray for evil, asking Allah to make easy for him fornication with his lover, or the killing of a Muslim who is his enemy, and similar things. Of this kind is the statement of Ibn Jami':

*I circle the House among those who circle, and I raise my trailing lower garment,*
*And I prostrate at night until morning, and I recite from the clear, revealed Book.*
*Perhaps the reliever of distress concerning Yusuf will subject to me the lady of the litter.*

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs. Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you might seek bounty from your Lord and that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. And every matter We have detailed with full detail.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He made the night and the day two signs (ayatayn), meaning two indications showing that He is the Lord deserving to be worshipped alone, and that nothing else is to be associated with Him. He, exalted, has repeated this meaning in many places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day﴾ [Fussilat: 37],

• and His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day, and at once they are in darkness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 37],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Allah﴾ [Yunus: 6],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which run in the sea with that which benefits people﴾ - up to His saying - ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164],

• and His saying: ﴿And it is He who gives life and causes death, and His is the alternation of the night and the day. Will you not reason?﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 80],

• and His saying: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day successive for whoever wishes to remember or wishes gratitude﴾ [Al-Furqan: 62],

• and His saying: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving﴾ [Az-Zumar: 5],

• and His saying: ﴿The Cleaver of the daybreak and He who made the night for rest and the sun and the moon for calculation. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96],

• and His saying: ﴿By the sun and its brightness, and by the moon when it follows it, and by the day when it displays it, and by the night when it covers it﴾ - the verse [Ash-Shams: 1-4],

• and His saying: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears﴾ - the verse [Al-Layl: 1, 2],

• and His saying: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾ - the verse [Ad-Duha: 1-2],

and other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra: 12], it means that He made the night dark, suited to quiet and rest, and made the day bright, suited to movement and occupation with livelihood in this world. So they strive for their livelihood during the day and rest from the fatigue of work at night. If the whole time were night, work for their livelihood would be difficult for them, and if the whole time were day, the fatigue of continuous work would destroy them.

Just as the night and the day are two signs from His signs, exalted is He, they are also two of His blessings, exalted is He.

This meaning alluded to here is explained in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made for you the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?" Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made for you the day perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you would rest? Then will you not see?" And out of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [Al-Qasas: 71-73].

So His saying ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ refers to the night, and His saying ﴿and seek of His bounty﴾ [Al-Qasas: 73] refers to the day. And His saying: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ ﴿And We made the night a covering﴾ ﴿And We made the day for livelihood﴾ - the verse [An-Naba': 9-11]; and His saying: ﴿And it is He who made for you the night as clothing and sleep as rest and made the day a resurrection﴾ [Al-Furqan: 47]; and His saying: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty﴾ - the verse [Ar-Rum: 23]; and His saying: ﴿And it is He who takes you in death by night and knows what you have committed by day﴾ [Al-An'am: 60]; and other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and that you might know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Al-Isra: 12], in it He explained another blessing upon His creation, which is their knowledge of the number of years and the reckoning. Because through the alternation of the night and the day they know the number of days, months and years, and by that they recognize Friday, so that they may perform the Friday prayer on it, and they recognize the month of fasting and the months of Hajj, and they know the passing of the months of the waiting period for one who observes the waiting period by months, as indicated in His saying: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation - if you doubt, then their waiting period is three months, and [the same for] those who have not menstruated﴾ [At-Talaq: 4], and His saying: ﴿And those who die among you and leave wives behind - they shall wait by themselves four months and ten days﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 234]. And they know the passing of the appointed terms set for debts, leases, and the like.

Exalted is He, explained this wisdom in other places, such as His saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. Allah did not create that except in truth. He details the verses for a people who know﴾ [Yunus: 5]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say, "They are measures of time for the people and for Hajj"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 189], and other verses besides these.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra: 12], there are two interpretive views among the scholars:

The first: that the speech contains an elided modifier (mudaf mahdhuf), and the intended meaning is: "And We made the two luminaries of the night and the day - that is, the sun and the moon - two signs."

According to this view, the sign of the night is the moon and the sign of the day is the sun, and al-mahw (effacement) is al-tams (obliteration). According to this view, the effacement of the sign of the night has been said to mean the blackness that is in the moon; this is the view of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mujahid, and it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾ [Al-Isra: 12] is that We did not place in the moon a ray like the ray of the sun by which you see things clearly; so the moon's light falls short of the sun's light, and this is the meaning of obliteration according to this view.

This is more apparent to me, because of His contrasting it with ﴿and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra: 12]. The claim that the meaning of effacing the sign of the night is the blackness in the moon does not appear to me to be correct, even though some of the noble Companions and some of the great scholars have said it.

As for His saying ﴿and made the sign of the day﴾ according to the explanation mentioned, that is: the sun is visible, meaning it has a ray by whose light everything is seen as it truly is.

Al-Kisa'i said: it is from the saying of the Arabs: "absara al-nahar" (the day became visible), when it brightened and became in a state in which one sees. Al-Qurtubi transmitted this from him.

The compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him, says: This explanation is of the same kind as their saying: "its day is fasting and its night is standing (in prayer)." And from it is the saying of the poet:

"You blamed us, O Umm Ghaylan, during the night journey, and you slept, though the night of the lover does not sleep."

The entire extent of the explanation in the aforementioned view is the elision of a modifier, and this is common in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech when a context indicates it. He said in the Khulasa: "What follows the mudaf comes in its place in i'rab when it is elided."

The context in the noble verse indicating the elided modifier is His saying ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾ [Al-Isra: 12], for the attribution of the sign to the night and the day is evidence that the two mentioned signs belong to them, not that they themselves are the signs. The elision of the modifier is common in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿And ask the town in which we were and the caravan in which we came﴾ [Yusuf: 82]; and His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers﴾ [An-Nisa': 23], meaning their marriage; and His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 3], meaning its eating; and the like.

According to the view that a modifier is elided and that the two signs intended are the sun and the moon, the verses clarifying that the sun and the moon are two signs have already been explained in Surat an-Nahl.

The second view of interpretation: that the noble verse contains no elided modifier, and that the two signs intended are the night and the day themselves, not the sun and the moon.

According to this view, the attribution of the sign to the night and the day is the attribution of a thing to itself with differing wording, treating the difference in wording as if it were a difference in meaning. The attribution of a thing to itself with differing wording is common in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. From the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿The month of Ramadan﴾ - the verse [Al-Baqarah: 185], and Ramadan is indeed the very same month in verification; and His saying: ﴿And the home of the Hereafter is better﴾ - the verse [Yusuf: 109], and the home is the Hereafter itself, as evidenced by His saying in another place: ﴿And the home of the Hereafter is truly [better]﴾ [Al-An'am: 32] with the definite article, where "the Hereafter" is an adjective of "the home"; and His saying: ﴿And We are closer to him than the jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16], where the jugular vein is the same as the vein; and His saying: ﴿And the evil plotting﴾ - the verse [Fatir: 43], where the plotting is the evil itself, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

From examples in Arabic speech is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Like a virgin of al-Muqana'a, white with yellow, nourished by water flowing freely, unmixed."

Because al-Muqana'a is the virgin herself. And the saying of 'Antarah in his Mu'allaqa:

"And a coat of mail, full-length, whose openings I tore with the sword from the defender of the truth, the one who makes himself known."

Because by "mishakk" he means the full-length coat itself, as evidenced by his saying "I tore its openings," since the pronoun refers to the full-length coat, which he expressed by "mishakk."

We have clarified this question in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) in Surat Fatir, and we explained that what appears to us is that the attribution of a thing to itself, with differing wording of the attributed and the attributed-to, is a stylistic feature of the Arabic language, because the difference of the two wordings is sometimes treated as a semantic difference, given how frequently such attribution occurs in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. Ibn Jarir decided this in some of his places in the Qur'an. On this basis there is no need for the interpretation referred to in His words in the Khulasa:

"A noun is not attributed to what is united with it in meaning; and interpret it when it occurs, if it seems problematic."

Among what indicates the weakness of the aforementioned interpretation is His saying:

"If the two are single, then attribute it definitively; otherwise, the following one takes after what precedes it."

Because the requirement of attributing a proper name to a title, while the two are united in meaning, if both are single nouns, necessitates interpretation, and the prohibition of the following construction (itba') which does not need interpretation is evidence that this is among the stylistic features of the Arabic language. If it were not among its features, it would be necessary to prefer what needs no interpretation over what needs interpretation, as you see.

On this second view of interpretation, the meaning is: "We effaced the sign which is the night, and We made the sign which is the day visible," that is, We made the night one whose light is effaced and obliterated, dark, in which things are not distinguished, just as what is on an erased tablet is not distinguished; and We made the day visible, that is, in it things are seen and distinguished.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And every matter We have detailed with full detail﴾ [Al-Isra: 12] has already been clarified, and the verses indicating it in Surat "an-Nahl," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification of all things﴾ - the verse [An-Nahl: 89].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open.﴾ ﴿"Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant."﴾.

Regarding His saying, glorified and exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck﴾ [al-Isra': 13], there are two well-known interpretations in tafsir (exegesis):

The first: that what is meant by "ṭā'ir" (omen) is his deeds, from the expression of the Arabs: "ṭāra lahu sahm" (an arrow flew out for him), when it came out for him; meaning: We have fastened to him what flew out for him of his deeds.

The second: that what is meant by "ṭā'ir" is what was decreed for him in the knowledge of Allah of wretchedness or happiness. The two views are mutually implicating, because what flies out for him of deeds is the cause of what he ends up with of wretchedness or happiness.

Now that you know the two mentioned interpretations, know that we have previously stated in the introduction to this blessed book that a verse may have two or more opinions among the scholars, all of which are true, and the Qur'an bears witness to it. So we will mention all the opinions and their evidences from the Qur'an, because they are all true. The two interpretations mentioned for this noble verse are both witnessed to by the Qur'an.

As for the first view, that what is meant by "ṭā'ir" is his deed, the verses indicating that a person's deed is fastened to him are very numerous:

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [an-Nisa': 123], etc.,

• and His saying: ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [at-Tahrim: 7], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are toiling toward your Lord with exertion, and you will meet Him﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 6],

• and His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾ [Fussilat: 46],

• and His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [az-Zalzalah: 7, 8].

Verses of this kind are very numerous.

As for the view that what is meant by "ṭā'ir" is his share which flew out for him in eternity of wretchedness or happiness, the verses indicating this are also numerous:

• such as His saying: ﴿It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [at-Taghabun: 2],

• and His saying: ﴿A party He has guided, and a party upon whom error was deserved﴾ [al-A'raf: 30],

• and His saying: ﴿A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze﴾ [ash-Shura: 7],

and other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿in his neck﴾ [al-Isra': 13]; meaning: We have made his deed, or what was decreed for him of wretchedness, in his neck, i.e., binding upon him like a necklace or a shackle that does not separate from him. From this is the saying of the Arabs: "taqallada-hā ṭawq al-ḥamāmah" (he wore it like the collar of the dove), and their saying: "al-mawt fī al-riqāb" (death is in the necks), and this matter is a noose around his neck. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Take her away, take her away; you have put her on like the dove's collar."

So the meaning in all of this is: binding and inseparability.

His saying, glorified and exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open﴾ [al-Isra': 13]: He mentioned, glorified and exalted, in this noble verse, that this deed which He fastened upon the person, He will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection in a record which he will find spread open, i.e., open, which he and others will read.

He explained some attributes of this record which he finds spread open in other verses. He made clear that among its attributes: the criminals will be fearful (mushfiqun), i.e., afraid of what is in it; that it leaves out nothing small or great except that it enumerates it; that they will find all that they did present, and none of it absent; and that Allah, glorified and exalted, will not wrong them in the recompense for it at all. This is in His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿And the record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this record that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

He explained in another place that some people will be given this record in their right hand — may Allah make us and our Muslim brethren among them — and whoever is given it in his right hand will be reckoned with an easy reckoning and will return to his family joyful, and he will be in a pleasing life, in a lofty garden whose fruits are near. He, exalted, said: ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be reckoned with an easy account, and he will return to his people joyful﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 7–9], and He, exalted, said: ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account." So he will be in a pleasant life, in an elevated garden, its fruits near﴾ [al-Haqqah: 19–23].

He explained in another place that whoever is given his record in his left hand will wish that he had not been given it, and that he will be commanded regarding him and will burn in Hellfire, and he will be threaded into a chain of the chains of the Fire whose length is seventy cubits. This is in His saying: ﴿And as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known what my account is. Oh, I wish it had been the decisive end. My wealth has not availed me. My authority has passed from me." [Allah will say], "Seize him and shackle him, then burn him in Hellfire; then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him"﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25–32]. May Allah protect us and our Muslim brethren from the Fire, and from what brings us near to it of speech and deed.

He explained in another place that whoever is given his record behind his back will burn in the Blaze and call for destruction. This is in His saying: ﴿But as for he who is given his record behind his back, he will call for destruction, and he will burn in the Blaze﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 10–12]. And His saying, exalted: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant﴾ [al-Isra': 14], meaning that his own self knows that he did not wrong, and nothing was written against him except what he did; because at that time he will remember all that he did in the world from the beginning of his life to its end, as He, exalted, said: ﴿Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13].

He, exalted, has also explained in other places that if he denies any of his deeds, his limbs will testify against him, such as:

• His saying, exalted: ﴿This Day We seal over their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet testify to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65],

• and His saying: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned." And you were not hiding, lest your hearing testify against you, or your eyes or your skins, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do. And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers﴾ [Fussilat: 21–23],

• and His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness, even if he presents his excuses﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 14–15].

Further clarification of this will come, Allah willing, in Surat al-Qiyamah.
