Note

The word "kafā" is used in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language in two ways:

It is used transitively, and it usually takes two objects, and the agent of this transitive usage is not introduced with "bi" (the preposition ba'), as in His saying: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in battle﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25], and His saying: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], and His saying: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137], and similar verses.

And it is used intransitively, and its agent is regularly put in the genitive with the added "bi" to emphasize sufficiency, as in His saying in this noble verse ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant﴾ [al-Isra': 14], His saying, exalted: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾, and similar.

The specification (tamyiz) frequently comes after its agent when it is in the genitive with "bi". Some scholars of Arabic claimed that the genitive of its agent with "bi" is obligatory, but the truth is that it is permissible not to put it in the genitive with "bi". From this is the saying of the poet:

"Umayrah, bid farewell, if you prepare to depart in the morning; old age and Islam suffice a man as a restrainer."

And the saying of another:

"His guidance informs me about the absent person of a man... guidance suffices, regarding what the man has hidden, as an informer."

As for the reading of the one who read "yalqāhu" with a dammah on the yā' and a shaddah on the qāf in the passive, the meaning is that Allah casts that record upon him on the Day of Resurrection, so the agent was omitted and the verb was made passive.

As for the reading of the one who read "yakhruju" with a fatḥah on the yā' and a ḍammah on the rā' as an active imperfect of kharaja, the agent is a pronoun referring to the omen, meaning the deed, and His saying "kitāban" is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) from the pronoun of the agent; meaning, on the Day of Resurrection it will come out — i.e., the deed expressed by the omen — in the state of being a record which he will find spread open. Likewise, on the reading "yukhraju" with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the rā' in the passive, the substitute pronoun for the agent refers also to the omen which is the deed, i.e., it will be brought out for him, that is his omen, meaning his deed, in the state of being a record.

As for the reading "yukhrijų" with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the rā' in the active, the agent is a pronoun referring to Allah, exalted, and His saying "kitāban" is the direct object, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection He, i.e., Allah, will bring out for him a record which he will find spread open.

As for the reading of the majority, including the seven: the nūn in "nukhriju" is the nūn of majesty, to match His saying "alzamnāhu," and "kitāban" is the direct object of "nukhraja" as is clear. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 15 (part 1 of 4):**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own self, and whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions that whoever is guided, acting in a way that pleases Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, his guidance is only for his own self, because it is he who receives the benefit of that guidance and its fruit in this world and the Hereafter. And whoever strays from the path of rectitude, acting in a way that angers his Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, his straying is only against his own self, because it is he who reaps the fruit of its evil and dreadful consequences, and so he will abide therein in the Fire.

He clarified this meaning in many places, (p-64)

• such as His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46],

• and His saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief, and whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare﴾ [al-Rum: 44],

• and His saying: ﴿There have certainly come to you insights from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own self, and whoever is blind, it is against it. And I am not a guardian over you﴾ [al-An'am: 104],

• and His saying: ﴿So whoever is guided, is only guided for his own self, and whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment. And I am not a trustee over you﴾ [Yunus: 108].

The verses of this kind are very numerous, and we have already presented a portion of them in surah "al-Nahl."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions that no soul bears the sin of another soul; rather, no soul bears anything but its own sin.

His saying: ﴿wa-la taziru﴾ [al-Isra': 15], meaning: does not bear, from "wazara, yaziru," when he carried (a load). From this comes the name "wazir" (vizier) of the ruler, because he bears the burdens of managing the affairs of the state. The "wizr" is sin; one says: "wazara yaziru wizran," when he sinned. "Wizr" also means a heavy weight that is laden; i.e., no bearer of burdens (wazirah) bears, meaning: sinful, the burden of another soul, i.e., its sin, or its heavy load. Rather, it bears only the burden of its own self.

This meaning has come in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and if a heavily laden one calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a near relative﴾ [Fatir: 18], and His saying: ﴿And every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and His saying: ﴿That is a nation that has passed away. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you earned, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do﴾ [al-Baqarah: 134, 141], and other verses besides these.

We have already explained in detail in surah "al-Nahl" that this verse is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13], nor by His saying: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Nahl: 25]. This is because what is meant by that is that they bore the burdens of their own straying, and the burdens of their misleading others; for whoever initiates an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, and that does not diminish anything from the burdens of the others, as has been fully explained previously.

* *

**Caution (tanbih)**

Two questions are raised against this noble verse:

The first: what is established in the Sahih from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "the deceased is punished for the weeping of his family over him." It is said: what is the basis for his being punished for the weeping of others, since holding him accountable for the weeping of others may lead one who does not know to think that it is from a person being taken to account for the sin of another?

The second question: the obligation of blood money for accidental killing upon the 'aqilah (the paternal kin who bear the liability), so it is said: what is the basis for imposing the blood money upon the 'aqilah (p-65) for the crime of another person?

As for the answer to the first: the scholars interpreted it in one of two ways:

The first: that the deceased had bequeathed that he be wailed over, as Tarafah ibn al-'Abd said in his Mu'allaqah:

"When I die, then lament me with what I am worthy of, and tear the collar over me, O daughter of Ma'bad."

Because if he bequeathed that he be mourned over, then his punishment is due to his bequeathing of the reprehensible, and that is from his own action, not the action of another.

The second: that he neglected to forbid them from wailing over him before his death, while knowing that they would wail over him; because his neglect of forbidding them is a failure on his part, and a violation of His saying: ﴿Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6]. So his punishment is then due to his failure and his leaving what Allah commanded him with His saying: ﴿Protect yourselves﴾, and so on. This is clear, as you see.

As for the second: that the imposition of blood money upon the 'aqilah is not a burdening of them with the burden of the killer; rather, it is a pure act of solidarity which Allah imposed upon the 'aqilah of the perpetrator, because the perpetrator did not intend harm, and there is no sin upon him at all. So Allah imposed, for his unintentional offense, the blood money by way of declaratory ruling (khitab al-wad'), and imposed the duty of solidarity in it upon the 'aqilah. There is no difficulty in Allah's imposing upon some of His creation the solidarity of some of His creation, just as He imposed the taking of zakat from the wealth of the rich and its return to the poor. Those who held that blood money for the unintentional killer is imposed upon the people of the killer's diwan (register), such as Abu Hanifah and others, believed that it is on the basis of support (al-nusrah), so they imposed it upon the people of the diwan. This view is supported by what al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir. He said: "The people of biographical reports and knowledge agree that blood money in the Jahiliyyah was borne by the 'aqilah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ affirmed it in Islam, and they used to bind themselves by mutual support (ta'aqqul bil-nusrah). Then Islam came and the matter continued in that way, until 'Umar established the diwan.

The jurists agreed on the transmission of this and its being held, and they agreed that there was no diwan during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor during the time of Abu Bakr; that 'Umar established the diwan, gathered the people together, made the people of each region one hand, and made it obligatory upon them to fight whoever was adjacent to them of the enemy." End of al-Qurtubi's words, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, does not punish anyone of His creation, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, until He sends to him a messenger who warns him and admonishes him, and that messenger is disobeyed, and [the person] persists in disbelief and disobedience after the warning and the establishment of proof (al-i'dhar).

Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, has clarified this meaning in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165]. In this noble verse He stated explicitly that there must be a cutting off of every person's argument by the sending of messengers, bringing good news to whoever obeys them of Paradise, and warning whoever disobeys them of the Fire.

This argument which He clarified here, that He cut off through the sending of messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, He explained at the end of surah Ta-Ha by His saying: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134].

He alluded to it in surah al-Qasas by His saying: ﴿And if not that a disaster should afflict them for what their hands have sent forth, they would say, "Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and be among the believers"﴾ [al-Qasas: 47],

• and His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are unaware﴾ [al-An'am: 131],

• and His saying: ﴿O People of the Book, there has come to you Our messenger, making clear to you after a gap (fatrah) of messengers, lest you say, "There came to us no bringer of good news or warner." But there has come to you a bringer of good news and a warner﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19],

• and like His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy﴾ ﴿Lest you say, "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of what they studied"﴾ ﴿Or lest you say, "If the Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than them." There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 155-157],

and other verses besides these.

What clarifies what these mentioned verses and their likes in the Noble Qur'an indicate, that Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, does not punish anyone except after warning and establishment of proof through the tongues of the messengers, peace be upon them, is His explicit statement, may He be glorified and exalted, in many verses: that He does not admit anyone into the Fire except after the establishment of proof and warning through the tongues of the messengers. Among that is His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?"﴾ ﴿They say, "Yes, there came to us a warner, but we denied and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything.'"﴾ [al-Mulk: 8, 9].

It is well known that His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: "Every time a group is thrown into it" encompasses all the groups thrown into the Fire.

Abu Hayyan said in "al-Bahr al-Muhit" in his tafsir of this verse which we are concerned with, his exact words: "'Kullama' (every time) indicates the generality of the times of throwing, and so it encompasses those who are thrown." And from that is His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers"﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. And His saying in this verse: "And those who disbelieved were driven" is general for all the disbelievers.

It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence (al-usul) that relative pronouns such as "alladhi" and "allati" and their derivatives are among the forms of generality, because of their generality over all that their relative clauses include. He arranged this in "Maraqi al-Su'ud" in his saying about the forms of generality:

"The form of 'kull' (all) or 'jami'' (whole), and the 'alladhi' and 'allati' and their derivatives have followed."

Its meaning in the verse: the words "kull," "jami'," "alladhi," "allati," and their derivatives are all forms of generality. So His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved were driven to Hell in groups﴾ up to His saying: ﴿They said, "Yes"﴾ [al-Zumar: 71] is general for all the disbelievers, and it is evident that all the people of the Fire had been warned by the messengers in the abode of this world, but they disobeyed the command of their Lord, as is clear.

Similar to it also is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is the Fire of Hell. It will not be decreed upon them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ ﴿And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do." Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would remember could remember therein, and the warner had come to you?﴾ [Fatir: 36, 37]. So His saying: "And those who disbelieved, for them is the Fire of Hell" up to His saying: "And the warner had come to you" is also general for all the people of the Fire, as its explanation was mentioned shortly before.

Similar to that is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?" They said, "Yes." They said, "Then call." But the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾ [Ghafir: 49, 50], and other verses besides these which indicate that all the people of the Fire were warned by the messengers in the abode of the world.

These verses that we have mentioned, and their likes in the Qur'an, indicate the excuse of the people of the fatrah, that no warner came to them, even if they died upon disbelief. And with this said a group of the people of knowledge.

But another group of the people of knowledge held that everyone who died upon disbelief is in the Fire, even if no warner came to him. They based this on the apparent meanings of verses from the Book of Allah, and on hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ. Among the verses they cited is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who die while they are disbelievers, for them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾ [al-Nisa': 18]; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, upon them is the curse of Allah, and the angels, and the people, all together﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161]; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold even if he ransomed himself by it. For them is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 91]; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]; and His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him, or the wind blew him down into a far place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31]; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾; and His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 50], and other verses besides these.

The apparent meaning of all these verses is generality, because they do not specify one disbeliever over another; rather, their apparent meaning is the inclusion of all the disbelievers.

"And among the hadiths indicating that disbelievers are not excused in their disbelief by the fatrah (the interval between prophets) is what Muslim related in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: 'A man said: O Messenger of Allah, where is my father? He said: "In the Fire." Then when he turned away, he called him and said: "Indeed my father and your father are in the Fire."' End quote. Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, also said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, and the wording is Yahya's, the two of them said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Yazid, that is Ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I asked my Lord for permission to seek forgiveness for my mother, but He did not permit me; and I asked Him for permission to visit her grave, and He permitted me.' Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, the two of them said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'The Prophet ﷺ visited the grave of his mother, and he wept and made those around him weep. Then he said: "I asked my Lord for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but I was not permitted; and I asked Him for permission to visit her grave, and He permitted me. So visit the graves, for they remind of death."' End quote. And other hadiths besides these indicate that the polytheists are not excused by the fatrah.

This dispute is well known among the scholars of usul (legal theory): Are the polytheists who died during the fatrah while worshipping idols in the Fire because of their disbelief, or are they excused by the fatrah? Al-Shinqiti (Mukhtar?) — [the author] set it out in Maraqi al-Su'ud with his words:

"The one in the fatrah, in the branch, is not to be regarded, / and in the usul there is dispute among them."

Among those who held that the people of the fatrah who died upon disbelief are in the Fire is al-Nawawi in his commentary on Muslim, and al-Qarafi in Sharh al-Tanqih reported consensus upon it, as the author of Nashr al-Bunud quoted him.

The proponents of this view answered the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15] in four ways:

The first: that the punishment negated in His words ﴿And We would never punish﴾ and similar verses refers only to worldly punishment, as occurred in this world to the people of Nuh, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, the people of Lut, the people of Shu'ayb, the people of Musa and others. Accordingly, this does not conflict with punishment in the Hereafter.

al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan, al-Shawkani and others in their tafsirs attributed this view to the majority (al-jumhur).

The second: that the excuse by the fatrah stated in His words ﴿And We would never punish﴾ and similar verses applies to what is not clear, which is not hidden from even the least intelligent person. As for what is clear and not hidden from anyone with intellect, such as worshipping idols, no one is excused in it, because the disbelievers acknowledge that Allah is their Lord, the Creator, the Provider, the One who benefits and harms, and they fully realize that idols cannot bring benefit or repel harm, as He said about the people of Ibrahim, upon him and our Prophet be blessings and peace: ﴿You certainly know that these do not speak﴾ [al-Anbiya: 65]. And as the Qur'anic verses many times state, that at times of hardship they sincerely call upon Allah alone, knowing that others neither benefit nor harm:

• as in His words: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Ankabut: 65],
• and His words: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32],
• and His words: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him﴾ [al-Isra: 67],
and other verses. But the disbelievers deceived themselves due to their intense fanaticism for their idols, claiming that they bring them near to Allah and are their intercessors with Allah, though reason decisively rejects this.

The third: that they retained some remnant of warning from what the messengers sent before our Prophet ﷺ brought, such as Ibrahim and others, and that the proof is thereby established against them. al-Nawawi affirmed this in his commentary on Muslim, and al-'Ibadi inclined to it in (al-Ayat al-Bayyinat).

The fourth: the authentic hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ indicating that some of the people of the fatrah are in the Fire, as we have already mentioned some of the hadiths narrated on this in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere.

Those who held the excuse of the fatrah answered these four points. As for the first, that the punishment in His words ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15] refers only to worldly punishment and not the otherworldly, they answered on two grounds:

The first: that it contradicts the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, for the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is the negation of punishment absolutely, which is more general than being in this world, and diverting the Qur'an from its apparent meaning is impermissible except by a proof to which one must return.

The second: that the Qur'an, in many verses, indicates that the punishment negated in the verse includes punishment in the Hereafter, such as His words: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them: Did no warner come to you?﴾ ﴿They say: Yes﴾ [al-Mulk: 8-9]. This is evidence that all groups of the people of the Fire were not punished in the Hereafter except after the warning of the messengers, as already explained with Qur'anic verses.

As for the second point, that the place of the excuse by the fatrah is in what is not clear and not hidden from anyone, they answered with the same two responses mentioned just above, because the distinction between what is clear and what is not is contrary to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, so it requires a proof to which one must return; and because Allah explicitly stated that the people of the Fire were not punished by it until they had denied the messengers in the worldly life, after being warned of that clear disbelief, as already explained.

As for the third point, which al-Nawawi affirmed and al-'Ibadi inclined to, namely that the proof is established against them by the warning of messengers sent before him ﷺ, they said it is a false statement without doubt, due to the abundance of Qur'anic verses explicitly declaring its falsehood, since its implication is that they were warned through some messengers, while the Qur'an categorically negates this in many verses, such as His words in Ya-Sin: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6]. The "ma" in His words ﴿ma unzira abaa'uhum﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6] is, in verification, a negation particle, not a relative pronoun, and the fa' in His words "fahum ghafiluna" (so they are heedless) indicates this. And His words in al-Qasas: ﴿And you were not at the side of the mountain when We called, but it was a mercy from your Lord, that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾ [al-Qasas: 46], and His words in Saba': ﴿And We did not give them books they study, nor did We send to them before you any warner﴾ [Saba': 44], and His words in al-Sajdah: ﴿Or do they say he has invented it? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾ [al-Sajdah: 3], and other verses.

As for the fourth point, they answered that those hadiths in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere are solitary reports (akhbar ahad), which are overridden by the definitive text, namely His words ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15], and His words ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them: Did no warner come to you? They say: Yes﴾ [al-Mulk: 8-9], and similar verses.

The proponents of the excuse by the fatrah also answered the verses that their opponents cited, such as His words: ﴿And those who die while they are disbelievers, for them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾ [al-Nisa: 18], and the rest of the verses previously mentioned, that the scope of those applies where messengers were sent to them and they denied them, as evidenced by His words: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15]. And the proponents of punishment of idol-worshippers among the people of the fatrah answered their opponents' claim that the definitive text, His words ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾, must be given precedence over the solitary hadiths indicating punishment of some of the people of the fatrah, such as the two hadiths of Muslim in his Sahih mentioned earlier: that the verse is general, while the two hadiths are both specific to a particular individual, and it is known in usul that a general and a specific text do not contradict, because the specific text restricts the general, as is the view of the majority, unlike Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, as we have explained in another place.

So whatever a specific proof has excluded has gone out from the generality, and whatever a specific proof has not excluded remains included in the generality, as is established in usul.

The opponents answered that this specification nullifies the wisdom of the general text, because Allah, exalted is He, praised Himself for perfect equity, and that He does not punish until He cuts off the proof of the one punished by warning through messengers in the worldly life. He pointed out that this complete equity and the establishing of excuse, which is cutting off excuse, is the cause for non-punishment; so if He punished a single person without warning, that wisdom by which He praised Himself would be undermined, and that person would have the proof for which Allah sent the messengers to cut it off, as He stated: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa: 165], and His words: ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger so we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134], as already explained.

The opponents answered this: even if it is granted that the absence of warning in the worldly life is a cause for non-punishment in the Hereafter, and the cause of the ruling (absence of warning in the world) is present while the ruling (non-punishment in the Hereafter) is absent, due to the explicit text of the hadiths on punishment there, then the presence of the cause without the ruling, which in the terminology of the usul scholars is called "naqd" (breach/counter-example), is a specification of the cause, meaning that it is restricted to some of the individuals of its effect by an external proof, like the specification of a general term; that is, restricting it to some of its instances by a proof. The disagreement over whether a breach is an invalidation of the cause or a specification of it is well known in usul, and the author of Maraqi al-Su'ud set out the views on this in his section on the defects of causes, saying:

"Among them is the presence of the attribute without the ruling, which the scholars of knowledge call a breach (naqd).
Most of them consider it not damaging; rather it is a specification, and this is what justifies it.
It has been narrated from Malik that it is a specification, if it is derived by deduction and not by explicit statement.
The opposite of this was held by some, and the choice for the concise is 'breach'.
If it is not expressly stated by an apparent text, and what is deduced is not harmful,
whether it is due to the absence of a condition or to what prevented it, and agreement occurred in cases like the 'arayā."

In these verses he pointed to five views on breach: whether it is a specification or an invalidation of the cause, together with the details he mentioned for those views.

Some verifying scholars of usul chose that if the non-application of the ruling to the cause is due to an impediment that prevented the cause from taking effect, or due to the absence of a condition for its effect, then it is a specification of the cause; otherwise it is a breach and invalidation of it. Thus, deliberate unjust killing is a cause for retaliation (qisas) by consensus.

When this compound attribute, deliberate unjust killing, is present but the ruling, retaliation, is not applied in the case of a father killing his son, because paternity is an impediment preventing the cause from taking effect in the ruling, it is not said that this cause is breached because the ruling does not follow it in this case; rather it is a cause which an impediment has prevented from taking effect, so its effect is restricted to what no impediment has prevented.

Likewise, one who marries his slave-woman to a man and deceives him by claiming she is free, and she bears a child from him: the child is free, even though the slavery of the mother is by consensus a cause for the slavery of the child, because every possessor of a womb's offspring follows its status; but deception is an impediment that prevented the cause, which is the mother's slavery, from taking effect in the ruling, which is the child's slavery.

Likewise adultery, for it is a cause for stoning by consensus."

(p-73) Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the cause of this punishment in His words: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Hashr: 4]. Yet some who opposed Allah and His Messenger are not punished with the punishment that the Banu al-Nadir received, although they share the same cause, which is opposition to Allah and His Messenger.

This shows that the non-application of the ruling to the cause in some instances is a specification (takhsis) of the cause, not a counter-example (naqd) to it. Allah knows best.

As for the sale of dry dates for fresh dates in the matter of the sale of 'arayā (a permitted exception to the prohibition of riba), it is a specification of the cause by consensus (ijma'), not a counter-example to it, as he indicated in the verses where he said:

"Conformity occurred in cases like the 'arayā."

The author, may Allah pardon him, said: The apparent truth regarding this question, namely whether polytheists are excused by the fatrah (the period of no prophet between two messengers), is that they are excused by the fatrah in this world, and that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will test them with a fire, ordering them to plunge into it. Whoever plunges into it enters Paradise, and he is the one who would have believed the messengers had they come to him in this world. Whoever refrains enters the Fire and is punished therein, and he is the one who would have denied the messengers had they come to him in this world, because Allah knows what they would have done had the messengers come to them.

We say that this is the correct position on this question for two reasons:

The first: this has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and its authenticity from him is a text on the very point in dispute, so there is no basis for dispute at all in light of it.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his commentary on this verse under discussion, after citing the many hadiths that indicate their being excused by the fatrah and their being tested on the Day of Resurrection, while answering Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's weakening of the hadiths about their excuse and testing, on the grounds that the Hereafter is an abode of recompense, not of action, and that the obligation to enter the Fire is an obligation to what cannot be borne and is impossible, the following, and these are his words:

"As for the reply to what he said: the hadiths of this chapter include some that are sahih, as many imams of the scholars have stated, some that are hasan, and some that are da'if which are strengthened by the sahih and hasan. When the hadiths of one chapter are connected and mutually reinforcing in this manner, they establish proof for the one who examines them. As for his saying that the Abode of the Hereafter is an abode of recompense, there is no doubt that it is an abode of recompense, but this does not contradict obligation in its plains before entering Paradise or the Fire, as Shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari related from the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community regarding the testing of children. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when a shin will be laid bare, and they will be summoned to prostration﴾ [al-Qalam: 42].

It is established in the Sahih and other collections that: 'The believers will prostrate to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, while the hypocrite will not be able to do so; his back will become like a single slab, one layer, and whenever he tries to prostrate he falls on his back.' In the Two Sahihs, regarding the man who will be the last of the people of the Fire to leave it: 'Allah takes his covenants and pledges that he will not ask for anything other than what he is in, and this repeats, and Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, how excuse-seeking you are! Then He permits him to enter Paradise.'

As for his saying: 'How then does Allah obligate them to enter the Fire, when that is not within their capacity?' this is not an obstacle to the authenticity of the hadith. For Allah commands the servants on the Day of Resurrection to cross the Sirat, which is a bridge over the back of Hell, sharper than the sword and finer than a hair. The believers cross it according to their deeds, like lightning, like the wind, and like the finest swift horses and riding beasts. Some run, some walk, some crawl, and some are thrown on their faces into the Fire.' What is reported about those is no greater than this; rather, this is a graver and more severe matter.

Also: the Sunnah has established that the Dajjal will have with him a Garden and a Fire, and the Lawgiver commanded believers who meet him that one of them should drink from what appears to him as fire, for it will be cool and safe for him. So this is a parallel to that.

Also: Allah the Exalted commanded the Children of Israel to kill themselves, and so some of them killed others, until it is said that in one morning seventy thousand were killed, a man killing his father and his brother, while they were under a cloud that Allah had sent over them. That was a punishment for them for worshipping the calf. This too is very difficult for souls and is not less than what is reported in the hadith mentioned. And Allah knows best." End of Ibn Kathir's words, verbatim.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, also said shortly before this passage the following:

"Some have held that they will be tested on the Day of Resurrection in the plains of the gathering. Whoever obeys enters Paradise, and Allah's knowledge of him is revealed through his prior happiness. Whoever disobeys enters the Fire humiliated, and Allah's knowledge of him is revealed through his prior wretchedness.

This view reconciles all the evidences, and it is explicitly stated in the preceding mutually reinforcing hadiths, some of which corroborate others.

This is the view that Shaykh Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari related from the People of the Sunnah and the Community, and it is the view supported by the Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi in his book al-I'tiqad, as well as other verifying scholars, critics and hadith masters." End of the relevant part of Ibn Kathir's words, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is very clear in what we have mentioned.

The second matter: reconciling the evidences is obligatory wherever possible, without any disagreement, because acting on both proofs is better than discarding one of them. There is no way to reconcile the evidences except this view of excuse and testing. Whoever enters the Fire is the one who did not comply with what he was commanded during that test. Thus all the evidences are harmonized. Allah knows best.

It is not hidden that a statement like Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's, may Allah have mercy on him, that the Hereafter is an abode of recompense and not an abode of action, cannot be made to conflict with the authentic and established texts from the Prophet (ﷺ), as we explained in our book Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book).

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab:

(p-322) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah Bani Isra'il.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾.

This noble verse explicitly states that Allah, exalted is He, does not punish anyone until He warns them through His messengers, peace be upon them.

A parallel to it is His saying: ﴿messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165].

And His saying: ﴿If We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we could follow Your signs?"﴾ to the end of the verse [Ta-Ha: 134].

And His saying: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware﴾ [al-An'am: 131], and other verses.

It is confirmed by His explicit statement that every group of the people of the Fire had messengers come to them in the worldly abode, in His saying: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They will say, "Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him"﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Mulk: 8-9].

It is known that "every time" (kullama) is a form of generality. A parallel to it is His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾ up to His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come true upon the disbelievers"﴾ [al-Zumar: 71].

So His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven﴾ includes every disbeliever, because it is established in the principles of jurisprudence that relative pronouns are forms of generality by their generality, which encompasses whatever their clauses cover, as he indicated in Maraqi al-Su'ud with his words:

(p-323)
"The form 'kull' or 'jami'' and those that follow 'alladhi' and 'allati' and their derivatives."

The meaning of his saying "and those that follow alladhi, etc." is that alladhi, allati and their derivatives are forms of generality like kull and jami'.

A parallel to it is also His saying: ﴿And they will cry out therein … and there came to you the warner﴾ [Fatir: 37], which is also general, because the beginning of the speech is: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is the fire of Hell﴾ [Fatir: 36].

Similar verses in the Qur'an are many. However, some verses indicate that the people of the fatrah are in the Fire, such as His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Tawbah: 113]. Its generality indicates the entry of one who did not reach the Prophet (ﷺ). Likewise the generality of His saying: ﴿Nor those who die while they are disbelievers — for them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾ [al-Nisa': 18].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold﴾ to the end of the verse [Al 'Imran: 91], and other verses.

Know first that whoever did not receive a warner in the worldly abode and was a disbeliever until he died, the scholars differed about him: is he among the people of the Fire because of his disbelief, or is he excused because no warner came to him? As he indicated in Maraqi al-Su'ud with his words:

"One in a fatrah is not to be considered in the branches, but among the principles there is dispute among them."

We will mention, if Allah wills, the response of each of the two positions, and we will mention what the evidence indicates to be preferable. We say, and in Allah we seek help:

Some people have said that the disbeliever is in the Fire even if he died in the period of fatrah. Among those who firmly held this view is al-Nawawi in his commentary on Muslim, because of the hadiths indicating the punishment of some people of the fatrah.

(p-324) Al-Qarafi, in his commentary on al-Tanqih, related a consensus that the dead of the people of ignorance are in the Fire because of their disbelief, as related from him by the author of Nashr al-Bunud.

The proponents of this view answered the verse: ﴿And We would never punish﴾ and similar verses in three ways:

The first: the punishment negated in His saying: ﴿And We would never punish﴾ and similar verses is the worldly punishment, so it does not contradict the establishment of punishment in the Hereafter.

Al-Shawkani mentioned in his commentary that restricting this negated punishment to the worldly abode and not the Hereafter is the view of the majority, though he himself favoured the opposite, and he rejected restricting it to worldly punishment on the grounds that it contradicts the apparent meaning of the verses, and that the preceding verses which indicate the admission of all the people of the Fire that messengers warned them in the worldly abode are explicit in negating it.

The second: the place of the excuse of fatrah stated in His saying: ﴿And We would never punish﴾ and similar verses applies to what is not clear, which is not obscure to any rational person.

As for what is clear and not hidden from anyone with intellect, such as worshipping idols, no one is excused in it, because all disbelievers acknowledge that Allah is their Lord, their Creator and their Provider, and they are certain that idols cannot bring benefit or ward off harm. But they deceived themselves, claiming that the idols bring them near to Allah and are their intercessors with Allah, although reason definitively rules this out.

The third: they have a remnant of warning from what the messengers who came before him (ﷺ) brought, by which the proof is established against them. Ibn Qasim in al-Ayat al-Bayyinat inclined to this somewhat.

We have already stated in Surah Al 'Imran that this view is refuted by the Qur'an in many verses explicitly negating the very existence of a warner among them, such as His saying: ﴿So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6].

[p. 325] And His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾.

And His saying: ﴿You were not on the side of the mount when We called, but it was a mercy from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾ [al-Qasas: 46].

And His saying: ﴿We did not give them any books that they might study, nor did We send to them any warner before you﴾ [Saba': 44], and other verses besides these.

Those who held the opposing view answered: the people of the *fatra* (the interval between prophets, a period without a messenger) are excused, in light of His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Tawbah: 113], and the verses cited above, that it does not become clear to them that they are among the companions of the Fire, and they are not judged to be in the Fire even if they die as disbelievers, except after they have been warned and have refused to believe, like Abu Talib. They interpreted the aforementioned verses in this sense.

This answer was objected to on the basis of what is established in the Sahih (the authentic collections) concerning some people of the *fatra* entering the Fire, such as the hadith: "Indeed my father and your father are in the Fire," which is established in Sahih Muslim and similar hadiths. This objection was in turn answered: even if the hadiths are authentic, they are solitary reports (*akhbar ahad*), and they are outweighed by a definitive (*qati'*) text, such as His saying: ﴿We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾.

This objection was also answered: there is no contradiction between a general (*'amm*) and a specific (*khass*) text; whatever an authentic hadith excludes has gone out from the generality, and whatever no authentic text excludes remains within the generality.

This objection was also answered: this specification (*takhsis*) nullifies the effective cause (*'illah*) of the general ruling, because Allah the Exalted praised Himself for perfect equity, and declared that He does not punish until He has cut off the proof of the one who is punished by the sending of messengers in this world, and He made clear that this complete equity is the cause of the absence of punishment. So if He punished a single person without a warning, that wisdom would be disrupted, and the proof which Allah sent the messengers to cut off would be established against that punished person, as He declared in His saying: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165].

This proof, between the two of them, is in *Surat Taha* in His saying: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾ [Taha: 134].

He alluded to it in *Surat al-Qasas* in His saying: ﴿And had it not been that a calamity might befall them...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and that we might be among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 47].

This last objection follows the dispute over the *naqd* (counter-example, a case where the cause is present but the ruling is absent): is it a flaw in the cause or a specification of it? This is a well-known, widespread disagreement in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*), which he set out in *Maraqi al-Su'ud* in his enumeration of the defects in evidence, saying:

Among them: the presence of the attribute without the ruling,
Which the guardians of knowledge call *naqd* (counter-example).
Most of them hold that it does not invalidate,
Rather it is a specification, and this is the sound view.
It has been narrated from Malik that it is a specification,
If the derivation is by inference, not by explicit text.
The reverse of this has been held by some,
And the chosen view in the concise works is that it is *naqd*,
If its explicit text is not apparent,
And there is no harm in what was derived by inference,
If it comes due to the absence of a condition or due to something that prevents it,
And the agreement occurs in cases like *al-'araya*.

The verifying scholars among the jurists hold that if the absence of the cause's effect is due either to the presence of an obstacle to its effect or to the absence of a condition for its effect, then its presence alongside the non-existence of the ruling does not invalidate it or impair it. And the exclusion of some individual cases of the ruling in that situation is a specification of the cause, not a counter-example to it, like intentional unjust killing, which is the cause of retaliation (*qisas*) by consensus. The non-application of this ruling in the case of a father killing his son does not impair this cause, because its effect was prevented by an obstacle, namely fatherhood. But if the absence of its effect is not due to the presence of an obstacle or the absence of a condition, then it is a counter-example to it and an impairment of it. However, against this verification, there is what some scholars mentioned: that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 13] is an explicitly stated cause for His saying: ﴿Had Allah not decreed for them exile, He would have punished them﴾ [al-Hashr: 3], and so on.

Yet this cause may exist without the punishment that befell the Banu al-Nadir, namely exile or worldly chastisement, existing. This supports the view that the counter-example is a general specification and not an impairment.

This is answered by saying: some of the verifying scholars among the usulis said that the aforementioned verification applies to the derived (*mustanbata*) cause, not the explicitly stated (*mansusa*) one, and this is explicitly stated, as we have already mentioned in the verses of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* in His saying:
"... and there is no harm in what was derived by inference, if it comes due to the absence of a condition or due to something that prevents it."

This is the summary of the scholars' statements and their arguments on the question. What appears to be the stronger view by evidence is reconciling the texts, because reconciliation is obligatory when it is possible, without disagreement, as he indicated in *al-Maraqi* in his saying:

"And reconciliation is obligatory when it is possible."
Etc.

The way to reconcile these proofs is this: they are excused by the *fatra*, and they will be tested on the Day of Resurrection by being commanded to plunge into a fire. Whoever plunges into it enters Paradise, and this is the one who would have believed the messengers had they come to him in the world. Whoever refuses is punished with the Fire, and this is the one who would have disbelieved the messengers had they come to him in the world, for Allah knows what they would have done had the messengers come to them.

With this reconciliation the proofs agree: the people of the *fatra* are excused; some of them are among the people of the Fire after the testing, and some of them are among the people of Paradise after it as well. Each of the two statements is applied to some of them whose final destiny Allah knew and informed His Prophet ﷺ of, and thus the contradiction disappears.

The evidence for this reconciliation is the reports transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ concerning it. Ibn Kathir, in his commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾, after citing the hadiths that indicate their excuse and their testing on the Day of Resurrection, responded to Ibn Abd al-Barr's weakening of the hadiths about their excuse and testing, with the following text:

"The answer to what he said is that the hadiths of this topic include some that are authentic, as many of the leading scholars have stated, some that are good (*hasan*), and some that are weak but strengthened by the authentic and the good. When the hadiths of a single topic are connected and mutually supporting, this category becomes known, and they provide proof for the one who examines them." The relevant point ends with his words.

Then he said: "This view has been held by a group of verifying scholars, hadith critics and memorizers. As for what some have argued in rejecting these hadiths, namely that the Hereafter is a place of recompense, not a place of action and trial, this is rejected on two grounds:

The first: that claim is not contradicted by the authentic texts from him ﷺ. Even if we accept the generality of the one who said that the Hereafter is not a place of action, the aforementioned hadiths would be specifying that generality.

The second: we do not accept that testing is absent in the plains of the Gathering (*'arasat al-mahshar*). Rather, we say that a definitive text indicates it, because Allah the Exalted declared in *Surat al-Qalam* that they are called to prostrate, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostration﴾ [al-Qalam: 42], up to the end of the verse."

It is known that their being commanded to prostrate is an obligation in the plains of the Gathering. And it is established in the Sahih that the believers prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and that the hypocrite is unable to do so, and his back becomes like a single flat slab, one layer, whenever he tries to prostrate he falls on his back.

And in the two Sahihs, concerning the man who will be the last of the people of the Fire to leave it, that Allah takes his covenants and pledges that he will not ask for anything other than what he is in, and this repeats many times, and Allah the Exalted says: "O son of Adam, how treacherous you are!" Then He permits him to enter Paradise. It is known that those covenants and pledges are an obligation in the plains of the Gathering. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defiantly transgress therein; so the word takes effect against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction﴾, regarding His saying ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾ [al-Isra': 16], there are three well-known positions among the scholars of tafsir (exegesis) concerning this noble verse:

The first, which is the correct view attested by the Qur'an, and which is held by the majority of scholars, is that the "command" in His saying "We command" is the command that is the opposite of prohibition. The object of the command is omitted because it is evident, and the meaning is: We commanded its affluent ones to obey Allah and to affirm His oneness, to believe in His messengers and follow them in what they brought. ﴿So they transgressed﴾, meaning they departed from obedience to the command of their Lord, disobeyed Him, and denied His messengers. ﴿So the word took effect against it﴾, meaning the threat became due against it. ﴿So We destroyed it with complete destruction﴾, meaning We annihilated it with total annihilation. The verb "destroy" (tadmir) was emphasized by its verbal noun (masdar) to express intensity in the severity of the destruction that befell them.

This view, which is the truth in this verse, is supported by many verses, such as His saying: ﴿And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command immorality"﴾ [al-A'raf: 28], and so on. His, may He be exalted and high, explicit statement that He does not command immorality is clear evidence that His saying ﴿We command its affluent ones, and they transgress﴾ [al-Isra': 16] means: We commanded them to obedience and they disobeyed; the meaning is not "We commanded them to sin and they sinned," because Allah does not command immorality.

Among the verses indicating this is His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent"﴾ and ﴿They said, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished"﴾ [Saba': 34, 35].

His saying in this verse: ﴿And We did not send a warner into a town﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23] is a general expression covering all the affluent ones from all towns, that the messengers commanded them to obey Allah, and they said to them: ﴿Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent﴾, and they boasted of their wealth and children. Verses of this kind are numerous.

By this verification you know that what al-Zamakhshari claimed in his Kashshaf, that the meaning of "We command its affluent ones" is: We commanded them to sin and they sinned, and that this is a metaphor (majaz), treating the lavishing of blessings upon them, which necessitates their insolence and disbelief, as equivalent to the command to that, is a statement that is entirely evidently baseless and false. Abu Hayyan in al-Bahr and al-Razi in his tafsir have clarified its refutation, and no fair and knowledgeable person doubts its falsity.

This correct view of the verse is in accordance with the familiar Arabic usage, as in their saying: "I commanded him and he disobeyed me," meaning I commanded him to obey and he disobeyed. The meaning is not "I commanded him to disobey," as is clear.

The second view regarding the verse: the "command" in His saying ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾ is a cosmic, predestined command (amr kawni qadari), meaning: We decreed that for them and made them subject to it, because each is made easy for that for which he was created. The cosmic predestined command is

• like His saying: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50],

• and His saying: ﴿So We said to them, "Be apes, despised"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 65],

• and His saying: ﴿There came to it Our command by night or by day﴾ [Yunus: 24],

• and His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82].

The third view regarding the verse: that "amara" here means "akthara" (to increase), i.e., We increased its affluent ones, and they transgressed.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "amara" in the sense of "akthara" is an eloquent dialectal form, like "amara" with the lengthened alif (ā-mara), and the hadith that Imam Ahmad narrated from Suwayd ibn Hubayrah supports this, that the Prophet ﷺ said: «The best wealth of a man is a fruitful (ma'murah) mare, or a well-ordered (ma'burah) row of palms.»

Ibn Kathir said: Imam Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book al-Gharib: "al-ma'murah" means one with abundant offspring. "al-sikkah" means a row of palms arranged in a line. "al-ma'burah" is from ta'bir, which is hanging the male (pollen) on the palm tree so that its fruit does not fall. It is known that the form ma'murah on the pattern of the passive participle indicates that amara, with fatha on the mim, is unaugmented, transitive by itself to the object, so the meaning of its being "akthara" becomes clear. Yet more than one scholar denied that the triliteral amara in the sense of "increase" is transitive to an object, and they said: the hadith of Suwayd ibn Hubayrah mentioned is of the type of paired wording (izdiwaj), like their saying "al-ghadaya wa al-'ashaya" (the mornings and the evenings), and like the hadith «return with burdens (mazwurat) not rewarded (ma'jurat)». For "ghadaya" is not correct on its own; it was permitted only for the pairing with "'ashaya." Likewise "ma'zurat" with a hamza is contrary to the original, since the root is from wizr with a waw; but the hamza in His saying "ma'zurat" was for pairing with "ma'jurat," and pairing permits what is not permitted otherwise, as is known. Accordingly, "ma'murah" is a follower of "ma'burah," though it is mentioned before it, for the correspondence between the two words.

Shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: His saying, may He be exalted: "amrana" [al-Isra': 16]. Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, Abu Raja', Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi', Mujahid, and al-Hasan read "ammarna" with shaddah, and it is the reading of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, meaning: We made its evil ones rulers, so they disobeyed therein, and when they did that, We destroyed them.

Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi said: "ammarna" with the mim doubled: We made them commanders, empowered.

Ibn 'Aziz also said it, and "ta'ammara 'alayhim" means he became dominant over them. Al-Hasan also read, as did Qatadah, Abu Haywah al-Shami, Ya'qub, Kharijah from Nafi', Hammad ibn Salamah from Ibn Kathir, and 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas with variation from them: "amarna" with the madd and light pronunciation; meaning: We increased its tyrants and its commanders, as al-Kisa'i said.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "amartuhu" with the madd and "amartuhu" are two dialects meaning "akthartuhu" (I increased him).

From this is the hadith «The best wealth is a fruitful mare, or a well-ordered row of palms», meaning abundant in offspring and progeny. Likewise Ibn 'Aziz said: "amarna" and "amarna" have one meaning, i.e., We increased. And from al-Hasan also, and Yahya ibn Ya'mur: "amarna," with qasr and kasrah on the mim, on the pattern "f'ilna," and it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: the meaning is "We increased." Abu Zayd and Abu 'Ubayd related something similar, but al-Kisa'i denied it and said: from abundance one says only "amarna" with the madd, and its original is "a-amarna," which was lightened; this was related by al-Mahdawi.

In al-Sihah: Abu al-Hasan said: "amira maluhu" (with kasrah) means it became abundant, and "amira al-qawm" means they became numerous. The poet said, and he is al-A'sha:

> Tarifun wa la-ddunna kulla mubarakin, amiruna la yarithuna sahma al-qu'dudi

And "amara Allah malahu" with the madd. Al-Tha'labi: It is said of a large thing: amr, and the verb from it: amara al-qawm ya'muruna amran, when they became numerous.

Ibn Mas'ud said: In the Jahiliyyah we used to say of a tribe when they became numerous: "amara amri banu fulan." Labid said:

> Every family of Hurrah, their end is ... qul, even if they multiply in number
> If they prosper they will descend, and if they become numerous one day, they will come to ruin and misery

I say: and in the sound hadith of Heraclius: «Indeed, the affair of the son of Abi Kabshah has increased (amara), and indeed the king of the Banu al-Asfar fears him»; meaning it increased. All of these are intransitive, and for this reason al-Kisa'i denied it, and Allah knows best.

Al-Mahdawi said: As for the one who reads "amara," it is a dialect; and the way amara is made transitive is that he likened it to "'amara" (to populate), since abundance is closest to cultivation, so he made it transitive as 'amara is transitive. He went on to say: It was also said: "amarnahum" means "ja'alnahum umara'" (we made them rulers), since the Arabs say: "amir ghayr ma'mur" (a ruler not commanded), meaning not appointing others. It was also said its meaning is: We sent its arrogant ones. Harun said: it is the reading of Ubayy: "ba'athna akabira mujrimiha fa-fasaqu fiha," mentioned by al-Mawardi.

Al-Nahhas related: Harun said that in the reading of Ubayy: "wa-idha aradna an nuhlika qaryatan ba'athna fiha akabira mujrimiha fa-makaru fiha fa-haqqa 'alayha al-qawl." End of the relevant point from al-Qurtubi's words.

You have learned that the verification indicated by the Qur'an is that the meaning of the verse is: We commanded its affluent ones to obey, and they disobeyed Our command; so the threat became due against them, and We destroyed them, as its explanation has preceded.

Note (tanbih)

In this noble verse there is a well-known question: it may be said that Allah attributed the transgression therein specifically to the affluent ones, to the exclusion of others, in His saying ﴿We command its affluent ones, and they defiantly transgress therein﴾ [al-Isra': 16], although He mentioned the general destruction of all the affluent and others, in His saying ﴿So the word takes effect against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction﴾ [al-Isra': 16], meaning the town, and He did not exempt from it anyone other than the affluent?

The answer is in two respects:

The first: the non-affluent are followers of them. The affluent, who are their leaders and great ones, were specifically mentioned, because others are followers of them, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our great ones, and they led us astray from the way"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67],

• and like His saying: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their bonds are cut off﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166],

• and His saying: ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these led us astray"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38],

• and His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And they will come forth to Allah all together, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were to you followers; can you then avail us against the punishment of Allah at all?"﴾ [Ibrahim: 21],

• and His saying: ﴿And when they argue in the Fire, and the weak say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were to you followers; can you then avail us any portion of the Fire?"﴾ [Ghafir: 47],

and other verses besides these.

The second: if some of them disobey Allah, rebel and transgress, and the others do not forbid them, then the destruction encompasses all, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And beware of a trial that will not strike those among you who have wronged in particular﴾ [al-Anfal: 25]. In the Sahih, from the hadith of the Mother of the Believers Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her: that when she heard the Prophet ﷺ say: «There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today there has been opened from the barrier of Gog and Magog such an opening,» and he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it, she said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness increases." And we have already presented this discussion in explanation in surah al-Ma'idah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due striving, while being a believer—those are the ones whose striving will be appreciated﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions ﴿Blameworthy and rejected﴾ [al-Isra': 18] and ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due striving﴾ [al-Isra': 19], meaning: he performs for it the deed by which it is attained, which is obeying Allah's command and avoiding His prohibitions, sincerely and in the prescribed manner. ﴿While being a believer﴾ [al-Isra': 19] means one who affirms the oneness of Allah, exalted is He, not associating anything with Him and not disbelieving in Him. Then Allah appreciates his striving, by granting him a great reward for his small deed.

In the verse is the evidence that good deeds benefit only together with faith in Allah.

This is because disbelief is an evil that no good deed benefits alongside, since He made a condition in this His saying: ﴿while being a believer﴾ [al-Isra': 19].

Allah, exalted is He, has clarified this in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck on a date-seed﴾ [an-Nisa': 124], and His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer—We will surely give him a good life, and We will surely reward them with their best deeds﴾ [an-Nahl: 97], and His saying: ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, being provided therein without account﴾ [Ghafir: 40], and other verses.

The implication of these verses is that a non-believer who obeys Allah sincerely does not benefit from that, because the condition of acceptance, which is faith in Allah, exalted is He, is absent.

Allah, exalted is He, has clarified this implication in other verses, such as His saying concerning the deeds of non-believers: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23], and His saying: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes on which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾ [Ibrahim: 18], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert, which the thirsty man thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ [an-Nur: 39], and other verses.

Allah, exalted is He, has also made clear in other places that the deed of the disbeliever by which he seeks nearness to Allah is rewarded for him in this world, and he has no share of it in the Hereafter. Such as His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived﴾ ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein is nullified, and what they used to do is void﴾ [Hud: 15, 16], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase for him in his harvest, and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him from it, and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [ash-Shura: 20].

And there is established from the Prophet ﷺ something similar to what these verses bring, regarding the disbeliever benefiting from his deeds in this world, from the hadith of Anas. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb—and the wording is Zuhayr's—told us, both saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah does not wrong a believer in a good deed; he is given for it in this world and is recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for his good deeds that he did for Allah in this world, until, when he reaches the Hereafter, there is no good deed for which he is recompensed."

Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi told us, Mu'tamir told us, saying: I heard my father, Qatadah told us, from Anas ibn Malik: that he narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Indeed the disbeliever, when he does a good deed, is given a morsel of food for it from this world. As for the believer, Allah stores up his good deeds for him in the Hereafter, and gives him provision in this world as a consequence of his obedience."

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Razi told us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata informed us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of their hadith.

Know that this which we have mentioned, its evidences from the Book and the Sunnah, that the disbeliever benefits from his righteous deed in this world, such as kindness to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, honouring the guest and the neighbour, relieving the distressed, and the like, all of it is restricted by the will of Allah, exalted is He, as He stated this in His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the hasty life, We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ [al-Isra': 18], and the verse.

So this noble verse restricts what has come of verses and hadiths, and it is established in the principles of jurisprudence that the restricted (muqayyad) governs the unrestricted (mutlaq), especially when the ruling and the cause are unified, as here. And he pointed to this in "Maraqi as-Su'ud" with his saying:

"And the unrestricted is to be read in light of that when the ruling and the cause in both are one."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 22:

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿Do not set up another god alongside Allah, lest you sit reproached and forsaken.﴾

The apparent meaning is that the address in this noble verse is directed to the Prophet ﷺ, so that through his tongue he would legislate for his community the sincere monotheism (tawhid) in worship of Him, exalted and high. This is because it is known that the Prophet ﷺ does not set up another god alongside Allah, and that he would not sit reproached and forsaken.

Among the verses that clearly indicate that the address is directed to him ﷺ, while the intended meaning is legislation for his community and not the address to him ﷺ himself, is His saying: ﴿If one or both of them reach old age in your presence, do not say to them "uff" and do not rebuke them, but speak to them a generous word﴾ [al-Isra: 23]. This is because the meaning of His saying ﴿If one or both of them reach old age﴾ [al-Isra: 23] is: if your parents or one of them reach old age in your presence, ﴿then do not say to them "uff"﴾. It is known that his parents had died long before that, so there is no basis for conditioning their reaching old age, or one of them reaching it, after they had died a long time ago. Rather, the intended meaning is legislation for someone other than him ﷺ.

Among the methods of the Arabic language is addressing a person while the intended target of the address is someone else. Among the well-known examples of this is the saying of the rajaz poet, who was Sahl ibn Malik al-Fazari:

"It is you I mean, but listen, O neighbour!"

The cause of this proverb: he visited Harithah ibn Lam al-Ta'i and found him absent. His sister hosted him and honoured him, and she was beautiful, so her beauty pleased him. He then addressed another woman, other than her, so that she (the first) would hear:

"O sister of the best of the desert dwellers and the settled folk, how do you see a youth of Fazarah?
He has come to love a free woman, perfumed with scent. It is you I mean, but listen, O neighbour!"

The woman understood his intent and answered him with her words:

"I say, O youth of Fazarah, I do not seek a husband, nor debauchery,
nor separation from the people of this quarter. Return to your family with a reply (istihara)."

Regarding her words "bistihārah": its apparent origin is istif'al from the muhawarah (exchange of speech), meaning the return of speech between the two of them, i.e., "return to your family by the exchange that has taken place between me and you, which is your speech and my reply to it, and nothing from me will go beyond that!" The ha' in "al-istihārah" is a substitute for the dropped 'ayn through i'lal (morphological alteration), as is well known in the science of morphology (sarf).

Some scholars held that the address in His saying ﴿Do not set up another god alongside Allah﴾ and similar verses is directed at the mukallaf (the responsible adult person). Among the methods of the Arabic language is the singular form of address used with the intent of generalization, such as the saying of Tarafah ibn al-'Abd in his Mu'allaqa (the celebrated ode):

"Days will reveal to you what you did not know, and there will come to you with news one whom you have not provisioned."

Al-Farra', al-Kisa'i and al-Zamakhshari said: the meaning of His saying ﴿then you sit﴾ [al-Isra: 22] is: "you become." Al-Farra' cited from it the saying of the rajaz poet:

"Henna does not satisfy the girl, nor do the two necklaces, nor the robe,
without the riders meeting, and the penis drooling for it."

That is: it becomes drooling for it.

Al-Kisa'i reported: "He sat, not asked for any need but he fulfilled it," meaning "he became." This was reported by Abu Hayyan in al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit). Then he also said: sitting here is an expression for remaining, i.e., "you will remain among people reproached and forsaken," just as you say of one who asks about the state of a person: "he is sitting in the worst state," meaning he remains and abides, whether standing or sitting. The sitting may also be meant literally, because it is the nature of one who is reproached and forsaken to sit bewildered and reflecting, and the general state, which is sitting, is used to express it. It was also said: the meaning of ﴿then you sit﴾ [al-Isra: 22] is "then you are incapacitated." The Arabs say: "What has made you sit back from noble deeds?" This is the relevant point from the words of Abu Hayyan.

The reproached (madhmum) here is the one who is blamed by Allah and by the intelligent among people, since he associated with Allah what neither benefits nor harms, and has no power over anything.

The forsaken (makhdhul) is the one whom those he hoped for help do not support. From this is his saying:

"Indeed, a man is not dead merely by the ending of his life,
but he is dead when he is wronged and then forsaken."

[p-84] [p-85]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 23:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَقَضى رَبُّكَ ألّا تَعْبُدُوا إلّا إيّاهُ وبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾

، أمَرَ جَلَّ وعَلا في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ بِإخْلاصِ العِبادَةِ لَهُ وحْدَهُ، وقَرَنَ بِذَلِكَ الأمْرِ بِالإحْسانِ إلى الوالِدَيْنِ.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, commanded sincere worship of Him alone, and coupled with that command the good treatment of parents.

وَجَعْلُهُ بِرَّ الوالِدَيْنِ مَقْرُونًا بِعِبادَتِهِ وحْدَهُ جَلَّ وعَلا المَذْكُورُ هُنا ذَكَرَهُ في آياتٍ أُخَرَ؛

His making the dutifulness toward parents linked with worship of Him alone, majestic and exalted, which is mentioned here, He mentioned in other verses:

• كَقَوْلِهِ في سُورَةِ ”النِّساءِ“: ﴿واعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ولا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾ الآيَةَ [النساء: ٣٦]،

• such as His saying in Surat "an-Nisa'": ﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ [an-Nisa': 36], the verse;

• وقَوْلِهِ في البَقَرَةِ: ﴿وَإذْ أخَذْنا مِيثاقَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ لا تَعْبُدُونَ إلّا اللَّهَ وبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾ الآيَةَ [البقرة: ٨٣]،
