As for what Muqatil narrates from the book of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim in explanation of this verse, namely that Mecca will be ruined by Abyssinia, Medina will perish by hunger, Basra by drowning, Kufa by the Turks, and the mountains by thunderbolts and quakes, while the destruction of Khurasan takes various forms, then he mentioned city after city, it is not to be relied upon, because it has no basis of soundness. Likewise is what is narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih: that the Jazirah is safe from ruin until Armenia is ruined, Armenia is safe until Egypt is ruined, Egypt is safe until Kufa is ruined, and the Great Battle will not occur until Kufa is ruined; when the Great Battle occurs, Constantinople will be conquered at the hand of a man from the Banu Hashim, the ruin of al-Andalus will come from the Zanj, the ruin of Ifriqiyah from al-Andalus, the ruin of Egypt from the cessation of the Nile and the disagreement of the armies within it, the ruin of Iraq from hunger, the ruin of Kufa from an enemy who besieges them and prevents them from drinking from the Euphrates, the ruin of Basra from drowning, the ruin of al-Ubullah from an enemy who besieges them by land and sea, the ruin of al-Rayy from the Daylam, the ruin of Khurasan from Tibet, the ruin of Tibet from China, the ruin of India and Yemen from locusts and the ruler, the ruin of Mecca from Abyssinia, and the ruin of Medina from hunger. End of quotation.

All of this is not to be relied upon, because it belongs to the category of Israʼiliyyat (narratives from Jewish and Christian sources).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 60:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when We told you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people."﴾ [Al-Isra: 60]

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, makes clear that He informed His Prophet ﷺ that He has encompassed the people; that is, they are in His grip, and He does with them as He wills. So He empowers His Prophet over them and protects him from them.

Some scholars of knowledge have said: Among the verses that explained to some extent this encompassing is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The multitude will be defeated and will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45], and His saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome"﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 12], and His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67]. In this is the indication that this verse is Meccan, while some of the verses mentioned are Medinan. As for the verse of Al-Qamar, which is His saying: ﴿The multitude will be defeated﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45], which comes later, there is no difficulty in using it for clarification, because it is Meccan.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [the] cursed tree [mentioned] in the Qur'an.﴾

The verified meaning of this noble verse is that Allah, majestic and exalted, made what He showed His Prophet ﷺ of the wonders and marvels on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj a trial for the people, because the minds of some of them were too narrow to accept it, believing that it could not possibly be true. They said: How can he pray at Bayt al-Maqdis, pass through the seven heavens, see what he saw in a single night, and be back in his place in Makkah in the morning? This is impossible. So this matter became a trial for them, because they did not believe it and held that it was impossible. And He, majestic and exalted, made the cursed tree in the Qur'an, which is the tree of Zaqqum, a trial for the people, because when they heard him ﷺ recite: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾ [As-Saffat: 64], they said: His lie has become evident, for trees do not grow in dry land, so how could it grow at the root of the fire? Thus this became a trial. He made clear that this is what is meant by the tree mentioned being a trial for them, in His saying: ﴿Is that better as a dinner or the tree of Zaqqum? Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾ [As-Saffat: 62–64]; this is clear, as you see. In another place He also pointed to the vision which He made a trial for them, in His saying: ﴿Then will you dispute with him over what he sees? And he certainly saw him in another descent, at the Lote-tree of the utmost boundary, near it is the Garden of Refuge, when there covered the Lote-tree that which covered. The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾ [An-Najm: 12–18]. We have already presented the clarification of this at the beginning of this noble surah. By this verification which we have mentioned, you know (p-166) that the saying of one who says that the vision which Allah showed him was his dream in sleep of the Banu Umayyah upon his pulpit, and that what is meant by the cursed tree in the Qur'an is the Banu Umayyah, is not to be relied upon; for it has no basis of soundness, and the hadith narrated for that is weak and cannot serve as proof. Rather, the tree was described as cursed because it is at the root of the fire, and the root of the fire is far from the mercy of Allah; and cursing (al-la'n) means distance from the mercy of Allah. Or it is described so because of the wickedness of its attributes described in the Qur'an, or because of the cursing of those who eat from it. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 61:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾.

His statement, exalted is He, in this verse about Iblis: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isra': 61]. The interrogative particle of denial (hamzat al-inkar) in his statement indicates his refusal (iba') and arrogance (istikbar) towards prostrating to a creature made of clay. He explicitly stated this refusal and arrogance in other places. He stated both together in al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿Except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and he was among the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 34]. He stated his refusal in al-Hijr with His saying: ﴿Except Iblis. He refused to be among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 31], and his arrogance in Sad with His saying: ﴿Except Iblis. He was arrogant and he was among the disbelievers﴾ [Sad: 74]. He explained the cause of his arrogance with his saying: "I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay" [al-A'raf: 12; al-Isra': 61 (cf. Sad: 76)], as has already been clarified in al-Baqarah.

His statement, ﴿tinan﴾ (clay), is a circumstantial accusative (hal); i.e., "for one whom You created while he was clay." The permission given by al-Zamakhshari that it be a circumstantial accusative of the relative pronoun itself (nafs al-mawsul) is not apparent to me. It has also been said that it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition (nazi' al-khafid); i.e., "from clay." It has also been said that it is a specifying accusative (tamyiz), and this is the weakest of these views. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 17, Verse 62:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Do You see this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control of his descendants, except for a few."﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted mentions that the accursed Iblis said to Him: ﴿Do You see¹ this one﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62], meaning: tell me about this one whom You have honored above me, when You commanded me to prostrate to him, namely Adam; that is, why did You honor him over me when I am better than him. The *kaf* in ﴿ara'aytaka﴾ is a *harf khitab* (particle of address), and "*hadha*" (this) is the *maf'ul bihi* (direct object) of *ara'ayta* (did you see).

The meaning is: "Tell me." It has also been said that the *kaf* is the direct object and "*hadha*" is the *mubtada'* (subject of a nominal sentence), but this is a weak opinion.

As for His saying, ﴿la-ahtanikanna dhurriyyatahu﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62], Ibn 'Abbas said: "I will surely take control over them," and al-Farra' said the same. Mujahid said: "I will surely encompass them." Ibn Zayd said: "I will surely misguide them." Al-Qurtubi said: "The meanings are close." That is, I will surely uproot them through seduction and misguidance, and I will surely destroy them.

The one who narrows this (its meaning), may Allah pardon him, says: What appears to me regarding the meaning of the verse is that what is intended by His saying ﴿la-ahtanikanna dhurriyyatahu﴾ is: I will surely lead them wherever I wish. This derives from the saying of the Arabs: *ihtanaktu al-faras*, when you place the bridle (*rasan*) on its *hanak* (palate/jaw) in order to lead it wherever you wish. The Arabs say: *hanaktu al-faras ahnuku-hu* (from the pattern of *daraba* and *nasara*) and *ihtanaktu-hu*, when you put the bridle on it, because the bridle is on its *hanak*. And the saying of the Arabs, *ihtanaka al-jaradu al-ard*, meaning the locusts ate what was on it, falls under this category, because they eat with their mouths, and the *hanak* is around the mouth. This is the original usage in its apparent sense. The derivation of the root is from the *hanak*, although it is also used generally for destruction and uprooting, as in the words of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

*"I complain to You of a year that has crushed us, adding hardship upon hardship and weakening us,*
*and it has seized our wealth and devoured it."*

What the Exalted mentions here about Iblis in His saying ﴿la-ahtanikanna dhurriyyatahu﴾ etc. [al-Isra' 17:62], He has also explained in other places in His Book, such as His saying ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾ ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left; and You will not find most of them grateful﴾ [al-A'raf 7:16–17], and His saying ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ [Sad 38:82], and other verses, as has already been clarified in Surat al-Nisa' and elsewhere.

His saying in this verse, ﴿except for a few﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62], has its intended meaning explained in other places, such as His saying ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [Sad 38:82–83], and His saying ﴿I will surely make the earth seem fair to them and will surely mislead them all﴾ ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39–40], as has already been clarified.

Iblis's saying in this verse, ﴿la-ahtanikanna dhurriyyatahu﴾ etc. [al-Isra' 17:62], he said out of assumption that it would happen, and this assumption was indeed realized for him, as the Exalted said: ﴿And Iblis did indeed prove right his assumption about them, and they followed him, except for a group of the believers﴾ [Saba' 34:20].

---

¹ *Ara'ayta* here means "tell me."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them – indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense."﴾

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: ﴿"Go"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:63]: this is a command of humiliation; that is, exert your utmost effort, for We have granted you respite. ﴿Whoever follows you﴾, that is, obeys you, from the offspring of Adam, ﴿indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾ [al-Isra' 17:63], that is, abundant. This is related from Mujahid and others. Al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan said: "Go" is not from going (dhahab), which is the opposite of coming; rather its meaning is: proceed to your affair which you have chosen. He followed it with mention of what the evil of his choice brought upon him, in His saying: ﴿whoever follows you among them – indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾ [al-Isra' 17:63].

(p-168) This threat with which Iblis and whoever follows him are threatened in this noble verse, He has also explained in other places, such as His saying: ﴿He said, "Then the truth, and the truth I say: I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you all together."﴾ [Sad 38:84–85], and His saying: ﴿So they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators, and the soldiers of Iblis, all together﴾, and other verses, as its clarification has preceded.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: "jaza'an" (recompense) is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq) in the accusative by the verbal noun before it, in accordance with the words of Ibn Malik in al-Khulasa:

"It is put in the accusative like its like, or a verb, or a descriptor, and its being the origin of these two is chosen."

What appears to me is that the saying of whoever said that "mawfuran" means "wafir" (abundant) has no basis. Rather, "mawfuran" is a passive participle (ism maf'ul) in its proper form, from the expression of them: "wafara al-shay'a yafiruhu" (he made the thing abundant/complete). So the doer is "wafir," and the one acted upon is "mawfur." From it is the verse of Zuhayr:

"And whoever makes kindness at the expense of his honour, it will be made complete for him; and whoever does not guard against abuse will be abused."

Accordingly, the meaning is: a recompense that is complete and perfected. This root is also used intransitively: one says "wafara malahu, fahuwa wafir," i.e., his wealth became abundant. And His saying "mawfuran" is an adjective (na't) of the verbal noun before it, as is clear. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and launch against them your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them. But Satan does not promise them except delusion.﴾

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his explanation of this noble verse: This is a matter of divine decree, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with strong incitement?﴾ [Maryam: 83]; that is, they agitate them toward sins with agitation, and drive them toward it with driving. End of quote.

The one who restricts it, may Allah pardon him, says: What appears to me is that the imperative forms in His saying ﴿And incite﴾ [al-Isra: 64], and His saying ﴿and launch﴾, and His saying ﴿and share﴾, are only for threat, meaning: do that, and you will see its disastrous consequence. This is like His saying: ﴿Do what you will﴾ [Fussilat: 40]. Abu Hayyan in al-Bahr also affirmed this, and it is clear, as you see. As for His saying ﴿And incite﴾, meaning: provoke whomever you are able to provoke from among them, the object is omitted because the context indicates it. Al-istifzaz (provocation, inciting) is al-istikhaff (causing to be light-headed, stirring up). A man who is fazz means light, agile, and from this the calf is called fazz, because of the lightness of its movement. From this is the saying of Zuhayr:

*As the fazz of a wild cow (ghaytala) seeks refuge in a sayʾ, fearing the eyes, and does not look at it with the ḥashak.*

The word "sayʾ" in Zuhayr's line, with an unpointed sin, a fatha, then a sukun ya', and ending in a hamza, is the milk that forms at the tips of the udders before the flow of milk descends. "Ḥashak" originally has sukun, because it is the verbal noun of ḥashakat al-durra (the milk-flow filled), and Zuhayr vowelled it only for the meter. "Ghaytala" here means the wild cow that has milk.

His saying ﴿with your voice﴾ [al-Isra: 64]: Mujahid said: it is idle amusement, singing, and musical instruments; that is, provoke whomever you can provoke among them with idle amusement, singing, and musical instruments. Ibn Abbas said: "his voice" includes every caller who calls to disobedience, because that occurred in obedience to him. It was also said: "with your voice" means your whispering (waswasa).

His saying ﴿and launch﴾: the origin of al-ijlab is driving with a clamour from the driver. Al-jalaba is the shouts. The Arabs say: ajlaba ʿala faraslihi, and jalaba ʿalayhi, when he shouts at him from behind and urges him to race. The word "khayl" (cavalry) is applied to the mares themselves and to the riders mounted upon them, and this is what is meant in the verse. "Rajl" is the plural of rajil (on foot). As we have previously stated, the verified view is that the plural of the active participle described with the pattern "fa'l" (fatha then sukun) is attested, and we have clarified its examples extensively, and we have chosen that it is an existing plural that the morphologists overlooked, since the pattern fa'l (with fatha then sukun) is not among the plural patterns for them. They therefore say of what has come of that, such as rajil and rajl, sahib and sahb, rakib and rakb, sharib and sharb, that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), not a plural, which contradicts the verified view.

Hafs from ʿAsim recited ﴿wa-rajilika﴾ [al-Isra: 64] with a kasra on the jim, a dialectal form for al-rajl, the plural of rajil.

Al-Zamakhshari said: this recitation is on the basis that "faʿil" has the meaning of "fa'il," like taʿib and taʾib, and its meaning is: "and your gathered infantry (al-rajil)." End of quote; that is, those walking on their feet.

﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾ [al-Isra: 64]. As for his sharing with them in wealth, it takes several forms: (among them) what they forbade for themselves from their wealth in obedience to him, such as the baha'ir and sawa'ib and the like; and what he commands them of spending wealth in disobedience to Allah, the Exalted; and what he commands them of acquiring wealth through means forbidden by the Law, such as usury, usurpation, and kinds of embezzlement, because they only did that in obedience to him.

As for his sharing with them in children, it also takes several forms:

Among them is their killing some of their children in obedience to him.

Among them is that they make their children Magians, Jews, and Christians, in obedience to him and in allegiance to him.

Among them is their naming their children ʿAbd al-Harith, ʿAbd Shams, ʿAbd al-ʿUzza, and the like, because by that they name their children as slaves to other than Allah, in obedience to him. Among this is the children of fornication, because they only caused their existence by committing indecency, in obedience to him, and so on.

Once you know this, know that Allah has clarified in verses of His Book some of what this verse contains of Satan's sharing with them in wealth and children, such as His saying: ﴿Those who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge, and forbade what Allah had provided them, fabricating against Allah, have certainly lost; they have gone astray and were not guided﴾ [al-An'am: 140]. Their killing of their children mentioned in this verse, in obedience to Satan, is his sharing with them in their children, since they killed them in his obedience. Likewise, the forbidding of some of what Allah provided them, mentioned in the verse, in obedience to him, is his sharing with them in their wealth as well. Also His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, and they say: "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "this is for our partners"﴾ [al-An'am: 136], and His saying: ﴿And they say: "These are livestock and crops that are forbidden; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim; and livestock whose backs are forbidden; and livestock over which they do not mention the name of Allah, fabricating against Him. He will recompense them for what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-An'am: 138], and His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful?" Say: "Did Allah permit you, or do you fabricate against Allah?"﴾ [Yunus: 59], and others among the verses.

Among the hadiths that clarify some of his sharing with them in what was mentioned is what is established in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Iyad ibn Himar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I created My servants as ḥunafa', and the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and forbade them what I had made lawful for them.'" And what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "If one of you, when he wishes to approach his wife, says, 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide us,' then if a child is decreed between them from that, Satan will not harm it." End of quote.

So the devils' leading them astray from their religion, and their forbidding them what Allah made lawful for them (in the first hadith), and its harm to them if they leave out the naming (in the second hadith), are all kinds of their sharing with them. His saying: "fajtalathum" originally derives from ifta'ala from al-jawalan (roaming); that is, the devils lightened them and they roamed with them in misguidance. It is said: jala and ijtala, when one goes and comes; from it comes al-jawalan in war; and ijtala al-shay' means he took it away and drove it. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

The imperative in His saying "wa-ʿidhum" (and make promises to them) is like the imperative in His saying ﴿wa-staftiz﴾ and His saying ﴿wa-ajlib﴾, and we have previously stated that it is for threat.

His saying: ﴿But Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾ [al-Isra: 64] clarifies that all the promises of Satan are delusion and falsehood, such as his promise to them that the idols will intercede for them and bring them near to Allah in closeness, and that since Allah gave them wealth and children in this world, He will give them the like in the Hereafter, and other false promises.

Allah, exalted is He, has clarified this meaning in other places:

- such as His saying: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires; but Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾ [al-Nisa: 120],
- and His saying: ﴿But you led yourselves into temptation, and you waited and doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah﴾ [al-Hadid: 14],
- and His saying: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter is decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I betrayed you"﴾ [Ibrahim: 22],

and others among the verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 65:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them﴾ [al-Isra' 17:65] – the verse. In this noble verse, may He be exalted and glorified, He makes clear that His righteous servants have no authority over them from Satan. The apparent meaning is that the noble verse contains an ellipsis of the attribute (ḥadhf al-ṣifah), as we have estimated, and what indicates the omitted attribute is His attributing the servants to Himself in an attribute of honour (iḍafat tashrīf). Other verses also indicate this estimated attribute, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [al-Hijr 15:40],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [al-Nahl 16:99–100],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the deviators﴾ [al-Hijr 15:42],

along with other verses besides these, as has previously been clarified.

[p. 172] The Exalted, in these noble verses, explains that when the disbelievers are touched by harm at sea, that is, when the wind becomes violent, the waves of the sea surround them like mountains, and they think there is no escape for them from it, then everything they used to worship besides God, the Exalted, vanishes from their minds and thoughts at that time. So they call upon none but God, the Exalted, alone, knowing that none but Him, the Exalted, alone, rescues from that distress and from other calamities. [p. 172] They therefore devote worship and supplication to Him alone at that moment when the terror of the sea has encompassed them. When God rescues them, relieves them, and they reach the shore, they return to the disbelief they were in, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when He has delivered you to the land, you turn away. And man has ever been ungrateful.﴾ [al-Isra: 67].

This meaning mentioned in this noble verse, God, the Exalted, made clear in many verses:

- As in His saying: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a stormy wind and the waves come to them from everywhere, and they assume that they are surrounded. They supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion: "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." But when He saves them, they commit tyranny in the earth without right﴾ [Yunus: 22–23].

- And His saying: ﴿Say, "Who delivers you from the darkness of land and sea, when you call upon Him in humility and privately: 'If He should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'" Say, "God delivers you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him"﴾ [al-An'am: 63–64].

- And His saying: ﴿And when they board ships, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, they immediately associate others [with Him]﴾ [al-Ankabut: 65].

- And His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, some of them are moderate. And none rejects Our signs except every treacherous ingrate﴾ [Luqman: 32].

- And His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Him, he forgets what he had called upon Him for before and sets up rivals to God to mislead [others] from His way﴾ [al-Zumar: 8].

Other verses besides these exist, as we have already explained "in Surat al-An'am" and elsewhere.

Then God, the Exalted, in this place which we are addressing, explained the foolishness of the minds of the disbelievers: that when they reach the land and escape the terror of the sea, they return to their disbelief, feeling secure from the punishment of God, although He is able to destroy them after their arrival at the land, by causing the side of the land near the sea to sink so that the earth swallows them, or by sending down upon them stones from the sky so that He destroys them, or by returning them once more to the sea so that its churning waves drown them. As He said here, rebuking them for their security and their disbelief after reaching land: ﴿Then are you secure from His causing the side of the land to sink with you, or sending against you a storm of stones?﴾ [al-Isra: 68]. The ḥāṣib is the rain or the wind in which there are stones. ﴿Or are you secure from His returning you to it another time and sending against you a violent wind and drowning you for what you disbelieved?﴾ [al-Isra: 69]; that is, because of your disbelief. The bāʾ here is causal (bāʾ sababiyyah), and "mā" is verbal-masdarial (mā maṣdariyyah). The qāṣif is the violent sea wind that breaks ships and other things. From it is the saying of Abu Tammam:

*Indeed, when the winds blow fiercely, they snap the branches of Najd, and they do not heed the retam [broom plant].*

He means: when they blow with force, they break the branches of the trees of Najd, whether they are retam or others.

[p. 173] This meaning which God, the Exalted, has explained here, of His power to destroy them outside the sea by sinking or by punishment from the sky, He has made clear in other places:

- As in His saying: ﴿If We will, We will cause the earth to swallow them, or cause to fall upon them fragments from the sky﴾ [Saba: 9], the verse [in full].

- And His saying: ﴿Say, "He is the Able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet"﴾ [al-An'am: 65], the verse [in full].

- And His saying: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven that He will cause the earth to swallow you, so that it shakes? Or are you secure from He who is in the heaven that He will send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning was﴾ [al-Mulk: 16–17].

- And His saying, concerning the people of Lot: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot. We saved them before dawn﴾ [al-Qamar: 34].

- And His saying: ﴿To send upon them stones of clay﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 33].

Besides other verses.

As for the ḥāṣib in this verse, we have already mentioned that it has been said to be the cloud or the wind, and both opinions are correct, because every violent wind that pelts with pebbles is called ḥāṣib and ḥaṣbah, and every cloud that pelts with hail is also called ḥāṣib. From this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:

*Facing the north of Syria, it strikes us with a hail like scattered cotton fluff.*

And the saying of Labid:

*Over them dragged, after their people had departed, the skirts of every gusting, pebble-laden wind.*

As for His saying in this verse: ﴿Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger﴾ [al-Isra: 69], "tabīʿan" is in the pattern faʿīl meaning fāʿil. That is, a follower who pursues us by demanding vengeance for you, like His saying: ﴿So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and leveled them, and He does not fear its consequence﴾ [al-Shams: 14–15], meaning He does not fear the consequence of any pursuit that would reach Him because of that. Every claimant of a debt, or of vengeance, or of anything else, the Arabs call a tabīʿ. From this is the saying of al-Shammakh describing an eagle:

*The foxes of the two heights seek refuge from it, as a debtor seeks refuge from the creditor who pursues him.*

That is: like the refuge of the debtor from the creditor who demands repayment from him.

From this is the saying of another:

*They departed, and their gazelles departed, as if they were guarantors of a debt, whose creditor pursues them.*

That is, their adversary is one who demands a debt.

Of this kind is His saying: ﴿So follow up with reasonableness and pay him with good conduct﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178], and His saying ﷺ: "When one of you is referred to a wealthy person for payment, let him follow up." And this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Abbas and others: "tabīʿan" means a helper, and the saying of Mujahid: a helper who seeks vengeance.

* *

[p. 174] Warning

It is not hidden from one who reflects upon this noble verse that God rebuked the disbelievers and reproached them for devoting worship to Him alone especially in times of hardship and terror, and not directing any part of His right to a created being, while in times of security and well-being they associate others with Him in the rights that are due to Him alone, which is worshipping Him alone in all kinds of worship. From this it is known that some ignorant people who name themselves with the name of Islam are worse off than idol-worshippers, for when hardships overwhelm them and terror and distresses surround them, they turn to other than God, from those whom they believe to be righteous, at the very time when the disbelievers are sincere in worship to God. Yet God, the Exalted, has made clear in more than one place that answering the distressed one and delivering him from calamity are among His rights, in which none shares with Him.

Among the clearest proofs of this is His saying in Surat al-Naml: ﴿Is Allah best, or what they associate [with Him]? Is He not [best] who created the heavens and earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight, which you could not have grown their trees? Is there a deity with Allah? Rather, they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him]. Is He not [best] who made the earth a stable place and placed within it rivers and placed within it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with Allah? Rather, most of them do not know. Is He not [best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil?﴾ [al-Naml: 59–62; the source cites al-Saffat in error for the reference, but the verses are of al-Naml]. You see, the Exalted, in these noble verses, made answering the distressed one when he calls and removing evil from him one of His exclusive rights in which no one shares, like His creation of the heavens and the earth, His sending down water from the sky, His causing trees to grow by it, His making the earth a stable place, His placing rivers within it, His placing firm mountains in it, His placing a barrier between the two seas, and the rest of what He mentioned in these verses of His wondrous creation and marvels in which none shares with Him; glorified and exalted is He above that, to a great height.

What God, the Exalted, mentioned in these noble verses was the cause of the conversion to Islam of Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl. When the Messenger of God ﷺ conquered Mecca, he fled from it toward the land of Abyssinia, and he boarded a ship at sea heading for Abyssinia. A violent wind came upon them, and the people said to one another: "Nothing will avail you except that you call upon God alone." Ikrimah said to himself: "By God, if nothing else benefits at sea, then nothing else benefits on land. O God, I make a covenant with You: if You bring me out of this, I will go and place my hand in the hand of Muhammad ﷺ, and I will surely find him kind and merciful." They came out of the sea, and he went to the Messenger of God ﷺ, embraced Islam, and his Islam was good. May God be pleased with him. End quote.

[p. 175] Apparently the pronoun in His saying: ﴿then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger [tabīʿan]﴾ refers to destruction by drowning, which is understood from His saying: ﴿and drown you for what you disbelieved﴾ [al-Isra: 69]. That is, you will not find a pursuer who seeks vengeance from Us for you because of that drowning.

The author of Ruh al-Ma'ani said: the pronoun in "bihi" has been said to refer to the sending, and it has been said to refer to the drowning, and it has been said to refer to both together, according to what occurred. And knowledge is with God, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 70:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾.

Some of the people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) said: Among the forms of His honouring the children of Adam is that He created them in the most complete and best of forms (al-hay'at), for man walks upright, standing on his two legs, and eats with his hands, whereas other animals walk on four limbs and eat with their mouths.

Among what the Qur'an gives as evidence for this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4], and His saying: ﴿And He fashioned you and perfected your forms﴾ [Ghafir: 64]. There is other discussion of the verse beyond this, and Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We carried them on the land and the sea﴾, to the end of the verse. That is, on land upon the beasts (al-an'am), and on the sea upon the ships (al-sufun).

The verses clarifying this are very numerous, such as His saying: ﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 22], and His saying: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 12]. We have already presented this in full detail with clarification in "Surat al-Nahl."

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 17, verse 71:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day when We shall summon every people with their leader﴾.

Some scholars said: The meaning of "with their leader" here is the book of their deeds.

This is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have enumerated everything in a clear record﴾ [Ya-Sin: 12]; His saying: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do"﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 28]; His saying: ﴿And the Record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], to the end of the verse; and His saying: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record that he will find spread open﴾ [al-Isra': 13]. Ibn Kathir chose this view because of the indication of the verse of Ya-Sin mentioned above. This view is a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, which Ibn Jarir and others have recorded, and Ibn Kathir attributed it to Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Dahhak and al-Hasan. And from Qatadah and Mujahid: the meaning of ﴿with their leader﴾ is their prophet.

(p-176) This view is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For every nation there is a messenger; so when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus: 47]; His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nisa': 41]; His saying: ﴿And on the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 89]; and His saying: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Record will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Zumar: 69].

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: In this there is the greatest honour for the people of hadith (Ahl al-Hadith), because their leader is the Prophet (ﷺ).

Some people of knowledge said: ﴿with their leader﴾; that is, with their book which was revealed to their prophet containing the legislation. Among those who held this view is Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

Some people of knowledge said: ﴿On the Day when We shall summon every people with their leader﴾ [al-Isra': 71] means: We will summon every people with the one whom they follow. So the people of faith have as their leaders the prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and the people of disbelief have as their leaders their chiefs and great ones among the leaders of the disbelievers; as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Qasas: 41]. This last view is, in my opinion, the most evident of the views, and Allah knows best.

You have seen the views of the scholars concerning this verse and what Qur'an bears witness to them. His saying after this: ﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾ [al-Isra': 71] is among the indicators supporting the preference of what Ibn Kathir chose, that the "leader" in this verse is the record of deeds.

In this noble verse, He, the Most High, mentioned that those who are given their record in their right hands will read it, and they will not be wronged even a thread (fatil).

This has been clarified in other places, such as His saying: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: "Here, read my record!"﴾ [al-Haqqah: 19] to His saying: ﴿And as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record!"﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25]. We have already presented this in full at the beginning of this noble surah.

As for the saying of one who said that the meaning of ﴿with their leader﴾ is, as with Muhammad ibn Ka'b, "their mothers", meaning it will be said: "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so (of such a woman)", this is undoubtedly a false view. It has been established in the Sahih from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "On the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person, and it will be said: 'This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'"

The meaning of blindness in this noble verse is blindness of the heart, not blindness of the eye. The proof for this is His saying, ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. Blindness of the eye alongside sight of the heart does no harm, but the reverse is not so, for the blind man can take heed, and the reminder benefits him through the insight of his heart. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ ﴿because the blind man came to him﴾ ﴿and what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself﴾ ﴿or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him﴾ [Abasa: 1–4].

؎When the heart sees manliness and piety clearly, the blindness of the two eyes does not harm.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said when he went blind at the end of his life, as has been narrated from him by several routes, as Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and others mentioned:

؎If Allah takes the light of my two eyes, there remains in my tongue and my heart a light from them.
My heart is sharp, and my intellect is free of defect,
and in my mouth is a cutting sword, well transmitted.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿but he who is blind in this world, he will be blind in the Hereafter, and further astray from the way﴾ [al-Isra: 72], some scholars said: the form here is not a comparative form (ṣīghat al-tafḍīl, the elative/comparative form). Rather, the meaning is: he will be blind in the Hereafter, in the same way, unable to find the way to any benefit. Al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) firmly held this view.

Its compiler, may Allah pardon him, says: What comes to mind first is that the second word ʿaʿmā ("blind") is a comparative form, meaning: he will be more blind in the Hereafter.

This is supported by His saying after it, ﴿and further astray from the way﴾, for it is undisputedly a comparative form. It is established in the science of Arabic grammar that the exclamative form (ṣīghat al-taʿajjub) and the comparative form (ṣīghat al-tafḍīl) are not derived from a verb whose descriptive form is on the pattern afʿal, whose feminine is faʿlāʾ, as indicated in al-Khulasa (Ibn Malik's grammatical poem) in his saying:

؎And from a non-descriptive verb resembling ashhal

It appears that whatever is found in the speech of the Arabs formed from the comparative or exclamative form without meeting its conditions should be memorised and not analogised upon, as indicated in al-Khulasa in his saying:

؎Judge by rarity for what is not mentioned, and do not analogise upon what is transmitted from it.

Among the examples of this is his saying:

؎Of the lofty qualities you have neither shade nor fruit,
and in the shameful deeds you have the shadows of old men.
As for the kings, today you are the basest of them in baseness,
and the most white-garmented of them in the garment of a cook.

Some scholars said: his saying in this verse, "wa-abyaḍuhum sirbāla ṭabbākh" (the most white-garmented of them in the garment of a cook), is not a comparative form. Rather, the meaning is: you alone are the one white in the garment of a cook among them.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We have revealed to you, to fabricate against Us other than it; and then they would have taken you as a close friend.﴾

It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that it was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh, who said to him (ﷺ): "We will not let you touch the Black Stone until you pay heed to our gods." And from Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ata', that it was revealed concerning the delegation of Thaqif, who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him for an excessive thing. They said: "Allow us to enjoy our gods for a year, so that we may take what is offered to them, and make our valley sacred as you have made Makkah sacred." And there are other opinions concerning the occasion of its revelation. In any case, the lesson is drawn from the generality of the wording, not from the specificity of the occasion.

The meaning of the noble verse is that the disbelievers almost tempted him, that is, they came close to doing so. The meaning of "tempting you" is that they would make you slip away from that which We have revealed to you, so that you would fabricate against Us something other than what We have not revealed to you.

Some scholars said: they came close to it in their own assumption, not in reality. It was also said: the meaning is that there passed through his heart (ﷺ) the notion of agreeing with them in some of what they desired, in order to draw them to Islam, due to the intensity of his eagerness for their conversion.

In another place He made clear that they asked him to bring something other than what had been revealed to him, and that he refused most strongly, and said to them that it was not possible for him to bring anything of his own accord, but rather he follows what his Lord reveals to him. This is in His saying: ﴿Say, those who do not hope for meeting Us: "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say: "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾ [Yunus: 15]. And His saying in this verse: ﴿And indeed they almost [kadu]﴾ [al-Isra: 73], the "in" here is the lightened (mukhaffafah) form of the heavy (thaqilah) "inna", and here it is inactive (muhmalah), and the lam is the distinguishing particle between it and the negating "in", as he said in the Khulasah (Ibn Malik's Alfiyya):

"It is lightened, so its action is little, and the lam must accompany it when it is left inactive."

It is generally the case that it is not like this with a verb, except if the verb is abrogating (nasikh), as in this verse. He said in the Khulasah:

"And if the verb is not abrogating, you will rarely find it connected to 'in' that joins it."

As is well known in grammar.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 74:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would nearly have inclined toward them a little.﴾ ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] of life and double [punishment] of death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us.﴾

In this noble verse, the Majestic and Exalted explains His making His Prophet firm (ﷺ), and His protecting him from inclining toward the disbelievers, and that had he inclined toward them, He would have made him taste double the punishment of life (ḍi'f al-ḥayāh) (p-179) and double the punishment of death (ḍi'f al-mamāt); that is, twice the punishment of life in this world and twice the punishment of death in the Hereafter. Al-Qurtubi affirmed this in his tafsir. Some of them said: what is meant by double the punishment of death is the doubled punishment in the grave. And what is meant by double the punishment of life is the doubled punishment in the Hereafter after the life of resurrection. Al-Zamakhshari and others affirmed this. The verse includes all of this.

What he mentions here regarding the severity of the recompense for His Prophet, should he oppose, He explains elsewhere, such as His saying: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings,﴾ ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand,﴾ ﴿Then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ (Al-Haqqah: 44–46), the verse etc.

And this which this verse indicates, that when the rank is higher, the recompense upon opposition is greater, He explains in another place, such as His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twice over﴾ (Al-Ahzab: 30), the verse etc. And well has said the one who said:

"The major sins of the small man are minor sins, and the minor sins of the great man are major sins."

Note (tanbīh)

This noble verse has made abundantly clear the innocence of our Prophet (ﷺ) from even approaching inclination toward the disbelievers, let alone inclination itself; because "lawlā" [Al-Isra: 74] is a particle of prohibition due to the existence of something. So the approach to inclination was prevented by "lawlā" of prohibition, due to the existence of Allah's making firm of the most noble of His creation (ﷺ). Thus it is certainly established that approaching inclination is negated, let alone inclination itself. This verse clarifies what precedes it, that he did not approach inclining toward them at all; because His saying: ﴿you would nearly have inclined toward them a little﴾ (Al-Isra: 74), meaning you almost inclined toward them, is the very thing prohibited by "lawlā" of prohibition, as you see. And the meaning of ﴿inclined toward them﴾ is: to lean toward them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ ... the verse. We have already explained, "in Surah An-Nisa'," that this noble verse is among the verses that point to the times of prayer. His saying ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾ [Al-Isra: 78] means at its actual decline (zawal), so it encompasses the times of Zuhr and 'Asr. The evidence for this is the limit in His saying ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾, i.e., its darkness, which includes the times of Maghrib and 'Isha'. His saying ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾ means the Subh prayer, as its explanation has preceded. We have pointed out the verses that indicate the times of the prayers, such as His saying ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night﴾ [Hud: 114], and His saying ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [Ar-Rum: 17]. We have established the explanation of that from the Sunnah (p-180) in the discussion of His saying ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾ [An-Nisa: 103], so refer to it there if you wish. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 81:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "The truth has come and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart."﴾ Al-haqq (the truth) in the language of the Arabs is that which is firm and does not cease or vanish, and al-batil (falsehood) is that which goes away and vanishes. The meaning of al-haqq in this verse is what is in this Great Qur'an and the Prophetic Sunnah of the religion of Islam, and the meaning of al-batil in it is shirk (associating partners with) Allah and the sins that oppose the religion of Islam.

In this noble verse, the Majestic and Exalted has made clear that Islam came firm and established, and that shirk with Allah zahaqa, that is, went away, vanished and ceased. The Arabs say: "zahaqat nafsuhu" (his soul departed) when it has left his body and ceased to be in it.

Then the Majestic and Exalted made clear that falsehood was zahuqan, that is, vanishing and not firm at any time. This meaning has been made clear in other places, and He mentioned that the truth removes falsehood and eliminates it, as in His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord hurls the truth; He is Knower of the unseen."﴾ and ﴿Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate anything nor restore it."﴾ [Saba': 48, 49], and His saying: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and at once it departs.﴾

The author of ad-Durr al-Manthur, speaking on this noble verse, said: Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, Muslim, at-Tirmidhi, an-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began striking them with a stick in his hand and saying: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾ [al-Isra': 81], ﴿The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate anything nor restore it.﴾ [Saba': 49]."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ya'la and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We entered Makkah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded concerning them, and they were overturned on their faces, and he said: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾ [al-Isra': 81]."

At-Tabarani in as-Saghir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in ad-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest, and on the Ka'bah were three hundred and sixty idols. Iblis fastened their feet with lead for them; then he came with a staff and began to lunge at each idol of them, and it would fall on its face, and he would say: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾ [al-Isra': 81], until he had passed over all of them."

Al-Qurtubi said in his commentary on this verse: In this verse is evidence for breaking the idols (nusub) of the polytheists and all idols when they are overcome, and by implication the breaking of every instrument of falsehood and whatever serves only for disobedience to Allah, such as drums, lutes and flutes, which have no purpose except diversion with them from the remembrance of Allah.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: Included in the meaning of idols are images made of clay, wood and the like, and everything that people make which has no benefit except the forbidden diversion. It is not permissible to sell any of it, except idols that are made of gold, silver, iron or lead, when they are altered from their form and become ingots or pieces; then it is permissible to sell them and to buy with them. Al-Muhallab said: Whatever is broken of the instruments of falsehood, and whose keeping after breaking has a benefit, its owner has more right to it broken, unless the ruler sees fit to burn it with fire as a means of stringency and punishment concerning property. The burning by Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, has preceded. The Prophet (ﷺ) also intended to burn the houses of those who stayed away from congregational prayer, and this is a basis for punishment concerning property, together with his (ﷺ) saying concerning the she-camel that was cursed by its owner: "Leave her, for she is accursed," so he removed her ownership from her as discipline for her owner and as punishment for her, for what she was cursed with. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, also poured out milk that had been mixed with water, belonging to its owner. End. The purpose of al-Qurtubi's words, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him.

And his (ﷺ) saying: "By Allah, Jesus son of Mary will surely descend as a just judge, and he will surely break the cross and surely kill the swine," the hadith, is among the things we have mentioned as evidence of this verse. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 82:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾

We have already presented, at the beginning of "Surat al-Baqarah," the verses that clarify this meaning which this noble verse indicates, such as His saying: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has increased them in evil to their evil, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 124-125], and His saying: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is for them a blindness"﴾ [Fussilat: 44], as its explanation has preceded. His saying in this verse, ﴿that which is a healing﴾ [al-Isra': 82], includes that it is a healing for the heart from its diseases, such as doubt and hypocrisy and other than that, and that it is a healing for bodies when recited over them with it, as the story of the one who performed ruqyah (incantation) on the man stung by a scorpion with al-Fatihah indicates, and it is authentic and well known. Abu 'Amr recited ﴿nunzilu﴾ with a sukun on the nun and a light zay, while the rest recited it with a fatha on the nun and a shadda on the zay. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

(p-182) His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself (lit. turns aside with his side), and when evil touches him, he is ever despairing﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that when He bestows upon man health, well-being and provision, he turns away from the remembrance of Allah and His obedience, and "distances himself" (nata bi-janibihi), i.e., he moves far from obedience to his Lord, so he does not carry out His command nor refrain from His prohibition.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "He turns away from the remembrance of Allah as if he were independent of Him, self-sufficient," ﴿and distances himself﴾ [al-Isra': 83] is an emphasis on the turning away, because turning away from something means turning the side of one's face (ʿurḍ wajhihi) away from it. And "distancing with the side" (al-naʾy bi-l-janib) is to bend one's flank away from it and turn one's back to it, and he intends arrogance, because that is the habit of the arrogant. And "yaʾus" (ya'ūs): one who is intensely despairing, i.e., one who is hopeless of Allah's mercy.

Allah, exalted is He, has clarified this meaning in many places in His Book, such as His saying in Surat Hud:
﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us, then withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing, ungrateful﴾
﴿And if We let him taste favour after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: "The evils have gone from me," indeed he is exultant, boastful﴾ [Hud: 9–10]

And His saying in another surah, Fussilat:
﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing, desperate﴾
﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will be established; and if I am returned to my Lord, I will have the best with Him." So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾
﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he has abundant supplication﴾ [Fussilat: 49–51],

And His saying in Surat al-Rum:
﴿And when harm touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord﴾ [al-Rum: 33],

And His saying in the same surah:
﴿And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but if an evil befalls them for what their hands have sent forth, behold, they despair﴾ [al-Rum: 36],

And His saying in Surat Yunus:
﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us concerning a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12], the verse...

And His saying in Surat al-Zumar:
﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He bestows upon him a favour from Him, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before, and sets up rivals to Allah, to lead astray from His way﴾ [al-Zumar: 8], the verse... (cited in the text as Yunus: 12)

And His saying in the same surah:
﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favour from Us, he says, "I was given it only because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 49],

and other verses besides these.

Allah has excepted from these characteristics His believing servants in His saying in Surat Hud:
﴿Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Hud: 11], as its clarification has already passed (p-183). Ibn Dhakwan recited "wa-na'a" like "jaa," and it has the same meaning as "nata" (naʾa), as in their saying: "raa" for "ra'a" (to see).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little﴾.

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He has not given His creation of knowledge except a little, in relation to His own knowledge, majestic and exalted; because what the creation has been given of knowledge, in relation to the knowledge of the Creator, is very little indeed.

Among the verses that indicate this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾ [al-Kahf: 109]. And His saying: ﴿And if whatever trees on the earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [Luqman: 27].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 87:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, His bounty upon you has been great.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, makes clear that His bounty upon His Prophet ﷺ is great.

He elaborated on this meaning in other places:

• such as His saying: ﴿And He taught you what you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you has been ever great.﴾ [An-Nisa: 113],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path. And that Allah may aid you with a mighty victory.﴾ [Al-Fath: 1-3],

• and His saying: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed upon your back? And raised for you your repute.﴾ [Ash-Sharh: 1-4],

and other verses besides these.

Exalted is He, in another place, He made clear that His bounty is great upon all the believers, and that is His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 47]. He also made clear the meaning of "the great bounty" in His saying: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, in the gardens of paradise, they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 22].

This verse, "And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, 'Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?'" (al-Isra 17:94), is about a customary (ʿādī) obstacle.

The reason it is customary is that it has been the habit of all nations to find it strange that Allah sends messengers from among humans. Examples include:

• His saying: ﴿They said, "You are only human beings like us"﴾ (Ibrahim 14:10), and the rest of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿Shall we believe in two humans like us?﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:47).

• His saying: ﴿"Shall we follow a single human from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness"﴾ (al-Qamar 54:24).

• His saying: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, "Shall humans guide us?"﴾ (al-Taghabun 64:6), and the rest of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿And if you obey a human like yourselves, you would then be losers﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:34),

in addition to other verses.

The evidence that the obstacle in this verse is customary is that He, exalted is He, explicitly stated a different obstacle, not this one, "in Surat al-Kahf": ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that there come to them the way of the former peoples or the punishment come upon them in full view﴾ (al-Kahf 18:55). The obstacle mentioned "in al-Kahf" is a real (ḥaqīqī) obstacle, because whoever Allah intends for the way of the former peoples of destruction, or for the punishment to come upon him in full view, his being intended by Allah for that is an obstacle that prevents the contrary of what is willed. This is because it is impossible for the opposite of His will, exalted is He, to occur. This differs from the obstacle "in this verse about the Children of Israel," which is a customary obstacle whose non-occurrence is possible, and we have clarified this matter in our book "Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book).

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾.

The apparent contradiction of this verse with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that there come to them the way of the former peoples﴾ (al-Kahf 18:55). The way to reconcile them is that the restriction (ḥaṣr) in the verse of "al-Isra" is a restriction to the customary obstacle.

The restriction in the verse of "al-Kahf" is to the real obstacle. Its clarification is what Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam mentioned, that the meaning of the verse of "al-Kahf": ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing﴾ except that Allah willed that there come upon them the way of the former peoples of destruction in this world, or that the punishment come upon them in full view in the Hereafter. Thus He informed that He willed that one of the two matters befall them. There is no doubt that the will of Allah prevents the occurrence of what contradicts His will. So this is a restriction to the real obstacle, because Allah is the real obstacle.

As for the meaning of the verse: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ (al-Isra 17:1), it is that nothing prevented the people from faith except their astonishment that Allah sends a messenger from among humans. Their astonishment at this is not a real obstacle but a customary one, whose non-occurrence is possible, so faith is found along with it. This differs from the first, which is real and whose non-occurrence is not possible, nor is faith found along with it. The author of al-Itqan mentioned this reconciliation, and Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 95:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Had there been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down upon them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾

In this verse, He, majestic and exalted, makes clear that the messenger must be of the same kind (jins) as those to whom he is sent. If He were to send a messenger to the angels, He would send down to them an angel like them. That is, when He sends to mankind, He sends to them a human like them.

This meaning is clarified in other passages:

• His saying: ﴿And they say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?" And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved.﴾ And ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they confuse [themselves].﴾ [al-An'am: 8–9],

• And His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 7],

• And His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers but that they ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]

as has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 97:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse indicates that the disbelievers will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection blind, mute, and deaf.

Other verses have come which indicate the opposite of this, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿See them and hear them the Day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38], and His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53], and His saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may work righteousness﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12]. The answer to this is from several aspects:

The first aspect: it is what Abu Hayyan inferred, that what is mentioned is meant literally, and that this occurs at the beginning of the matter; then Allah, exalted is He, returns to them their sight, their speech, and their hearing, so they see the Fire, hear its roaring, and speak as Allah, exalted is He, related of them in more than one place.

The second aspect: they will not see anything that pleases them, nor will they hear in that way, nor will they speak with a proof, just as in the worldly life they did not perceive insightfully, did not speak the truth, and did not hear it. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this from Ibn Abbas, and it was also related from al-Hasan, as mentioned by al-Alusi in his tafsir. Thus, what they say, hear, and see is treated as nonexistent because it brings no benefit, as a parallel of this has already been mentioned.

The third aspect: when Allah says to them: ﴿Be driven into it, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108], that blindness, deafness, and muteness befall them due to the intensity of distress and despair of relief. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the word will be fulfilled against them for what they did wrong, so they will not speak﴾ [al-Naml: 85]. According to this view, the three states are considered hypothetical (muqaddarah).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 100:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold them for fear of spending. And mankind is ever tight-fisted."﴾

In this verse Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that if the children of Adam possessed the treasuries of His mercy—that is, the treasuries of provisions and bounties—they would be stingy with their provision toward others, and they would withhold giving, out of fear of spending, because of the severity of their miserliness.

He also makes clear that man is qatur, that is, stingy and niggardly; from their saying: qattara ʿalā ʿiyālihi (he restricted provision for his dependents), meaning he constricted it for them.

He makes this meaning clear in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion? Then they would not give people even a speck (naqir)﴾ [an-Nisa': 53], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious; when evil touches him, impatient; and when good touches him, withholding﴾ ﴿except the observers of prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 19–22], along with other verses besides these.

It is established in the science of Arabic grammar (ʿilm al-ʿarabiyyah) that "law" (lau, "if") is only followed by verbs. Therefore a verb is presumed to be omitted in the verse after it, and the pronoun in the nominative following "law" is originally the subject of the omitted verb; when the verb was omitted, the pronoun was made separate. The original is: "Say: If you possess," so the verb was omitted, the waw remained, and it was made a separate pronoun: "antum" (you). This is what more than one scholar has said, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 102:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "You certainly know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs (basa'ir)."﴾

The verse [and so on]. In this noble verse, exalted is He, makes clear that Pharaoh knows that the signs mentioned were sent down by none other than the Lord of the heavens and the earth, as clear proofs (hujaj wadiha), and that this indicates that Pharaoh's saying ﴿"Who then is the Lord of you two, O Moses?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 49], and his saying ﴿"And what is the Lord of the worlds?"﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 23], are all from him the feigned ignorance of one who knows.

(p-188) Exalted is He has explained this meaning further, clarifying the cause of his denial of what he knew, "in Surat an-Naml," by His saying: ﴿"And insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease, among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people."﴾ ﴿But when Our signs came to them as clear evidence, they said, "This is obvious magic."﴾ ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance.﴾ [an-Naml: 12–14] and the verse [and so on].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 105:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾.

In this noble verse, may He be majestic and exalted, He makes clear that He sent down this Qur'an with the truth, i.e., clothed with it and containing it. Everything in it that is true, its reports are truthful and its rulings are just, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115]. And how could it not be so, when He, may He be majestic and exalted, sent it down with His knowledge, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾ [al-Nisa': 166], and the verse continues. His saying: ﴿And with the truth it descended﴾ [al-Isra': 105] indicates that no alteration or change occurred in it in the manner of its descent.

This is because the messenger entrusted with its descent is strong, not overcome so that it could be altered in it, and trustworthy, who does not change or alter, as He indicated by His saying: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has descended with it﴾ ﴿upon your heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193-194], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ ﴿possessing power, with the Owner of the Throne secure in standing﴾ ﴿obeyed and then trustworthy﴾ [al-Takwir: 19-21]. And His saying in this verse: ﴿the word of a messenger﴾ means his conveying it from his Lord, as indicated by the word "messenger," because it indicates that he was sent with it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 106:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And (it is) a Qur'an which We have divided [into parts], that you might recite it to the people over a long period (ʿalā mukth)﴾.

The majority of reciters read this word "faraqnāhu" with the light (takhfīf) form, meaning: We made it clear and manifest (bayyannāhu wa-awḍaḥnāhu), We explained it in detail (faṣṣalnāhu), and We distinguished by it between the truth and falsehood (wa-farraqnā bihi bayna al-ḥaqq wa-al-bāṭil). Some of the Companions read "farraqnāhu" with the emphatic (tashdīd) form, meaning: We sent it down in parts, according to events, over twenty-three years.

Among the uses of faraqa in the sense of bayyana (to make clear) and faṣṣala (to detail) is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In it every matter of wisdom is made distinct﴾ [al-Dukhān: 4], and the verse [continues].

He, may He be exalted, has explained that He made this Qur'an clear to His Prophet so that he might recite it to the people over a long period (ʿalā mukth), that is, with leisure, deliberation and steadiness. This indicates that the Qur'an should not be recited except in this manner. He, may He be exalted, has commanded what indicates this in His saying: ﴿And recite the Qur'an in measured recitation (tartīl)﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4]. Also indicating this is His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus (it is) that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have recited it in measured recitation﴾ [al-Furqān: 32].

As for His saying, "Qur'ānan" [al-Isrā': 106], it is in the accusative (manṣūb) by a verb omitted (maḥdhūf) which is explained by what follows it, according to the principle stated in his verse in the Khulāṣah (Alfiyyah):

(p-189) "The preceding noun, put it in the accusative by a verb that is hidden, certainly agreeing with what has been made apparent."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 110:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted and majestic is He, commands His servants that they call upon Him by whichever of His names they wish. If they wish, they say: "Yā Allāh (O Allah)," and if they wish, they say: "Yā Raḥmān (O Most Merciful)," and so on with His other names, exalted and majestic is He.

He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾ [al-A'raf: 180], and His saying: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him. He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner; to Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Him, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.﴾ [al-Hashr: 22, 23].

And Allah, exalted and majestic is He, has clarified in another place that they ignored the name al-Raḥmān in His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾ and the verse [al-Furqan: 60]. He also explained to them some of the actions of al-Raḥmān, exalted and majestic is He, in His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquent speech.﴾ [al-Rahman: 1–4]. For this reason some scholars said: His saying, ﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an,﴾ is an answer to their saying, ﴿And what is the Most Merciful?﴾ and the verse [al-Furqan: 60]. More explanation of this will come, if Allah wills, "in Surat al-Furqan."
